Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
A. Rajendra I's Ganga expedition
B. Vijayabahu I expelled the Cholas from Sri Lanka
C. Kulottunga I sent a 72-member merchant mission to China
D. Rajendra III, the last ruler, was gone
85.x: Rajendra I's Ganga expedition took place in 1022 CE; Kulottunga I's China mission occurred later, Vijayabahu I expelled the Cholas around 1070, and Rajendra III was gone by 1279.
85.tq: Fix the dated event of 1022 first, then place the later 1070 and 1279 milestones.
85.sec: Later Cholas - Sri Lanka relations and decline

85.s: The Chola hold over Sri Lanka developed in which of the following ways?
o: Kulottunga I first conquered the north, and Rajendra III retained the whole island
Vijayabahu I established Chola rule over the whole island for about five decades
Rajaraja I controlled the whole island, while Rajendra I restricted Chola control to the north
Rajaraja I controlled the north, while Rajendra I extended control to the whole island for about five decades
85.x: Rajaraja I established Chola control in northern Sri Lanka, and Rajendra I extended it to the whole island, which remained under Chola control for about five decades.
85.tq: Split the comparison into ruler, territorial extent and duration instead of relying on a single familiar name.
85.sec: Later Cholas - Sri Lanka relations and decline

85.s: Who expelled the Cholas from Sri Lanka around 1070?
85.x: Vijayabahu I expelled the Cholas from Sri Lanka around 1070.
85.tq: Use the ruler–event association rather than confusing the Sri Lankan ruler with a Chola ruler.
85.sec: Later Cholas - Sri Lanka relations and decline

85.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Kulottunga I's foreign commercial policy?
o: He transferred the Chola capital to Kadaram to promote commerce.
He ended overseas trade and concentrated exclusively on inland revenue.
He sent a 27-member military mission to Sri Lanka.
He favoured trade and sent a 72-member merchant mission to China.
85.x: Kulottunga I favoured trade and sent a merchant mission consisting of 72 members to China.
85.tq: Pair the policy with its exact number and reject options that replace a commercial mission with a military or administrative act.
85.sec: Later Cholas - Sri Lanka relations and decline

85.s: Which of the following factors contributed to the decline of the Chalukya-Cholas after Kulottunga I?
o: Complete withdrawal of the Cholas from Vengi before Kulottunga I
Strengthening of the central bureaucracy and disappearance of local chiefs
Abolition of local authority by the Pandyas
Weakening of the central bureaucracy and growth of local chieftains
85.x: After Kulottunga I, the central bureaucracy weakened and local chieftains grew in power. The Chalukya-Cholas subsequently declined with the rise of the Pandyas.
85.tq: Identify the cause–effect chain and reject the option that reverses the administrative trend.
85.sec: Later Cholas - Sri Lanka relations and decline

85.s: The last ruler of the Chalukya-Chola line, who was gone by 1279, was
85.x: Rajendra III was the last ruler of the Chalukya-Chola line and was gone by 1279.
85.tq: Distinguish the final ruler from earlier major rulers and use the terminal date as a check.
85.sec: Later Cholas - Sri Lanka relations and decline

85.s:
With reference to the Chola period, consider the following statements:
1. The Cholas were the first Indian power associated with overseas naval campaigns.
2. Chola activity helped spread Dravidian art to Southeast Asia.
3. Chola naval activity was confined to the inland waterways of Tamil country.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
85.x: The Cholas are described as the first Indian power with overseas naval campaigns, and their activities spread Dravidian art to Southeast Asia. Their naval activity was not confined to inland waterways.
85.tq: The absolute geographical restriction in statement 3 is the false comparison trap.
85.sec: Universal angles

85.s: Which of the following statements regarding the Chola-era Anaimangalam copper plates is correct?
o: They were returned by China during Kulottunga I's merchant mission.
They were issued by Rajendra III after the decline of the Chalukya-Cholas.
They were returned by the Netherlands at The Hague during the Prime Minister's visit in May 2026.
They were discovered during the third phase of underwater exploration off Poompuhar in September 2026.
85.x: The Netherlands returned the Chola-era Anaimangalam, or Leiden, copper plates at The Hague during the Prime Minister's visit in May 2026. They were ordered by Rajaraja I, engraved under Rajendra I and extended by Kulottunga I.
85.tq: Separate the modern repatriation event from the historical rulers connected with the inscription.
85.sec: Universal angles

85.s: The Anaimangalam copper plates are associated, in sequence, with which combination of Chola rulers?
o: Ordered by Rajaraja I, engraved under Rajendra I and extended by Kulottunga I
Ordered by Rajendra I, engraved under Kulottunga I and extended by Rajendra III
Ordered by Kulottunga I, engraved under Rajaraja I and extended by Rajendra I
Ordered by Parantaka I, engraved under Rajendra I and extended by Vijayaditya VII
85.x: The plates originated through an order of Rajaraja I, were engraved under Rajendra I and were extended by Kulottunga I.
85.tq: Follow the sequence of administrative action, engraving and later extension across the three rulers.
85.sec: Universal angles

85.s: The third phase of underwater exploration mentioned in connection with the early Chola capital is being conducted off
85.x: Tamil Nadu began the third phase of underwater exploration off Poompuhar, identified as an early Chola capital.
85.tq: Use the location clue and distinguish the Tamil coastal site from the Andhra Chola-period sites.
85.sec: Universal angles

85.s: Which of the following correctly states the proposed Rajaraja Chola statue and museum project?
o: A 125-metre statue at Poompuhar, planned on 52 acres at a cost of Rs 56.41 crore
A 125-foot statue at the Grand Chola Museum, Thanjavur, planned on 52 acres at a cost of Rs 56.41 crore
A 52-foot statue at the Grand Chola Museum, Thanjavur, planned on 125 acres at a cost of Rs 56.41 crore
A 125-foot statue at Rajahmundry, planned on 56.41 acres at a cost of Rs 52 crore
85.x: The proposed project is a 125-foot Rajaraja Chola statue at the Grand Chola Museum in Thanjavur, spread over 52 acres and costing Rs 56.41 crore.
85.tq: Check each numerical component—height, area and cost—before accepting the combined option.
85.sec: Universal angles

85.s:
Consider the following statements about the Chola–Chalukya relationship in the Andhra region:
1. Vengi was a prize in the Chola–Chalukya wars.
2. Kulottunga I united the Tamil and Andhra kingdoms.
3. The Mandalika Yugam followed from 1076 to about 1210.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
85.x: Vengi was central to Chola–Chalukya rivalry; Kulottunga I united the Tamil and Andhra kingdoms; and the Mandalika Yugam followed from 1076 to approximately 1210.
85.tq: Treat the regional political development and its time span as separate checks before selecting the combination.
85.sec: Universal angles

85.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Last Eastern Chalukya — Vijayaditya VII, who died in 1279
Last Eastern Chalukya — Rajaraja I, who died in 1075
85.x: Kulottunga I was the first Chalukya-Chola king. Vijayaditya VII was the last Eastern Chalukya and died in 1075, not 1279.
85.tq: Check both the dynastic position and the associated date to detect the swapped ruler–date pair.
85.sec: Universal angles

85.s: The last Eastern Chalukya ruler and his year of death were respectively
85.x: Vijayaditya VII was the last Eastern Chalukya ruler and died in 1075.
85.tq: Use the dynasty boundary clue and distinguish the 1075 date from the later Chalukya-Chola terminal date.
85.sec: Universal angles

86.s: In the context of Chola local administration, the term ‘variyam’ denoted:
o: A member of the village assembly
86.x: Variyam referred to the committee system in Chola village administration.
86.tq: Test the exact meaning of an administrative term against closely related terms.

86.s: The term ‘kudavolai’ in Chola local administration referred to:
o: A system of collecting land revenue
A lottery system using palm-leaf ballots placed in a pot
86.x: Kudavolai was the selection procedure in which names written on palm leaves were placed in a pot and drawn by lot.
86.tq: Discriminate between similar administrative terms by identifying the precise procedure involved.

86.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Kudumbu — Ward
2. Perumakkal — Member of the village assembly
3. Variyapperumakkal — Elected committee members
4. Variyam — Lottery system
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
86.x: Kudumbu means ward, perumakkal means a member of the village assembly, and variyapperumakkal means elected committee members. Variyam means committee system, not lottery system.
86.tq: Find the single swapped meaning among a cluster of familiar administrative terms.

86.s: Which dynasty is particularly associated with village autonomy and an elaborate system of local self-government in South India?
86.x: The Cholas are renowned for their elaborate system of village self-government and autonomous local institutions.
86.tq: Use dynasty-identification through its distinctive administrative contribution.

86.s: The Uttaramerur inscriptions relating to Chola village administration were issued during the reign of:
86.x: The two important Uttaramerur inscriptions on village administration belong to the reign of Parantaka I.
86.tq: Apply the ruler–record association rather than confusing later Chola rulers.

86.s: The two important Uttaramerur inscriptions of Parantaka I are dated to:
86.x: The Uttaramerur inscriptions of Parantaka I are dated 919 CE and 921 CE.
86.tq: Distinguish close chronological figures by selecting the exact pair of dates.

86.s: Uttaramerur, famous for inscriptions on Chola village administration, is situated in present-day:
86.x: Uttaramerur is located in Kanchipuram district.
86.tq: Test the location of a historical administrative centre against nearby Tamil regions.

86.s: Which of the following is regarded as the principal source for reconstructing Chola village government?
86.x: The Uttaramerur inscriptions provide detailed information about Chola village government and administration.
86.tq: Identify the direct epigraphic source instead of literary works or a place-name distractor.

86.s: Which one of the following was a qualification for membership in a Chola village committee according to the Uttaramerur system?
o: Ownership of at least one-fourth veli of land
Service on a committee during the previous three years
86.x: A candidate was required to own at least one-fourth veli of land. Previous committee service during the last three years was a disqualification.
86.tq: Separate eligibility conditions from disqualifications in a qualification table.

86.s:
Consider the following statements regarding qualifications for membership of Chola village committees:
1. The candidate should own a residence.
2. The candidate should be between 35 and 70 years of age.
3. Knowledge of the Vedas was among the qualifications.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
86.x: Ownership of a residence, age between 35 and 70 years, and knowledge of the Vedas were listed among the qualifications.
86.tq: Use a complete-set option when all qualification statements belong to the same institutional rule.

86.s: Which one of the following was NOT a disqualification for membership of a Chola village committee?
86.x: Owning a residence was a qualification, whereas failure to submit accounts, committing sins and stealing property were disqualifications.
86.tq: Find the qualification wrongly placed among the disqualifications.

86.s: The resolutions of the Chola village sabha were passed in the presence of:
o: The chief merchant of the nagaram
The commander of the royal army
86.x: Resolutions of the sabha were made in the presence of an official appointed by the king.
86.tq: Identify the correct authority associated with formal validation of a local decision.

86.s: Under the kudavolai procedure, the village was divided into how many wards or kudumbus?
86.x: The village was divided into 30 kudumbus or wards for the selection process.
86.tq: Recall the exact administrative unit count rather than an approximate number.

86.s: Which of the following correctly describes the kudavolai method of selection?
o: Eligible names were written on palm leaves, placed in a pot, and drawn by a young boy or girl.
All adult residents voted by raising their hands in the sabha.
Committee members inherited office from their predecessors.
Candidates were nominated by the king and confirmed by merchants.
86.x: Names of eligible candidates were written on palm leaves, placed in a pot, and drawn by a young boy or girl, generally one from each ward.
86.tq: Reconstruct the procedure step by step and reject alternatives that change the selection method.

86.s: What was the normal term of office for members selected to Chola village committees?
86.x: Members of the committees held office for three-year terms.
86.tq: Test the precise duration of institutional tenure using nearby year-based distractors.

86.s: A person who had served on a Chola village committee during the preceding three years was:
o: Eligible only for a finance committee
86.x: Persons who had served on a committee during the previous three years were disqualified from selection.
86.tq: Identify the cooling-off rule by distinguishing a disqualification from re-election eligibility.

86.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Committee)
A. Samvatsara variyam
B. Eri variyam
C. Pon variyam
D. Thotta variyam

List-II (Function)
1. Gardens or orchards
2. Gold and financial matters
3. Annual works
4. Tanks and distribution of water

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
86.x: Samvatsara variyam dealt with annual works, eri variyam with tanks and water distribution, pon variyam with gold and finance, and thotta variyam with gardens.
86.tq: Start with the distinctive eri and thotta functions, then complete the committee–function pairs.

86.s: The Eri variyam in the Chola village administration was primarily concerned with:
o: Tanks and distribution of water to fields
86.x: Eri variyam managed tanks and the distribution of water to agricultural fields.
86.tq: Associate the committee name with its functional subject and avoid a neighbouring committee’s role.

86.s: Which committee was concerned with gold, finance and currency checking?
86.x: Pon variyam dealt with gold and related financial and currency-checking matters.
86.tq: Use the semantic clue in a committee name while checking it against exact functions.

86.s: The Panchavara variyam was described as the:
o: Committee for distribution of irrigation water
86.x: Panchavara variyam functioned as a standing committee concerned with supervision.
86.tq: Distinguish the standing supervisory body from committees with specialised sectoral functions.

86.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
86.x: Pon variyam dealt with gold, finance and currency checking, not temple worship.
86.tq: Find the committee whose function has been replaced by a function belonging outside the list.

86.s: The ‘ur’ in Chola local administration was the general assembly of residents in:
86.x: Ur was the general assembly in ordinary non-brahmadeya, or vellanvagai, villages.
86.tq: Distinguish village assemblies by settlement type and social composition.

86.s: Which of the following correctly describes the Sabha or Mahasabha in the Chola period?
o: An assembly of merchants in commercial centres
A general assembly of all residents of non-brahmadeya villages
A royal committee for checking currency
A Brahmin-only assembly of agraharas or brahmadeya villages
86.x: Sabha or Mahasabha was the Brahmin-only assembly of agraharas or brahmadeya villages, with membership based on property, family, learning and conduct.
86.tq: Discriminate among ur, sabha and nagaram by composition and settlement type.

86.s: The nagaram in the Chola administrative system was an assembly of:
86.x: Nagaram was the assembly of merchant groups in market and commercial centres.
86.tq: Match the institution with its economic setting rather than its village counterpart.

86.s: The term ‘brahmadeya’ referred to:
o: A military settlement of the Chola king
Rent-free land or villages granted to Brahmins
A tax imposed on merchant groups
86.x: Brahmadeya denoted rent-free land or villages granted to Brahmins.
86.tq: Test a specialised land-tenure term against administrative and fiscal distractors.

86.s:
Consider the following statements about the powers of Chola village assemblies:
1. They possessed proprietary rights over communal land.
2. They exercised control over private land.
3. They could deal with newly acquired village land.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
86.x: Chola village assemblies had proprietary rights over communal land, controlled private land and were regarded as the absolute proprietors of newly acquired village lands.
86.tq: Recognise the broad extent of local land authority when all three statements describe related powers.
86.sec: Powers of assemblies - land, tax, justice, temple

86.s: Which one of the following was within the fiscal authority of Chola village assemblies?
o: Raising loans, levying taxes and collecting royal dues
86.x: Village assemblies could raise loans, levy taxes and collect royal dues in cash, kind or both.
86.tq: Identify the locally exercisable fiscal powers without extending them to sovereign powers.
86.sec: Powers of assemblies - land, tax, justice, temple

86.s: If a landholder failed to meet the obligations imposed by the Chola village assembly, the assembly could:
o: Transfer the matter only to a foreign merchant guild
86.x: The assembly could auction the land of defaulters after exercising its fiscal and land-management powers.
86.tq: Apply the stated enforcement power to a concrete fiscal default scenario.
86.sec: Powers of assemblies - land, tax, justice, temple

86.s: Which of the following functions was performed through committees of the Chola village assemblies?
o: Law and order and administration of justice
86.x: Committees of the village assemblies handled law and order and justice, in addition to other local functions.
86.tq: Separate local committee functions from powers belonging to the central monarchy.
86.sec: Powers of assemblies - land, tax, justice, temple

86.s: Rajaraja I directed the Cholamandalam sabhas to provide services to the:
86.x: Rajaraja I directed the Cholamandalam sabhas to serve the Brihadeshvara temple.
86.tq: Use the ruler–temple association while avoiding famous South Indian temple distractors.
86.sec: Powers of assemblies - land, tax, justice, temple

86.s: Which one of the following combinations correctly represents the areas covered by the committees recorded at Uttaramerur?
o: Foreign trade, naval warfare, diplomacy and coin minting
Royal succession, military conquest, espionage and taxation alone
Agricultural slavery, overseas colonisation, astronomy and medicine
86.x: The Uttaramerur record refers to committees dealing with irrigation, gardens, justice and finance.
86.tq: Select the combination formed entirely from documented local administrative functions.

86.s: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the method of selecting members to the Chola village assembly from that followed under the 73rd Constitutional Amendment?
o: Chola members were nominated by the king, whereas PRI members are selected by lottery
Chola members were selected by lottery among qualified persons, whereas PRIs are directly elected
Both used direct election by universal adult franchise
Both used nomination by the village assembly
86.x: The Chola system used the kudavolai lottery among qualified persons. Under the 73rd Amendment framework, representatives are directly elected by the Gram Sabha electorate.
86.tq: Discriminate between two similar-looking selection systems.

86.s:
Consider the following statements regarding eligibility for membership of the Chola village assembly and the Panchayati Raj Institutions:
1. Chola eligibility included property ownership, Vedic learning and an age range of 35 to 70 years.
2. Panchayati Raj elections operate on universal adult franchise.
3. The 73rd Amendment prescribes Vedic learning as a constitutional qualification.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
86.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The 73rd Amendment does not prescribe Vedic learning; qualifications for PRI elections operate within the constitutional and state-law framework.
86.tq: Separate historical eligibility conditions from modern constitutional qualifications.

86.s: The normal term of the Chola village assembly, in comparison with that of a Panchayati Raj Institution, was respectively:
86.x: The Chola village assemblies had three-year terms, whereas Panchayati Raj Institutions have five-year terms.
86.tq: Compare closely related numerical terms.

86.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: 73rd Amendment PRI — Vedic learning as an eligibility condition
Chola village assembly — One-third reservation for women
73rd Amendment PRI — Variyams as the standard committee system
Chola village assembly — Kudavolai selection and Variyams
86.x: The Chola village assembly used the kudavolai method and functioned through vari yams or committees. Women’s reservation and state-law-based standing committees belong to the modern PRI framework, while Vedic learning was not a PRI condition.
86.tq: Find the correctly matched historical institution among reversed comparisons.

86.s: Under the 73rd Constitutional Amendment, which of the following is the correct constitutional range dealing with Panchayati Raj Institutions?
86.x: Panchayats are dealt with in Part IX of the Constitution, covering Articles 243 to 243O.
86.tq: Use the constitutional Part and Article-range distinction.

86.s: Which Article of the Constitution recognises the Gram Sabha under the Panchayati Raj framework?
86.x: Article 243A deals with the Gram Sabha. Article 243C concerns the composition of Panchayats, Article 243D reservations, and Article 243E duration.
86.tq: Discriminate among neighbouring constitutional Articles.

86.s:
Consider the following statements about the Panchayati Raj structure under the 73rd Amendment:
1. It provides for a three-tier structure.
2. The intermediate tier may be omitted in a State having a population not exceeding twenty lakh.
3. The term of a Panchayat is five years.
4. Election must be held within six months of the dissolution of a Panchayat.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
86.x: All four statements are correct. The intermediate tier is optional below the twenty-lakh population threshold, Panchayats normally have five-year terms, and elections after dissolution are to be completed within six months.
86.tq: Combine structural, numerical and time-limit provisions in one coded question.

86.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with regard to the modern Panchayati Raj framework?
86.x: Article 243C deals with the composition of Panchayats. Article 243D concerns reservation, Article 243E duration, and Article 243A the Gram Sabha.
86.tq: Start from the sure Article–provision pair and eliminate reversals.

86.s: Which dynasty is most prominently associated with the culmination of village autonomy and elaborate local self-government in early medieval South India?
86.x: The Cholas are especially remembered for elected village assemblies, committees and the kudavolai lottery, representing the culmination of local self-government.
86.tq: Identify the dynasty associated with the hallmark institutional feature.
86.sec: Village autonomy as the hallmark - dynasty comparison

86.s:
Consider the following statements regarding local government under different South Indian dynasties:
1. Pallava inscriptions refer to sabha and ur assemblies.
2. The Cholas developed local institutions on an existing base.
3. The Badami Chalukya polity is described as highly centralised.
4. Rashtrakutas allowed village assemblies a significant role in administration and disputes.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
86.x: All four statements are correct. Pallava institutions provided an earlier base, the Cholas elaborated them, Badami Chalukya administration was highly centralised, and Rashtrakuta village assemblies had a significant administrative and dispute-related role.
86.tq: Test a dynasty comparison through several independently correct statements.
86.sec: Village autonomy as the hallmark - dynasty comparison

86.s: Who described the Chola system of elected assemblies, committees and lottery as an example of “grassroots democracy”?
86.x: Nilakanta Sastri regarded the Chola system as a remarkable example of grassroots democracy. Burton Stein is associated with the segmentary-state interpretation.
86.tq: Avoid the author–interpretation swap trap.
86.sec: Village autonomy as the hallmark - dynasty comparison

86.s: Burton Stein’s concept of the Chola polity as a “segmentary state” primarily stresses that:
o: local autonomy remained intact at the periphery
the king exercised uniform direct control over every village
the Chola state had no administrative institutions
village assemblies were abolished outside the capital
86.x: The segmentary-state interpretation stresses the persistence of local autonomy, particularly at the periphery, rather than uniform central control.
86.tq: Translate an interpretive theory into its central administrative implication.
86.sec: Village autonomy as the hallmark - dynasty comparison

86.s: The nattar was primarily associated with which level of Chola administration?
o: The nadu level above the village
86.x: The nattar was the assembly of a nadu, functioning above the village level and dealing with matters such as revenue collection and local disputes.
86.tq: Use the administrative-level distinction between village and nadu.

86.s: Who constituted the nattar of a nadu?
o: Royal officials appointed from the capital
Leading peasant landholders, mainly vellalas, of the nadu
86.x: The nattar consisted of leading peasant landholders, particularly vellalas, of the nadu.
86.tq: Test composition through the local elite versus royal-official trap.

86.s: Which of the following functions was associated with the nattar?
o: Collecting revenue and settling local disputes above the village level
86.x: The nattar handled revenue collection and local disputes at the nadu level, above the individual village.
86.tq: Match an assembly with its actual functions rather than a neighbouring institution’s task.

86.s: The nagaram of a nadu was associated mainly with its:
86.x: The nagaram was the organisation of the nadu’s market town and worked alongside the nattar.
86.tq: Distinguish the commercial town institution from the agrarian nadu assembly.

86.s: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between the nattar and the nagaram?
o: The nattar operated at the village level, while the nagaram operated at the imperial level
The nattar represented the nadu’s leading landholders, while the nagaram of its market town worked alongside it
The nagaram replaced the nattar in all revenue matters
Both terms referred exclusively to women’s committees
86.x: The nattar was the nadu-level assembly of leading landholders, while the nagaram was associated with the nadu’s market town and functioned alongside it.
86.tq: Separate two related local institutions by composition and sphere of activity.

86.s: Prime Minister Narendra Modi cited the Chola kudavolai system at Uttaramerur as evidence of:
o: exclusive royal appointment of village officers
the complete absence of local elections in India
the origin of modern political parties
86.x: The kudavolai, or ballot-pot system, was cited as evidence of India’s early democratic traditions. Its current relevance was highlighted in August 2025.
86.tq: Connect a historical institution with its stated contemporary relevance.

86.s: The term “kudavolai” in the context of Chola local administration refers to:
o: a ballot-pot lottery for selecting qualified representatives
a tax imposed on market towns
86.x: Kudavolai was the ballot-pot method by which qualified persons were selected through lottery for village administration.
86.tq: Resolve a specialised institutional term by its exact function.

86.s: Which of the following is the most appropriate criticism of the democratic character of the Chola village assemblies?
o: They were entirely controlled by foreign merchants
They excluded every form of local participation
They operated only through direct universal adult franchise
They were democratic in form but limited by property, education and elite status
86.x: The system had democratic procedures, but participation was restricted to an educated and propertied elite, especially Brahmins in sabhas.
86.tq: Distinguish democratic procedure from inclusive participation.

86.s:
Consider the following statements about the limitations of Chola local self-government:
1. Participation in sabhas was associated with propertied and Vedic-learned Brahmins.
2. The system has been criticised as elitist despite its democratic form.
3. Universal adult franchise was its basis of representation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
86.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The system was not based on universal adult franchise; eligibility was restricted by property, learning and other conditions.
86.tq: Spot the modern democratic concept inserted into a historical system.

86.s: Which of the following provides a weaker Andhra parallel to the Chola village mahajana assemblies?
86.x: Kakatiya and Velanati inscriptions refer to village mahajana assemblies in Andhra, forming a weaker parallel to the Chola institutions.
86.tq: Identify the correct regional comparison from closely related dynastic names.

86.s: Which one of the following statements is NOT correctly matched?
o: Nattar — direct universal adult franchise body under the 73rd Amendment
Burton Stein — segmentary state and local autonomy
Nilakanta Sastri — Chola local self-government as grassroots democracy
86.x: The nattar was a Chola nadu-level assembly of leading vellala landholders. It was not a body created under the 73rd Amendment and was not based on universal adult franchise.
86.tq: Find the institutional term wrongly transferred from the medieval to the modern system.

87.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?

1. Vellanvagai — Land of non-Brahmin peasant proprietors
2. Brahmadeya — Land gifted to Brahmins
3. Devadana — Land gifted to temples
4. Pallichchandam — Land donated to Jaina institutions
87.x: Vellanvagai denoted land held by non-Brahmin peasant proprietors, while brahmadeya, devadana and pallichchandam referred respectively to land gifted to Brahmins, temples and Jaina institutions.
87.tq: Start from the sure pair and eliminate combinations that omit correctly matched terms.
87.sec: Land and revenue terms → meaning (eripatti, vellanvagai, brahmadeya, devadana, salabhoga, pallichchandam)

87.s:
With reference to Chola land classifications, consider the following statements:
1. Salabhoga was land assigned for the maintenance of a school.
2. Taniyur was a large village, often a brahmadeya village, made into a separate administrative unit.
3. Brahmadeya villages were generally associated with a sabha.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
87.x: Salabhoga supported the maintenance of a school. Taniyur was a large, often brahmadeya, village treated as a separate unit, and brahmadeya villages had a sabha.
87.tq: Use the distinctive institutional clues—school, separate unit and sabha—to verify each statement.
87.sec: Land and revenue terms → meaning (eripatti, vellanvagai, brahmadeya, devadana, salabhoga, pallichchandam)

87.s: In the Chola land-rights system, Karanmai and Mitachi respectively denoted:
o: right to cultivate and superior possessory right
right to collect tax and right to perform forced labour
ownership of temple land and ownership of school land
tenant right and royal right over irrigation tanks
87.x: Karanmai was the right to cultivate, whereas Mitachi was the superior possessory right. Together they constituted aspects of kani rights.
87.tq: Separate the two closely related components of kani rights by matching each term with its precise function.
87.sec: Land and revenue terms → meaning (eripatti, vellanvagai, brahmadeya, devadana, salabhoga, pallichchandam)

87.s: Which of the following correctly describes the terms Kaniyudaiyar and Ulukudi in Chola agrarian society?
o: Kaniyudaiyar were land-owning farmers, while Ulukudi were tenants.
Kaniyudaiyar were temple officials, while Ulukudi were village judges.
Kaniyudaiyar were tenants, while Ulukudi were land-owning farmers.
Both terms referred exclusively to Brahmin landholders.
87.x: Kaniyudaiyar were farmers who owned land, whereas Ulukudi denoted tenants.
87.tq: Test the reversed-meaning trap by distinguishing ownership from tenancy.
87.sec: Land and revenue terms → meaning (eripatti, vellanvagai, brahmadeya, devadana, salabhoga, pallichchandam)

87.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Kadamai — Land revenue collected in kind
Vetti — Forced labour owed by villagers to the state
Irai — Compulsory feeding of state officials
87.x: Irai meant a tax or levy on land. The obligation to feed state officials was called Eccoru.
87.tq: Find the single swapped meaning among closely related revenue and service terms.
87.sec: Land and revenue terms → meaning (eripatti, vellanvagai, brahmadeya, devadana, salabhoga, pallichchandam)

87.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Chola fiscal and labour terminology:
1. Antarayam was a rural tax collected in cash.
2. Eccoru referred to the obligation to feed state officials.
3. Nettal denoted compulsory labour.
4. Kasu was a gold coin.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
87.x: All four statements are correct: Antarayam was a cash rural tax, Eccoru was the obligation to feed officials, Nettal was compulsory labour and Kasu was a gold coin.

87.sec: Land and revenue terms → meaning (eripatti, vellanvagai, brahmadeya, devadana, salabhoga, pallichchandam)

87.s: Which of the following statements regarding Chola kingship is correct?
o: The successor was named during the king’s lifetime and could function as yuvaraja and co-regent.
The Chola king generally named his successor only after his own death.
The office of yuvaraja was reserved exclusively for Brahmin officials.
Chola succession was decided by the nadu assembly in every case.
87.x: Chola kings commonly named their successor during their own lifetime and made him yuvaraja and co-regent. Rajendra I became co-regent in 1012 and king in 1014.
87.tq: Reject absolute alternatives and identify the succession practice tied to the yuvaraja.
87.sec: Chola kingship - succession, titles, rituals, temple role

87.s: Rajaraja I was described by the title ‘Ulakalanada Perumal’ because he was regarded as:
o: the king who abolished hereditary officials
the ruler who measured the earth, like Vishnu’s three strides
the conqueror of the entire island of Sri Lanka
the patron who built all the major Chola temples
87.x: Ulakalanada Perumal means one who measured the earth, an image associated with Vishnu’s three strides.
87.tq: Use the literal meaning of the title to identify the correct royal association.
87.sec: Chola kingship - succession, titles, rituals, temple role

87.s:
Which of the following combinations contains only titles used for Chola kings in inscriptions?

1. Ko
2. Perumal
3. Raja-rajadhiraja
4. Ko-konmai kondan
87.x: Ko, Perumal, Raja-rajadhiraja and Ko-konmai kondan were all inscriptional titles associated with Chola kingship.
87.tq: Treat a list question as an inclusion test and verify every listed title.
87.sec: Chola kingship - succession, titles, rituals, temple role

87.s:
Consider the following statements about the religious and political representation of Chola kings:
1. Chola kings were compared to gods.
2. Images of kings and queens were installed beside deities in temples.
3. Inscriptions praised the king as a warrior, patron of arts and protector of varnashrama dharma.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
87.x: The Chola king was presented in divine and royal terms: royal images could be placed beside deities, and inscriptions praised his military, cultural and social-religious roles.
87.tq: Combine political, temple and inscriptional evidence to test the full conception of Chola kingship.
87.sec: Chola kingship - succession, titles, rituals, temple role

87.s: Which institution advised the Chola king in matters of governance?
87.x: A council of ministers advised the Chola king. The nadu assembly and hereditary bodyguards had different functions.
87.tq: Identify the body associated specifically with advice to the sovereign.
87.sec: Chola kingship - succession, titles, rituals, temple role

87.s: The bureaucracy of the Chola state expanded notably during the reign of Rajaraja I but weakened after the reign of:
87.x: The bureaucracy expanded from the reign of Rajaraja I and weakened after Kulottunga I as local chieftains gained greater power.
87.tq: Use the change-over-time clue and distinguish the period of expansion from the period of decline.
87.sec: Chola kingship - succession, titles, rituals, temple role

87.s: Chola kings were protected by hereditary bodyguards who were generally paid through:
87.x: Hereditary bodyguards were maintained through land assignments yielding revenue. Officials too were commonly paid through revenue-bearing land assignments.
87.tq: Match the security arrangement with its stated fiscal source rather than with a general tax category.
87.sec: Chola kingship - succession, titles, rituals, temple role

87.s:
Arrange the following Chola administrative units from the lowest to the highest level:
A. Nadu
B. Mandalam
C. Ur
D. Kottam or Valanadu
87.x: The order from lowest to highest was Ur, Nadu, Kottam or Valanadu, and Mandalam.
87.tq: Build the hierarchy from the village upward and identify the highest provincial unit last.

87.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the Chola administrative hierarchy?
87.x: The hierarchy proceeded from Ur at the village level, through Nadu and Kottam or Valanadu, to Mandalam at the provincial level.
87.tq: Read the units as levels and eliminate options that reverse adjacent administrative stages.

87.s:
With reference to the Mandalams of the Chola Empire, consider the following statements:
1. A Mandalam was a province.
2. The Chola Empire had eight Mandalams.
3. Mandalams were placed under viceroys or governors, who could be princes or nobles.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
87.x: Mandalam was the provincial unit, the empire had eight such provinces, and they were administered by viceroys or governors, often princes or nobles.
87.tq: Verify the unit, its numerical count and its administrative head separately.

87.s: The assembly associated with the Chola district-level unit called Nadu was known as:
87.x: Nadu was the district-level unit, and its assembly was associated with the nattar. Ur, sabha and nagaram referred to village or settlement institutions in different contexts.
87.tq: Use the unit-to-assembly association to distinguish nattar from the other local bodies.

87.s: Which of the following statements about Chola provincial territories is correct?
o: Some provinces were annexed principalities, while others were vassal territories paying tribute.
All provinces were independent republics outside the imperial structure.
Vassal territories were exempt from all tribute obligations.
Every province was directly administered by the king without intermediary authorities.
87.x: Chola provincial territories included both annexed principalities and samanta or vassal territories that paid tribute.
87.tq: Avoid absolute statements and distinguish annexed territories from tributary samanta territories.

87.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Adhikari — Royal officer supervising local bodies
Nattar — Members of the royal court of justice
87.x: An adhikari was a royal officer supervising local bodies. Perundaram were the highest officials, sirudaram were lower officials, and nattar were members of the nadu assembly.
87.tq: Start with the functional description of adhikari and reject reversed ranks or substituted institutions.

87.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Chola officials and departments:
1. Perundaram denoted the highest officials.
2. Sirudaram denoted lower officials.
3. Puravu-varitinaikkalam or Shrikaranam was the revenue department.
4. Dharmasana was the royal court of justice.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
87.x: All four statements are correct. Perundaram and sirudaram represented higher and lower officials respectively; Shrikaranam was the revenue department and Dharmasana the royal court of justice.
87.tq: Check rank, department and judicial function separately before choosing the complete combination.

87.s: Which of the following is the correct association between a Chola local institution and its description?
o: Nattar — Members of the Nadu assembly
Perundaram — Members of the village sabha only
87.x: Nattar were members of the Nadu assembly. Adhikari were royal officers supervising local bodies, while perundaram and sirudaram referred to higher and lower officials, not provincial governors.
87.tq: Use the specific institutional role and watch for rank and office substitutions.

87.s: Who among the following Chola rulers is associated with a detailed land survey and assessment that was repeated periodically?
87.x: Rajaraja I conducted a detailed land survey and assessment, and such surveys were repeated periodically.

87.s: The normal rate of Chola land revenue was approximately:

87.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Chola land revenue:

2. It was collected through village assemblies.
3. It was invariably collected only in cash.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
87.x: Chola land revenue could be paid in cash, kind or both, and was collected through village assemblies. It was not invariably collected only in cash.

87.sec: Land survey and revenue - Rajaraja's survey, kadamai, taxes

Kudimai — Duty to feed visiting state officials

A duty to supply elephants to the army
A rural tax collected in cash

Kulottunga I — 8,943 elephants granted to a temple

87.x: Rajendra I dug the Chola Gangam tank, and later Cauvery channels were built on the Sangam-era Kallanai of Karikala. The eri variyam managed tanks, not royal correspondence.

Loyal bodyguard troops sworn to die with the king
Provincial governors appointed from among princes

87.s: The principal function of the olai-nayagam was to:

87.s: Chola royal orders generally consisted of:
o: A Sanskrit preamble followed by a Tamil operative part
Tamil genealogy followed by a Sanskrit grant
87.x: The royal orders had a Sanskrit preamble containing genealogy and conquests, followed by the Tamil operative portion.

87.s: Each Chola mandalam was generally governed by:
o: A viceroy or governor, often a royal prince or noble
The eri variyam elected by cultivators
A temple priest appointed by the village assembly
87.x: Each mandalam was governed by a viceroy or governor, often a royal prince or noble; offices were paid by land assignments.

87.s: Kulottunga I’s sons governed which region as viceroys or Rajapratinidhis?

87.s: Which of the following correctly represents the succession of Kulottunga I’s sons as viceroys in Vengi?
o: Vira Chola, Rajaraja Chola Gangu, Rajaraja Mummadi Chola
Rajaraja Mummadi Chola, Vira Chola, Rajaraja Chola Gangu
Rajaraja Chola Gangu, Vira Chola, Rajaraja Mummadi Chola
87.x: Rajaraja Mummadi Chola ruled first from Jagannathapuram, followed by Vira Chola and then Rajaraja Chola Gangu up to Mahendragiri.

87.s: A ‘Samanta’ in the Chola political system was:
o: A royal secretary who countersigned orders
A tank committee member elected by villagers
A temple servant given tax-free land
A defeated king restored after accepting overlordship, tribute and military obligations
87.x: A Samanta was a defeated king restored on condition that he accepted overlordship, paid tribute and provided military help.

87.s: Burton Stein characterised the Chola state as ‘segmentary’ because:
o: The entire kingdom was divided only according to caste groups
The state had no recognised royal authority
All provinces were governed directly by a centrally appointed bureaucracy
Royal authority radiated from the Kaveri core while peripheral local autonomy remained intact
87.x: Burton Stein’s segmentary model emphasised a strong Kaveri core with continuing local autonomy in peripheral areas.

87.s: Which of the following correctly contrasts the views of Burton Stein and K. A. Nilakanta Sastri on the Chola state?
o: Stein described it as centralised, whereas Sastri rejected all royal authority.
Stein described it as segmentary, whereas Sastri presented a centralised picture.
Both described it exclusively as a loose confederation.
Both denied the importance of the Kaveri core.
87.x: Burton Stein used the concept of a segmentary state, while K. A. Nilakanta Sastri offered a more centralised interpretation.
87.tq: Compare the two historians by the precise interpretation assigned to each.

87.s: The term ‘Devadana’ in the Chola period referred to:
o: Land used exclusively for tank repairs
87.x: Devadana lands were grants made to temples.
87.tq: Distinguish temple endowment terminology from irrigation and military terms.

87.s:
Consider the following statements about Chola temples:
1. They could function as major landholders.
2. They served as employers and lenders in the locality.
3. They provided venues for village assembly meetings.

87.x: Chola temples were major landholders, employers and lenders, and also served as venues for village assembly meetings.

87.s: Rajaraja I directed the Sabhas of Cholamandalam to perform services for the:

87.s: Which practice illustrates the political symbolism associated with Chola temples?
o: Using temples only as military cantonments
Installing images of kings and queens beside the deities
Prohibiting royal names in temple inscriptions
Replacing all royal images with images of village officials

The construction of the Grand Anicut by Karikala
The abolition of tolls by Kulottunga I

Prakrit for genealogy and Tamil for the grant
Tamil for genealogy and Sanskrit for the grant

With reference to land-revenue rates, consider the following statements:

2. A later bilingual Telugu-Tamil charter was issued by Anavota Reddi.
3. The Motupalli Dharma Sasanam of 1416 was associated with Deva Raya I.
4. The 1416 Dharma Sasanam belonged to the reign of Ganapatideva.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
94.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. The 1416 Motupalli Dharma Sasanam belonged to Vijayanagara ruler Deva Raya I, not Ganapatideva.
94.tq: Separate similar charters by issuer, date and dynasty.

94.s: In the expression ‘Abhaya Sasanam’, the word ‘Abhaya’ conveys the idea of
94.x: ‘Abhaya’ means assurance of safety. The charter used this principle to protect foreign and seafaring traders.
94.tq: Use the literal meaning of the key term to identify the charter’s purpose.

94.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

1. Arikesari Samudram — Prola II
2. Ramappa tank — Recherla Rudra
3. Pakhala tank — Mummadi Nayaka
4. Laknavaram — Ganapatideva
94.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. Arikesari Samudram was built by Prola II, Ramappa tank by Recherla Rudra, Pakhala tank by Mummadi Nayaka, and Laknavaram by Ganapatideva.
94.tq: Start with the sure builder-tank pairs and eliminate codes containing a swapped ruler or tank.

94.s: Who constructed the Ghanapuram tank?
94.x: Ghanapuram tank was constructed by Ganapatideva.
94.tq: Test a direct builder-tank association from the irrigation record.

94.s: Bayyaram tank is associated with which builder?
o: Surambika, wife of Peda Komati Vema
Mummadi Nayaka, son of Bayyana Nayaka
94.x: Bayyaram tank was built by Mailamba, the sister of Ganapati.
94.tq: Use the kinship detail to distinguish the builder from other tank patrons.

94.s: Kunda Samudram, also called Chouda Samudram, was associated with
94.x: Kunda Samudram or Chouda Samudram was associated with Kundamamba and Malyala Chauda respectively.
94.tq: Combine alternative names with their associated patrons to avoid splitting one tank into two unrelated entries.

94.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
94.x: Pakhala tank was built by Mummadi Nayaka, son of Bayyana Nayaka, not by Mailamba. Mailamba was associated with Bayyaram tank.
94.tq: Find the swapped builder by comparing patrons of neighbouring tanks.

94.s:
Which one of the following statements about tank irrigation is correct?

1. Large tanks were called Samudrams.
2. Golusukattu cheruvulu were linked chain tanks.
3. Surplus water could pass downhill from one tank to the next.
4. Dashabandhamu referred to tax-free land assigned for tank maintenance.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
94.x: All four statements are correct. Samudrams were large tanks, Golusukattu cheruvulu formed linked chains, surplus flowed to lower tanks, and Dashabandhamu was tax-free land for upkeep.
94.tq: Confirm the complete irrigation-system description, including the maintenance arrangement.

94.s: Tank-building was counted among the Sapta Santanalu, which refers to
94.x: Sapta Santanalu means seven meritorious works. The list included a son, temple, garden, tank, agrahara, literature and treasure.
94.tq: Distinguish a cultural-religious classification from administrative and fiscal categories.

94.s: Which of the following was NOT included among the Sapta Santanalu?
94.x: The Sapta Santanalu included son, temple, garden, tank, agrahara, literature and treasure. A merchant guild was not one of the seven meritorious works.
94.tq: Eliminate the item belonging to trade rather than the list of meritorious works.

94.s: The Porumamilla tank inscription is associated with which combination?
o: 1369, Bhaskara, son of Bukka I, Vijayanagara period
1416, Deva Raya I, Motupalli, Reddi period
94.x: The Porumamilla tank inscription dates to 1369 and was issued by Bhaskara, son of Vijayanagara ruler Bukka I. It belongs to the Vijayanagara period and lists twelve requisites of a good tank.
94.tq: Combine date, person, dynasty and inscription subject to separate similar records.

94.s: The Porumamilla inscription is particularly important in the study of irrigation because it
o: records the twelve requisites of a good tank
defines the five classes of merchant guilds
records the tax rates on imported perfumes
lists the foreign merchants protected at Motupalli
94.x: The Porumamilla inscription of 1369 lists twelve requisites of a good tank. It is from the Vijayanagara period, though it is often studied alongside Kakatiya irrigation works.
94.tq: Identify the inscription from its distinctive technical subject rather than its dynasty alone.

94.s: Which one of the following places was noted for the production of iron during the Kakatiya period?
94.x: Guthikonda and Palnadu were known for iron production. Nirmal was associated with knives, while Warangal was known for carpets and textiles.
94.tq: Use the industry–centre association and eliminate nearby but different craft centres.

94.s:
Consider the following pairs:

1. Ratna kambalu — Warangal
2. Knives — Nirmal
3. Diamonds — Golconda region
4. Iron — Warangal

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
94.x: Ratna kambalu was associated with Warangal, knives with Nirmal and diamonds with the Golconda region. Iron was associated with Guthikonda and Palnadu, not Warangal.
94.tq: Start from the sure industry–centre pairs and identify the reversed association.

94.s: Marco Polo is said to have remarked that the fineness of which Kakatiya textile was such that a seven-yard saree could fit into a matchbox?
94.x: Marco Polo is said to have described the extremely fine cloth of the region in this manner; the material is identified as fine muslin.
94.tq: Test the distinctive traveller–observation association directly.

94.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding painting in Orugallu during the Kakatiya period?
o: Machaladevi was a male court painter of the Kalyani Chalukyas.
Painting was confined to the Golconda region and had no association with Orugallu.
Orugallu had about 1,500 painters' houses, and Machaladevi was a woman painter.
Orugallu had about 150 painters' houses, led by Machaladevi.
94.x: Orugallu is described as having 1,500 painters' houses, and Machaladevi is identified as a woman painter.
94.tq: Separate the precise number from the nearby wrong figure and swapped identity.

94.s:
Which of the following statements about Kakatiya economic activity is correct?

1. Cotton growing and weaving were major activities.
2. Fine muslin was exported.
3. Diamond trade was associated with the Golconda region.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
94.x: Cotton cultivation and weaving were major activities, fine muslin was exported, and the Golconda region was associated with diamond trade.
94.tq: Check each economic activity independently before choosing the combined code.

94.s: The Nayankara system in its reorganised Kakatiya form is principally associated with which ruler?
94.x: Prataparudra II is identified with the introduction or reorganisation of the Nayankara system in the Kakatiya kingdom.
94.tq: Use the ruler–administrative reform association without confusing earlier Kakatiya rulers.

94.s: Which one of the following best describes the Nayankara system?
o: Military commanders were made administrators of Sthalas or Mandalams and were assigned responsibility for forts.
Temple authorities collected all taxes and maintained the royal army.
Civil scribes were appointed as village accountants without military duties.
Merchants were granted exclusive control over provincial administration.
94.x: Under the Nayankara system, military commanders served as administrators of Sthalas or Mandalams and protected specified forts.
94.tq: Identify the institutional arrangement from the roles performed by the Nayakas.

94.s: Which of the following was NOT an obligation of a Kakatiya Nayaka holding Nayakasthalam?
o: Paying a fixed annual sum or tribute to the king
Keeping the entire revenue without any payment to the king
Maintaining a fixed military force for the king
Remitting the remaining revenue after meeting prescribed obligations
94.x: A Nayaka retained a share of revenue for maintaining troops, paid a fixed annual sum to the king and remitted the balance. The entire revenue was not retained.
94.tq: Find the option that reverses the stated revenue and military obligations.

94.s: The villages assigned to Nayakas in lieu of salary were known as:
94.x: Nayakas received villages called Nayakasthalam instead of a regular salary, drawing revenue from them to meet their obligations.
94.tq: Discriminate between the Kakatiya grant term and the later Vijayanagara term Amaram.

94.s: The Kakatiya Nayankara system was continued in a modified form by the Vijayanagara rulers as the:
94.x: Vijayanagara continued the arrangement as the Amara-Nayankara system. The land was called Amaram and the tribute was known as Kappam or Kist.
94.tq: Match the earlier administrative institution with its later institutional form.

94.s: Which one of the following combinations is correctly matched with the Vijayanagara continuation of the Nayankara system?
o: Amaram — land; Kappam or Kist — tribute
Amaram — village accountant; Kappam — grazing tax
Amaram — judicial office; Kist — marriage tax
94.x: In the Vijayanagara form, the land assignment was called Amaram and the tribute was called Kappam or Kist.
94.tq: Separate the names of the land assignment and tribute from unrelated administrative terms.

94.s: The break-up of the Amara-Nayankara system is associated with the emergence of the:
94.x: The break-up of the Amara-Nayankara system produced the Poligars.
94.tq: Test the institutional legacy through its historical consequence.

94.s:
Which of the following works are cited as sources for the study of the Nayankara system?

1. Baddena's Neeti Sastra Muktavali
2. Ekamranatha's Pratapa Charitra
3. Shivadevayya's Purushartha Saram

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
94.x: Baddena's Neeti Sastra Muktavali and Ekamranatha's Pratapa Charitra are cited as sources for the Nayankara system. Purushartha Saram is associated with information on the 72 Niyogas.
94.tq: Distinguish sources for the Nayankara system from a source for central departments.

94.s:
Arrange the following administrative units from the largest to the smallest:

A. Grama
B. Rashtra or Mandala
C. Sthala
D. Nadu or Bhumi

Select the correct sequence.
94.x: Rashtra or Mandala was the largest province, followed by Nadu or Bhumi, Sthala and finally Grama.
94.tq: Arrange administrative units by territorial scale, using the largest and smallest as anchors.

94.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Sthala — a group of about 20 villages
Grama — largest province under a prince
94.x: A Sthala consisted of about 20 villages. Rashtra was the largest province, while Grama denoted a village.
94.tq: Use the hierarchy of territorial units to reject swapped meanings.

94.s: In Kakatiya administration, the term 'Karanam' denoted the:
o: Village headman responsible for revenue and order
94.x: Karanam was the village accountant. The Reddi was the village headman, Talari the village watchman and Sunkadhikari the toll collector.
94.tq: Discriminate among closely related village and revenue offices.

94.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Pradvivaka — collector of customs and tolls
94.x: Pradvivaka was an adviser to the king on the judicial system. The Sunkadhikari or Sunkamanya collected customs and tolls.
94.tq: Find the swapped official function in a list of administrative offices.

94.s: The 72 central departments under the Kakatiyas were known as Niyogas and were placed under the:
94.x: The central departments were called 72 Niyogas and were supervised by the Bahattara Niyogadhipati.
94.tq: Link the distinctive number with the corresponding supervising authority.

94.s: Which one of the following was NOT a member of the council comprising Pradhani, Pragada, Amatya, Mantri and Senadhipati?
94.x: Sunkamanya was a collector of tolls and customs. The other three named officials, along with Pragada and Mantri, formed the stated council.
94.tq: Use exclusion from the stated council rather than confusing a revenue officer with a ministerial office.

94.s: Who served as prime minister during the reign of Ganapatideva according to the administrative record?
94.x: Malyala Hemadri Reddi served as prime minister under Ganapatideva. Muppidi Nayudu served under Prataparudra.
94.tq: Test the ruler–prime minister association and avoid swapping the two reigns.

94.s: Which description of the nature of the Kakatiya state is correctly matched with the scholar?
94.x: Most scholars describe the Kakatiya state as a decentralised monarchy. Romila Thapar called it a metropolitan state, while Burton Stein compared it to a segmentary state.
94.tq: Keep the three scholarly characterisations separate instead of treating them as synonyms.

94.s: Land revenue during the Kakatiya period was generally fixed at what fraction of the produce?
94.x: Land revenue, referred to as bhaga or Ari, was generally one-sixth of the produce.
94.tq: Identify the precise revenue fraction and reject nearby traditional shares.

94.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes Magani from Metta?
o: Magani was irrigated wet land, whereas Metta was rain-fed dry land.
Magani was rain-fed dry land, whereas Metta was irrigated wet land.
Both terms denoted newly cultivated forest land.
94.x: Magani denoted irrigated wet land, generally used for food crops, while Metta denoted rain-fed dry land.
94.tq: Test the reversed meaning of two similar land-classification terms.

94.s:
Which of the following statements regarding Kakatiya taxes is correct?

1. Sunkam meant customs or tolls.
2. Angadisunkam was a tax on weekly markets.
3. Pullari was a grazing tax.
4. Pellipannu was a marriage tax.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
94.x: All four statements are correct: Sunkam was customs or tolls, Angadisunkam a weekly-market tax, Pullari a grazing tax and Pellipannu a marriage tax.
94.tq: Verify each tax against its taxable activity before selecting the complete combination.

94.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with its land category?
94.x: Thotapolam denoted garden land. Podu was newly cultivated land, Velipolam was rain-fed dry land and Magani was irrigated wet land.
94.tq: Identify the exact land-category meaning and reject reversed classifications.

94.s: Which one of the following statements about land rights and taxation is correct?
o: All forest land was permanently exempt from taxation.
Temple, Brahmin and Ayagar lands paid the highest land revenue.
Dashabandhamu referred to lands maintained for tanks.
94.x: Dashabandhamu referred to lands connected with tank maintenance. Arigapulu were tax-paying farmers, while temple, Brahmin and Ayagar lands were tax-exempt.
94.tq: Match the land category with its fiscal treatment and reject absolute claims.

94.s: Forest land was cleared with tax concessions primarily to:
o: Transfer all forest revenue to temples
94.x: Tax concessions on cleared forest land were intended to encourage settlement and cultivation.
94.tq: Infer the administrative purpose from the stated fiscal concession.

94.s: The twelve village functionaries known as Ayagars were generally remunerated through:
o: Only gold coins issued by the king
A fixed share of customs collected at ports
Shares of produce and service lands
94.x: The twelve Ayagars were paid through shares of produce and service lands.
94.tq: Distinguish the village-service remuneration system from military land assignments.
94.sec: Society → ayagars, caste mobility, women donors

94.s: Which one of the following pairs of women donors and tanks is correctly matched?
o: Mailamba — Bayyaram tank; Kundamamba — Kunda Samudram
Mailamba — Kunda Samudram; Kundamamba — Bayyaram tank
Mailamba — Warangal fort; Kundamamba — Bayyaram tank
94.x: Mailamba is associated with the Bayyaram tank and Kundamamba with Kunda Samudram.
94.tq: Start with the sure donor–tank pair and avoid swapping the two women.
94.sec: Society → ayagars, caste mobility, women donors

94.s:
Which of the following statements regarding the number and territorial control of Nayankaras is correct?

1. There were 72 Nayankaras, according to one account.
2. Each Nayankara guarded a fort.
3. Nayankaras controlled one-fourth of the kingdom's land.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
94.x: One account gives the number as 72; each Nayankara guarded a fort, and the Nayankaras controlled one-fourth of the kingdom's land.
94.tq: Combine the numerical, military and territorial facts without confusing them with the 75 or 77 principalities account.
94.sec: Number of Nayakas and fort bastions under Prataparudra

94.s: Which of the following groups consisted of the three generals of Prataparudra who survived the events of 1323?
o: Prolaya Nayaka, Racherla Singama and Prolaya Vemareddy
Racherla Rudra, Natavadi Buddharaja and Kundamamba
Malyala Hemadri Reddi, Muppidi Nayudu and Prolaya Nayaka
94.x: The three surviving generals named are Prolaya Nayaka, Racherla Singama and Prolaya Vemareddy.
94.tq: Use the complete name-set to distinguish the surviving generals from rulers and officials.
94.sec: Number of Nayakas and fort bastions under Prataparudra

94.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
94.x: Ari denoted land revenue or Bhumi sistu. Koru was levied on wet land, Pullari was a grazing tax, and Kanika was a customary gift.
94.tq: Start from the sure meaning and eliminate the swapped tax descriptions.

94.s: The tax levied on wet or Magani land during the Kakatiya period was known as
94.x: Koru was the tax imposed on wet or Magani land. Putti Pahindi was the tax on dry land.
94.tq: Confusable-pair discrimination between wet-land and dry-land taxes.

94.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Putti Pahindi — Tax on dry land
94.x: Pellipannu was a wedding tax, not a cattle tax. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
94.tq: Find the one wrong description among closely related taxes and cesses.

94.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Pullari — Grazing or grass-land tax
2. Kanika — Customary gift to the king or officials
3. Alam — Tax on vegetables or produce
4. Angadi Sunkam — Wedding tax
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
94.x: Pullari, Kanika and Alam are correctly matched. Angadi Sunkam was a weekly-market tax, whereas Pellipannu was the wedding tax.
94.tq: Split the options by checking the easily confused market and wedding cesses.

94.s: Which of the following was NOT listed among the other agricultural levies of the Kakatiya period?
94.x: Siddhayam, Ardhayam and Niruvidi were agricultural levies. Dari Sunkam was a road toll and belonged to the category of other sunkams.
94.tq: Classify each term by its levy category before selecting the exception.

94.s: Which of the following was included among the other sunkams mentioned in the Kakatiya period?
94.x: Burra, Madiga, Gandi and Revu were named as other sunkams. Koru, Pellipannu and Putti Pahindi had specific descriptions as land or social taxes.
94.tq: Direct recall from a named list, with nearby tax terms as distractors.

94.s: The village functionaries collectively known as Ayagars were primarily associated with which combination of activities?
94.x: The Ayagars handled village revenue, order, irrigation and records. Their functions were administrative and local rather than confined to temples or foreign trade.
94.tq: Identify the administrative cluster that fits the village-functionary system.
94.sec: Ayagar system - village functionaries, number, mode of payment

94.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the usual list of Kakatiya Ayagars?
94.x: Karanam was included among the Ayagars and was associated with village records. Gaja Sahini, Padmanayaka and Chaturanga belonged to military terminology.
94.tq: Separate village offices from military designations before matching.
94.sec: Ayagar system - village functionaries, number, mode of payment

94.s: Which of the following groups consists entirely of names included in the usual list of Ayagars?
o: Gaja Sahini, Ashwa Sahini, Mula Balam, Padmanayaka
94.x: Karanam, Reddi, Talari and Purohita were all village functionaries in the Ayagar system. The other groups contain military, trade-centre or taxation terms.
94.tq: Check whether all items belong to the same institutional list.
94.sec: Ayagar system - village functionaries, number, mode of payment

94.s: The usual mode of payment to an Ayagar consisted of
o: Cash salary alone from the royal treasury
Military jagirs without any agricultural share
Tax-free manyam land and a share of each harvest
A share in customs duties collected at ports
94.x: Ayagars received tax-free Ayagar or manyam land together with a share of each harvest instead of cash payment.
94.tq: Discriminate between land-and-harvest payment and cash or military remuneration.
94.sec: Ayagar system - village functionaries, number, mode of payment

94.s: Chaturanga bala in the Kakatiya military organisation referred to
94.x: Chaturanga bala means the army organised into four arms. It is a military classification, not a classification of forts, officers or taxes.
94.tq: Use the literal institutional context to distinguish the military term.
94.sec: Military organisation - corps, Padmanayaka chiefs, fort types

94.s: The army of Prataparudra is stated to have consisted of approximately
94.x: The figures associated with Prataparudra's army were 100 elephants, 20,000 cavalry and 900,000 infantry.
94.tq: Keep the three arms and their figures together instead of matching numbers independently.
94.sec: Military organisation - corps, Padmanayaka chiefs, fort types

94.s:
Which of the following statements regarding Kakatiya military divisions is correct?
1. Mula Balam was the king's standing army.
2. The Nayankara army formed the other major division.
3. Mula Balam consisted exclusively of village functionaries.
94.x: Mula Balam was the king's standing army, and the Nayankara army was the other major division. The third statement is false because Mula Balam was a military division, not a body of village functionaries.
94.tq: Reject the extreme exclusive description after identifying the two genuine divisions.
94.sec: Military organisation - corps, Padmanayaka chiefs, fort types

94.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Gaja Sahini — Jayapa Senani under Ganapatideva
Ashwa Sahini — Jayapa Senani under Ganapatideva
Gaja Sahini — Maraya under Prataparudra II
Ashwa Sahini — Induluri Annayya under Prataparudra II
94.x: Jayapa Senani held the position of Gaja Sahini under Ganapatideva. Gangaya Sahini was associated with Ashwa Sahini under Ganapatideva, while Maraya held that position under Prataparudra II.
94.tq: Match the corps head with both the correct corps and ruler.
94.sec: Military organisation - corps, Padmanayaka chiefs, fort types

94.s: Padmanayakas in the Kakatiya period were
o: A group of port merchants from Motupalli
Village accountants paid only in cash
Recherla Velama chiefs and important Kakatiya commanders
94.x: Padmanayakas were Recherla Velama chiefs and key Kakatiya commanders. They later founded the Velama kingdom.
94.tq: Use the person-group and later political role to identify the correct description.
94.sec: Military organisation - corps, Padmanayaka chiefs, fort types

94.s: Which of the following is correctly matched?
94.x: Giridurga means a hill fort. Jaladurga was a water fort, Vanadurga a forest fort and Sthaladurga a plain fort.
94.tq: Discriminate among similar fort names by their environmental prefixes.
94.sec: Military organisation - corps, Padmanayaka chiefs, fort types

94.s: Which statement about the Warangal fort is correct?
o: It was a water fort without any surrounding land defence.
It was exclusively a forest fort without defensive walls.
It consisted only of a single wall on a hill.
It had concentric walls and a moat.
94.x: Warangal fort was characterised by concentric walls and a moat. Its defensive design was not limited to a single wall or a purely natural setting.
94.tq: Select the precise structural feature rather than the generic fort type.
94.sec: Military organisation - corps, Padmanayaka chiefs, fort types

94.s: Which one of the following ports was located on the Nellore coast?
94.x: Krishnapatnam was situated on the Nellore coast. Hamsaladeevi was associated with the Krishna delta, while Machilipatnam was associated with Krishna.
94.tq: Use coastal-location discrimination among the listed ports.
94.sec: Ports and trade centres → other names, imports and exports

94.s: Hamsaladeevi was associated with the
94.x: Hamsaladeevi was located in the Krishna delta. It is also identified with the Guntur area in the stated geographical description.
94.tq: Match the port with its coastal or deltaic location.
94.sec: Ports and trade centres → other names, imports and exports

94.s: Which of the following was included among the exports from Kakatiya ports?
94.x: Diamonds, fine cotton textiles or muslin, spices, iron, gold and rubies were listed as exports. Arabian war horses, silk and perfumes were imports.
94.tq: Separate exported commodities from the specifically listed imports.
94.sec: Ports and trade centres → other names, imports and exports

94.s: Which one of the following was imported for use by the Kakatiya cavalry?
94.x: Arabian war horses were imported for the cavalry. Fine muslin, rubies and iron were among the listed exports.
94.tq: Link the imported commodity to its stated military use.
94.sec: Ports and trade centres → other names, imports and exports

94.s:
The Kakatiya ports maintained trade relations with which of the following regions?
1. China
2. Persia
3. Arabia
4. Ceylon
5. The East Indies
94.x: China, Persia, Arabia, Ceylon and the East Indies were all listed as trading partners of the Kakatiya ports.
94.tq: Verify the complete partner list before choosing the inclusive combination.
94.sec: Ports and trade centres → other names, imports and exports

94.s: Which of the following was NOT included among the other trade centres associated with the Kakatiyas?
94.x: Pedaganjam, Tripurantakam and Manthena were listed as other trade centres. Krishnapatnam was listed as a port on the Nellore coast.
94.tq: Distinguish the inland trade-centre list from the separate list of ports.
94.sec: Highways and trade routes → towns connected

94.s: The Kakatiyas controlled routes connecting the
o: Tamil interior and the Arabian Peninsula exclusively
Deccan interior and the eastern coast
Western coast and the Himalayan region
94.x: Kakatiya control extended over routes between the Deccan interior and the eastern coast.
94.tq: Identify the broad geographical direction of the controlled trade routes.
94.sec: Highways and trade routes → towns connected

94.s: Marco Polo arrived on the Coromandel coast in 1292 during the reign of
94.x: Marco Polo arrived on the Coromandel coast in 1292, during the reign of Rudrama Devi.
94.tq: Match the precise date with the ruler who was reigning at that time.
94.sec: Marco Polo on Motupalli - goods and trade, Rudrama's reign

94.s:
Which of the following observations is associated with Marco Polo's account of Motupalli?
1. It was a flourishing sea-trade centre.
2. Oppressive taxes on merchants were absent.
3. Rice was described as the only local grain.
4. People generally wore loincloths because of the heat.
94.x: Marco Polo described Motupalli as a flourishing sea-trade centre and noted the absence of oppressive merchant taxes, the heat and loincloths, and rice as the only local grain.
94.tq: Check all four distinct observations from the traveller's account.
94.sec: Marco Polo on Motupalli - goods and trade, Rudrama's reign

94.s: Marco Polo noted the diamond mines in the region of
94.x: Marco Polo referred to the diamond mines of the Golconda region while describing the area and its trade.
94.tq: Distinguish the mining region from the port and inland centres.
94.sec: Marco Polo on Motupalli - goods and trade, Rudrama's reign

94.s: Which of the following crops was associated with the agricultural economy of the Kakatiya period?
o: Maize as a regular medieval crop
94.x: Betel was among the crops listed, along with rice, wheat, sorghum, sugarcane, oilseeds, sesame, cotton, ginger and horse gram. Maize is excluded because it reached India only after 1500.
94.tq: Reject an anachronistic crop and select one from the stated crop list.
94.sec: Agriculture - wet and dry cultivation, crops, tank cesses

94.s: Which of the following sets contains only crops and fruit mentioned in connection with Kakatiya agriculture?
94.x: Rice, sugarcane, cotton and coconut were all listed. Maize was specifically excluded from the medieval crop list, and tea, coffee and tobacco were not included.
94.tq: Check every item against the stated crop and fruit inventory.
94.sec: Agriculture - wet and dry cultivation, crops, tank cesses

94.s: What was the purpose of Dashabandhamu in the Kakatiya period?
o: It was a tax on dry land cultivation.
