101.x: Nannechoda was known by the title Kavirajasekhara, also rendered as Kaviraja Shikhamani.
101.tq: Test the exact title rather than the author's literary work.
101.sec: Other poets and scholars - work, patron, title  [APPSC]

101.s: Nannechoda is associated with which of the following works?
101.x: Nannechoda composed Kumara Sambhava, which is noted for Kannada influence and for beginning the eight descriptions of the prabandha tradition.
101.tq: Use the work–author pair while separating Nannechoda from other medieval poets.
101.sec: Other poets and scholars - work, patron, title  [APPSC]

101.s:
Which of the following statements regarding Ketana is correct?
1. He was also known as Mula Ghatika.
2. He dedicated his work to Tikkana.
3. He was the first to use the words ‘Tenugu’ and ‘Telugu’.
101.x: All three statements are correct. Ketana, known as Mula Ghatika, dedicated his work to Tikkana and is credited with the early use of the words Tenugu and Telugu.
101.tq: Verify biographical title, literary association and linguistic contribution together.
101.sec: Other poets and scholars - work, patron, title  [APPSC]

101.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
101.x: Ketana wrote Andhra Bhasha Bhushanam. Marana wrote Markandeya Puranam, Pavuluri Mallana wrote Ganita Sarasangraha, and Nitisaramukhavali is associated with Baddena.
101.tq: Identify the correct author–work pair by eliminating cross-paired names.
101.sec: Other poets and scholars - work, patron, title  [APPSC]

101.s: Andhra Bhasha Bhushanam is notable as:
o: The first Telugu Purana describing Basava's life
The first Telugu Ramayana in dwipada form
The first Telugu grammar, consisting of 196 padyas
101.x: Andhra Bhasha Bhushanam, written by Ketana, is described as the first Telugu grammar and contains 196 padyas.
101.tq: Use the distinctive numerical feature to separate related literary works.
101.sec: Other poets and scholars - work, patron, title  [APPSC]

101.s: Dashakumara Charitra of Ketana is significant because it is:
o: The first Telugu Purana, derived from Basava's life
A Sanskrit treatise on dance with eight prakaranas
The first Telugu Ramayana in dwipada metre
The first Telugu prose-story kavya, derived from Dandin's Sanskrit work
101.x: Ketana's Dashakumara Charitra is regarded as the first Telugu prose-story kavya and is based on Dandin's Sanskrit work.
101.tq: Combine the work's form, priority and source to identify the precise option.
101.sec: Other poets and scholars - work, patron, title  [APPSC]

101.s: Which one of the following was written by Marana?
101.x: Marana, a disciple of Tikkana, wrote Markandeya Puranam and belonged to the Kakatiya period.
101.tq: Use the disciple–work association to distinguish Marana from Tikkana and Ketana.
101.sec: Other poets and scholars - work, patron, title  [APPSC]

101.s:
Arrange the following in the order in which the associated works are traditionally described as firsts in Telugu literature, beginning with the earliest stated literary category:
A. Basava Puranam — first Telugu Purana
B. Markandeya Puranam — first Purana in the cited firsts list
C. Ranganatha Ramayanam — first Telugu Ramayana
D. Andhra Bhasha Bhushanam — first Telugu grammar
101.x: The stated sequence of literary distinctions is Basava Puranam, Markandeya Puranam, Ranganatha Ramayanam and Andhra Bhasha Bhushanam. The sequence follows the order in which these firsts are presented in the literary tradition summarized here.
101.tq: Track the sequence of the stated literary ‘firsts’ and compare the middle items carefully.

101.s: Which of the following correctly describes Panditaradhya Charitra?
o: A work on statecraft written by Rudradeva
A mathematical treatise translated from Mahaviracharya
A Sanskrit dance treatise with eight prakaranas
A work on the life of Mallikarjuna Panditaradhya, regarded as the first Telugu encyclopedia
101.x: Panditaradhya Charitra, by Palkuriki Somanatha, narrates the life of Mallikarjuna Panditaradhya and is described as the first Telugu encyclopedia.
101.tq: Use the subject and literary classification of the work to reject neighbouring options.

101.s: Which statement about Basava Puranam is correct?
o: It was composed by Vidyanatha as a Sanskrit alankara work.
It is associated with Palkuriki Somanatha and is described as the first Telugu Purana.
It was composed by Jayapa Senani as a dance treatise.
It was written by Nannechoda and began the eight descriptions of prabandha.
101.x: Basava Puranam was composed by Palkuriki Somanatha, is in dwipada form, deals with the life of Basava and is described as the first Telugu Purana.
101.tq: Combine author, genre, metre and subject to identify the precise literary description.

101.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
101.x: Nitisaramukhavali was written by Baddena, not Agastya. Agastya is associated with Bala Bharatamu and Saugandhikaharanamu.
101.tq: Look for the author–work swap among poets whose works are all from the same broad period.
101.sec: Other poets and scholars - work, patron, title  [APPSC]

101.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with its literary description?
o: Ranganatha Ramayanam — first Telugu Ramayana and first dwipada kavya
101.x: Ranganatha Ramayanam, by Gona Budda Reddy, is described as the first Telugu Ramayana and the first dwipada kavya.
101.tq: Compare the distinctive ‘first’ associated with each work rather than only its title.

101.s: Nirvachanottara Ramayanam was the first work of which poet and was dedicated to whom?
101.x: Nirvachanottara Ramayanam was Tikkana's first work and was dedicated to Manumasiddhi.
101.tq: Test two linked details—author and dedicatee—to avoid confusing different Ramayana traditions.

101.s:
Which of the following statements regarding Ketana's works is correct?
1. Dashakumara Charitra was derived from Dandin's Sanskrit work.
2. Andhra Bhasha Bhushanam is associated with Telugu grammar.
3. Vijnaneswariyam is connected with the Mitakshara tradition.
101.x: All three statements are correct. Ketana is associated with Dashakumara Charitra, Andhra Bhasha Bhushanam and Vijnaneswariyam, the Telugu rendering connected with the Mitakshara.
101.tq: Group the three works under their separate literary functions and check all statements.
101.sec: Other poets and scholars - work, patron, title  [APPSC]

101.s: Which one of the following scholars is correctly associated with a work on statecraft?
101.x: Nitisara, a work on polity or statecraft, is associated with Rudradeva of the Kakatiya dynasty.
101.tq: Ask who would be responsible for the subject of polity and distinguish the ruler from literary specialists.

101.s: Srinatha, who served as a bridge between the Kavitraya and the Prabandha age, was honoured with which title?
101.x: Srinatha was titled Kavi Sarvabhauma and is regarded as the bridge between the Kavitraya and the Prabandha age.
101.tq: Directly identify the title associated with the poet.

101.s: Who was the principal patron of Srinatha?
101.x: Pedakomati Vema Reddi was the main patron of Srinatha. Kataya Vema is specifically associated with the request for Kashikhandam.
101.tq: Use the patron–poet association and distinguish it from a work-specific patron.

101.s: Which one of the following works of Srinatha is based on Sriharsha’s Naishadhiyacharita and deals with the story of Nala and Damayanti?
101.x: Sringara Naishadham is derived from Sriharsha’s Naishadhiyacharita, which narrates the story of Nala and Damayanti.
101.tq: Match the work with its literary source and subject.

101.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the works of Srinatha:
1. Haravilasam was dedicated to the merchant Tippayya Setti.
2. Haravilasam describes sea trade.
3. Kashikhandam deals with Kashi and Shiva.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
101.x: All three statements are correct. Haravilasam was dedicated to Tippayya Setti and describes sea trade, while Kashikhandam concerns Kashi and Shiva.
101.tq: Combine several work-specific details and eliminate options that omit one correct statement.

101.s: Kashikhandam is said to have been written at the request of which patron?
101.x: Kashikhandam is linked with Kataya Vema’s request. Tippayya Setti was associated with Haravilasam.
101.tq: Discriminate between a general patron and a work-specific patron.

101.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

1. Bhimakhandam — Bhimeswara of Draksharama
2. Palnati Veera Charitra — Battle of Palnadu
3. Haravilasam — Description of sea trade
4. Sringara Naishadham — Story of Kashi and Shiva
101.x: The first three pairs are correct. Sringara Naishadham concerns Nala and Damayanti, whereas Kashi and Shiva are associated with Kashikhandam.
101.tq: Find the single swapped subject among closely related literary works.

101.s: The Battle of Palnadu and musical instruments such as Sannai and Mukha Veena are mentioned in which work?
101.x: Srinatha’s Palnati Veera Charitra describes the Battle of Palnadu and mentions instruments including Sannai and Mukha Veena.
101.tq: Link a literary work with its historical subject and distinctive detail.

101.s: Which one of the following is NOT a work of Srinatha?
101.x: Veerabhadra Vijayam was composed by Bammera Potana, not Srinatha. The other three works are associated with Srinatha.
101.tq: Use the wrong-author trap to identify the exception.

101.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Composer)

a. Pampa
b. Kamban
c. Sarala Dasa
 d. Kasirama Das

List-II (Epic version and language)
 i. Mahabharata — Bengali
 ii. Ramavataram — Tamil
 iii. Vikramarjuna Vijaya — Kannada
 iv. Mahabharata — Odia

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
101.x: Pampa composed Vikramarjuna Vijaya in Kannada, Kamban composed Ramavataram in Tamil, Sarala Dasa composed the Mahabharata in Odia, and Kasirama Das composed the Mahabharata in Bengali.
101.tq: Start from the sure composer–language pair and complete the remaining matches.
101.sec: Epic versions in other Indian languages - composer + language

101.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
101.x: Sarala Dasa composed a version of the Mahabharata in Odia. Pampa is associated with Kannada, Kamban with Tamil, and Kasirama Das with Bengali.
101.tq: Discriminate among similar epic titles by checking both composer and language.
101.sec: Epic versions in other Indian languages - composer + language

101.s: Tikkana’s contribution to the Andhra Mahabharatam comprises how many parvas?
101.x: Tikkana’s Andhra Mahabharatam covered 15 parvas.
101.tq: Test the exact numerical extent of a literary contribution.
101.sec: Epic versions in other Indian languages - composer + language

101.s: The Kalamalla inscription, regarded as the earliest Telugu inscription, belongs to which dynasty?
101.x: The Kalamalla inscription of about 575 CE is associated with the Renati Chola ruler Erikal Mutturaju Dhananjaya.
101.tq: Identify the dynasty linked with the earliest inscription.

101.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Kalamalla inscription is located in Kadapa.
2. It is dated approximately to 575 CE.
3. It is a prose inscription.
4. It was issued by Dhanunjaya Varma of the Renati Cholas.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
101.x: All four statements are correct. Kalamalla is a Kadapa inscription of about 575 CE, associated with Dhanunjaya Varma of the Renati Cholas and written in prose.
101.tq: Check location, date, issuer and form as separate factual components.

101.s: Which inscription is regarded as the first fully available Telugu inscription and is written in a song or geya style?
101.x: The Erragudipadu inscription of Punyakumara of the Renati Cholas is regarded as the first fully available Telugu inscription and uses a song or geya style.
101.tq: Distinguish between the earliest inscription and the first fully available inscription.

101.s: The Addanki inscription is associated with which of the following?
o: Jayasimha Vallabha I and complete prose
Yuddhamalla II and the Madhyakkara metre
Pandaranga, commander of Gunaga Vijayaditya, and the Taruvoja metre
101.x: The Addanki inscription was issued by Panduranga, the commander of Eastern Chalukya ruler Gunaga Vijayaditya, and is the first Telugu poetic inscription in the Taruvoja metre.
101.tq: Match the inscription with its issuer, significance and metre.

101.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Inscription)

a. Addanki
b. Bezawada
c. Sataluru
 d. Kandukur and Dharmavaram

List-II (Metre or significance)
 i. Seesa and Ataveladi verses
 ii. First Telugu poetic inscription; Taruvoja metre
 iii. Champakamala verse with prasa
 iv. First Madhyakkara poem

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
101.x: Addanki is linked with Taruvoja and the first Telugu poetic inscription; Bezawada with the first Madhyakkara poem; Sataluru with Champakamala and prasa; and Kandukur–Dharmavaram with Seesa and Ataveladi.
101.tq: Begin with the distinctive first-poem associations and then match the metres.

101.s: Which one of the following inscriptions is associated with Yuddhamalla II and is regarded as the first Madhyakkara poem?
101.x: The Bezawada inscription of Yuddhamalla II is regarded as the first Madhyakkara poem and is associated with the Nagamalleswara temple.
101.tq: Identify the inscription from its ruler and literary distinction.

101.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Lakshmipuram — Jayasimha I — first complete early Telugu prose inscription
Chejarla — Kubja Vishnuvardhana — more than 50 per cent Telugu words
Vipparla — Jayasimha Vallabha I — first complete early Telugu text
Pitikayagulla — Gunaga Vijayaditya — first Telugu poetic inscription
101.x: Pitikayagulla is associated with the eighth century and post-Badami Chalukya influence, particularly in relation to early Telugu script; it is not the first Telugu poetic inscription. That distinction belongs to Addanki.
101.tq: Spot the wrong issuer–inscription–significance combination.

101.s: The Chebrolu inscription is significant because it shows which of the following?
o: The transition from Sanskrit to Tamil exclusively
The first use of the Madhyakkara metre
101.x: The Chebrolu inscription is noted for showing the Marga and Desi forms.
101.tq: Identify the distinctive linguistic feature associated with an inscription.

101.s: Which work is regarded as the first Telugu grammar written in Telugu and contains 196 padyas?
101.x: Andhra Bhasha Bhushanam by Ketana is regarded as the first grammar written in Telugu and contains 196 padyas.
101.tq: Distinguish a work by combining its title, authorial field and numerical detail.
101.sec: Early Telugu grammar and prosody - author

101.s: Who authored Kavijanasrayam, regarded as the first Telugu work on prosody?
101.x: Kavijanasrayam, the first Telugu work on prosody, was authored by Malliya Rechana.
101.tq: Match the specialised literary subject with its author.
101.sec: Early Telugu grammar and prosody - author

101.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Work)

a. Andhra Shabda Chintamani
b. Kavi Vakbandham
c. Kavyalankara Chudamani
 d. Appakaviyam

List-II (Author)
 i. Kakunuri Appakavi
 ii. Nannaya
 iii. Tikkana
 iv. Vinnakota Peddana

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
101.x: Andhra Shabda Chintamani is traditionally ascribed to Nannaya; Kavi Vakbandham is by Tikkana; Kavyalankara Chudamani is by Vinnakota Peddana; and Appakaviyam is by Kakunuri Appakavi.
101.tq: Use author–work associations, especially the distinction between grammar, prosody and poetics.
101.sec: Early Telugu grammar and prosody - author

101.s:
Which of the following statements regarding early Telugu grammar and literary theory are correct?
1. Andhra Shabda Chintamani was written in Sanskrit and is traditionally ascribed to Nannaya.
2. Ketana was the first to use the words Tenugu and Telugu.
3. Kavyalankara Chudamani is regarded as the first alankara work.
4. Appakaviyam belongs to the seventeenth century.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
101.x: All four statements are correct. Andhra Shabda Chintamani is traditionally attributed to Nannaya, Ketana used Tenugu/Telugu, Kavyalankara Chudamani is regarded as the first alankara work, and Appakaviyam belongs to the seventeenth century.
101.tq: Verify each statement independently across grammar, terminology, alankara and chronology.
101.sec: Early Telugu grammar and prosody - author

101.s: Which one of the following metres was used by Palkuriki Somanatha in the composition of Basava Puranam?
101.x: Basava Puranam was composed in the dwipada metre. Palkuriki Somanatha popularised this and other native Telugu metres.
101.tq: Identify the exact metre associated with the work rather than the broader literary movement.

101.s:
Palkuriki Somanatha is associated with which of the following combinations?
1. Prathama Andhra Viplava Kavi
2. Veerashaiva tradition
3. Palakurthi in Janagama district
4. Exclusive use of the Sanskritised marga style
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
101.x: Somanatha was hailed as Prathama Andhra Viplava Kavi, belonged to the Veerashaiva tradition and was a native of Palakurthi in Janagama district. He opposed the heavily Sanskritised marga style by popularising desi metres, so statement 4 is false.
101.tq: Find the one reversed or extreme statement in a biographical description.

101.s: Which of the following works is associated with Palkuriki Somanatha rather than with Mallikarjuna Panditaradhya?
101.x: Basavodaharanam is listed among Palkuriki Somanatha's Telugu works. Sivatattvasaram was composed by Mallikarjuna Panditaradhya.
101.tq: Separate closely associated authors by eliminating the work belonging to the other writer.

101.s:
Palkuriki Somanatha's writings are particularly significant for recording which of the following?
1. Brahmin–Veerashaiva conflict
2. Daily life of common people
3. Exclusive courtly life of Sanskrit scholars
Select the correct answer.
101.x: His texts record the Brahmin–Veerashaiva conflict and the daily life of commoners. They are not described as records of an exclusively courtly scholarly life.
101.tq: Reject the exaggerated exclusive claim and retain the two supported social themes.

101.s: Mallikarjuna Panditaradhya is associated with which one of the following descriptions?
o: First prabandha writer and author of Nrusimha Puranam
Author of Sugriva Vijayam and pioneer of Yakshagana
Author of Raghavapandaviyam and pioneer of dvyarthi kavya
Originator of the Sataka form and author of Sivatattvasaram
101.x: Mallikarjuna Panditaradhya wrote Sivatattvasaram, consisting of about 400 kanda poems, and is regarded as the originator of the Sataka form.
101.tq: Match a literary personality with both the distinctive work and epithet associated with him.

101.s: Sivatattvasaram of Mallikarjuna Panditaradhya consists of approximately how many kanda poems?
101.x: Sivatattvasaram is described as containing about 400 kanda poems.
101.tq: Test the quantitative detail directly with nearby numerical distractors.

101.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
101.x: Ranganatha Ramayanam is identified as the earliest dwipada kavya. Sugriva Vijayam is associated with Yakshagana, Raghavapandaviyam with dvyarthi kavya, and Dasakumara Charitra with story kavya.
101.tq: Start from the sure genre–work pair and eliminate the swapped literary forms.

101.s:
With reference to early Telugu literary genres, consider the following statements:
1. Nannaya's Bharatam is in champu form.
2. Errana was the first prabandha writer.
3. Nannechoda began the tradition of the eight descriptions.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
101.x: All three statements are correct. Nannaya's Bharatam uses verse and prose in champu form; Errana is identified as the first prabandha writer, while Nannechoda began the eight descriptions.
101.tq: Use a three-statement combination to distinguish genre, author and literary development.

101.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
101.x: Nrusimha Puranam is identified as a Purana, not as a Kshetra-mahatmya. Dasakumara Charitra is story kavya, Raghavapandaviyam is dvyarthi kavya, and Markandeya Puranam is a Purana.
101.tq: Find the single genre substitution among several familiar author–work classifications.

101.s: Who composed Sugriva Vijayam, regarded as an early example of Telugu Yakshagana?
101.x: Sugriva Vijayam is associated with Kandukuri Rudrakavi and is identified as an early Yakshagana work.
101.tq: Test the author–genre association directly.

101.s: Raghavapandaviyam is notable because it presents which two narratives simultaneously?
o: The Basava tradition and the Ramayana
101.x: Pingali Surana's Raghavapandaviyam is a dvyarthi kavya that conveys the Ramayana and the Mahabharata at the same time.
101.tq: Distinguish a rare literary form by identifying its two simultaneous narrative themes.

101.s:
Arrange the following works according to the literary forms with which they are associated, selecting the correctly matched sequence:
A. Dasakumara Charitra
B. Markandeya Puranam
C. Nrusimha Puranam
D. Raghavapandaviyam
Which of the following is correct?
o: Story kavya, Purana, Kshetra-mahatmya, Dvyarthi kavya
Purana, Story kavya, Dvyarthi kavya, Kshetra-mahatmya
Kshetra-mahatmya, Dvyarthi kavya, Story kavya, Purana
Dvyarthi kavya, Kshetra-mahatmya, Purana, Story kavya
101.x: Dasakumara Charitra is a story kavya, Markandeya Puranam is a Purana, Nrusimha Puranam is a Kshetra-mahatmya, and Raghavapandaviyam is a dvyarthi kavya.
101.tq: Map each item to its literary category before selecting the complete combination.

101.s: Which of the following statements regarding the Desi and Marga literary traditions is correct?
o: The Marga style was based entirely on the speech of commoners.
The Bhakti poets introduced native Telugu idiom in opposition to a heavily Sanskritised style.
The Desi movement aimed to replace Telugu with Sanskrit.
The Desi tradition exclusively rejected all metres used in Telugu.
101.x: The Bhakti poets brought a native Telugu idiom into literature in opposition to the heavily Sanskritised marga style. The other statements reverse or exaggerate the relationship between the two traditions.
101.tq: Apply the Desi–Marga distinction to identify the correctly stated literary tendency.

101.s: The Nandampudi agrahara associated with Rajaraja Narendra is connected with which person in the context of the translation of the Mahabharata?
101.x: The Nandampudi donation is associated with Narayana Bhattu, who assisted Nannaya in the translation. The inscription is treated as evidence of his assistance.
101.tq: Distinguish the two agraharas by first identifying their recipients.
101.sec: Grants to poets and scholars → recipient; assistant in the translation

101.s: Which grant–recipient pair is correctly matched?
101.x: Nandampudi agrahara was associated with Narayana Bhattu, while Navakhandavada agrahara was granted to Pavuluri Mallana.
101.tq: Start with the grant–recipient pair and use the two similar agrahara names as the trap.
101.sec: Grants to poets and scholars → recipient; assistant in the translation

101.s: The evidence for Narayana Bhattu's assistance to Nannaya in translating the Mahabharata is provided by which source?
101.x: The Nandampudi donation inscription is cited as evidence of Narayana Bhattu's assistance in the translation. The other inscriptions belong to the evidence for pre-Nannaya Telugu.
101.tq: Separate inscriptional evidence for a literary collaboration from inscriptions used for language history.
101.sec: Grants to poets and scholars → recipient; assistant in the translation

101.s:
Narayana Bhattu was known by which of the following descriptions?
1. He knew eight languages.
2. He bore the title Ashtabhasha Kavisekhara.
3. Someshwara I of Kalyani appointed him as his representative at Rajamahendravaram.
Select the correct answer.
101.x: All three statements are correct. Narayana Bhattu was a polyglot familiar with eight languages, held the title Ashtabhasha Kavisekhara, and represented Someshwara I at Rajamahendravaram.
101.tq: Combine ability, title and political role to test the complete profile of one scholar.
101.sec: Grants to poets and scholars → recipient; assistant in the translation

101.s: Which of the following was NOT a title associated with Narayana Bhattu?
101.x: Prathama Andhra Viplava Kavi was an epithet of Palkuriki Somanatha. Kaviraja Shekhara, Karibha Vajrankudu and Vangmaya Durandharudu were titles associated with Narayana Bhattu.
101.tq: Use the author–epithet trap by separating titles belonging to two Veerasaiva-era figures.
101.sec: Grants to poets and scholars → recipient; assistant in the translation

101.s: Which one of the following statements about Pavuluri Mallana is correct?
o: He wrote Basava Puranam in the dwipada metre.
He composed Raghavapandaviyam under the patronage of Pingali Surana.
He translated Mahaviracharya's Sanskrit Ganita Sara Sangraha into Telugu verse as Sara Sangraha Ganitam.
He translated a Telugu mathematical work into Sanskrit prose as Sivatattvasaram.
101.x: Pavuluri Mallana rendered Mahaviracharya's Sanskrit Ganita Sara Sangraha into Telugu verse as Sara Sangraha Ganitam, also called Pavuluri Ganitam.
101.tq: Match the mathematician with the source text and Telugu title rather than with unrelated literary works.
101.sec: Early Telugu mathematical work → author + patron court

101.s:
Sara Sangraha Ganitam is significant in Telugu literary history as which of the following?
1. The first mathematics book in Telugu
2. The first scientific kavya in Telugu
3. A translation of Mahaviracharya's Sanskrit work
Select the correct answer.
101.x: All three statements are correct. Sara Sangraha Ganitam is described as the first Telugu mathematics book and scientific kavya, and it derives from Mahaviracharya's Sanskrit Ganita Sara Sangraha.
101.tq: Test significance, genre and source together in a three-statement format.
101.sec: Early Telugu mathematical work → author + patron court

101.s: Pavuluri Mallana is associated with which approximate date and patronage combination?
o: 1300 CE and the court of Prataparudra II
800 CE and the court of Someshwara I
1000 CE and the court of Rajaraja Narendra
1100 CE and an agrahara granted by Rajaraja Narendra
101.x: Pavuluri Mallana is dated to approximately 1100 CE, and his agrahara, Navakhandavada, was granted by Rajaraja Narendra.
101.tq: Combine the approximate date with patronage to avoid confusing neighbouring rulers and periods.
101.sec: Early Telugu mathematical work → author + patron court

101.s: Which statement correctly describes the position of Sanskrit and Telugu in the Eastern Chalukya period referred to here?
o: Telugu was the official language and Sanskrit was used only for private correspondence.
Sanskrit was the official language, while Telugu was the people's and favoured language.
Kannada replaced both Sanskrit and Telugu as the official language.
Both languages were prohibited in inscriptions.
101.x: Sanskrit was the official language, whereas Telugu was the language of the people and the favoured language. Nannaya's work subsequently helped Telugu become a language of high literature.
101.tq: Keep official status separate from popular and literary preference.

101.s: In the bilingual inscriptions described for this period, which language was generally used for the eulogy and which for the grant details?
o: Telugu for both the eulogy and grant details
Sanskrit for the eulogy and Telugu for the grant details
Sanskrit for both the eulogy and grant details
Telugu for the eulogy and Sanskrit for the grant details
101.x: The eulogy was written in Sanskrit, while the details of the grant were written in Telugu. This illustrates the simultaneous official and popular roles of the two languages.
101.tq: Test the functional division between two languages within the same inscription.

101.s:
Which of the following provides epigraphic evidence for the existence of written Telugu before Nannaya?
1. Renati Chola prose inscription at Kalamalla
2. Chalukya prose inscription at Vipparla
3. Poetic inscriptions at Addanki and Bezawada
Select the correct answer.
101.x: All the listed sources provide evidence: Renati Chola prose at Kalamalla, Chalukya prose at Vipparla, and poetic inscriptions at Addanki and Bezawada. Together they show that written Telugu verse existed before the Mahabharata of Nannaya.
101.tq: Recognise that several inscriptional sources, rather than a surviving literary book, support the conclusion.
101.sec: Pre-Nannaya Telugu literature debate - claims and evidence

101.s: The Renati Chola prose inscription at Kalamalla is dated to which year?
101.x: The Renati Chola prose inscription at Kalamalla is dated to 575 CE and is important evidence of early written Telugu.
101.tq: Test the precise epigraphic date using closely spaced century options.
101.sec: Pre-Nannaya Telugu literature debate - claims and evidence

101.s: Which conclusion is most appropriate regarding pre-Nannaya Telugu literature?
o: Epigraphic evidence proves that no Telugu existed before Nannaya.
Only oral Telugu existed before Nannaya, with no written form.
Inscriptions show the existence of written Telugu, but no pre-Nannaya literary text survives in the available evidence.
A complete pre-Nannaya literary text has survived in the available evidence.
101.x: The inscriptions demonstrate that written Telugu, including Telugu verse, existed before Nannaya; however, no pre-Nannaya literary text survives in the evidence described.
101.tq: Distinguish evidence for an earlier written language from the survival of a complete literary text.
101.sec: Pre-Nannaya Telugu literature debate - claims and evidence

101.s: The statement that Nannaya relied on a written form of Telugu tested through approximately five centuries of inscriptions implies which of the following?
o: Nannaya created Telugu writing without any earlier tradition.
All inscriptions before Nannaya were written only in Sanskrit.
Nannaya's literary achievement rested on an already developing written linguistic tradition.
Telugu literary language began only after the fourteenth century.
101.x: The statement indicates that Nannaya built on a written Telugu tradition evidenced by about five centuries of inscriptions, rather than creating written Telugu without precedent.
101.tq: Infer the historical implication of cumulative inscriptional evidence without overstating the conclusion.
101.sec: Pre-Nannaya Telugu literature debate - claims and evidence

101.s: Who coined the epithet “Italian of the East” for Telugu?
101.x: The Venetian traveller Niccolo de' Conti, who visited in the fifteenth century, is associated with the epithet “Italian of the East” for Telugu.
101.tq: Match the famous epithet with the traveller who coined it.

101.s: The expression “Desa bhashalandu Telugu lessa” is associated with which person and work?
o: Niccolo de' Conti — a travel account
101.x: Sri Krishnadevaraya used the expression “Desa bhashalandu Telugu lessa” in Amuktamalyada, meaning that Telugu is the finest among regional languages.
101.tq: Use the author–work–quotation triad to distinguish two famous statements about Telugu.

101.s: The epithet “Italian of the East” is linked to which characteristic of Telugu?
o: Its rounded, vowel-ending and highly phonetic character
Its exclusive use in royal courts
Its use only in inscriptional prose
Its derivation exclusively from Sanskrit vocabulary
101.x: The epithet is linked to the rounded, vowel-ending and highly phonetic character of Telugu. It does not indicate that the language was restricted to courts or inscriptions.
101.tq: Connect a descriptive epithet with the linguistic feature it is intended to convey.

101.s: Who identified the word ‘Nagabu’ in the Amaravati inscription?
101.x: Veturi Prabhakara Sastri identified ‘Nagabu’ as the first Telugu word in the Amaravati inscription.
101.tq: Test the scholar associated with a specific epigraphic identification.
101.sec: Earliest Telugu words in Prakrit records → site  [GROUP-II]

101.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
101.x: ‘Vepuru’ appears in the Myakadoni inscription. ‘Andhrapatha’ belongs to the Mayidavolu plates, ‘Nagabu’ to Amaravati, and ‘-ambul’ to Vishnukundin plates.
101.tq: Start from the sure inscription–word pair and eliminate swapped locations.
101.sec: Earliest Telugu words in Prakrit records → site  [GROUP-II]

101.s: Which of the following words is NOT listed among the Telugu words occurring in Hala’s Gatha Saptasati?
101.x: The listed words include atta, addam, potta, tuppu, padi, pandi and pilla. Vepuru belongs to the Myakadoni inscription.
101.tq: Find the odd item by separating literary evidence from inscriptional evidence.
101.sec: Earliest Telugu words in Prakrit records → site  [GROUP-II]

101.s: The Telugu plural suffix ‘-ambul’ is found in the:
101.x: The Vishnukundin Chikkulla plates use the Telugu plural suffix ‘-ambul’, as in ‘Vijayarajya Samvatsarambul’.
101.tq: Test the exact grammatical form against its inscriptional source.
101.sec: Earliest Telugu words in Prakrit records → site  [GROUP-II]

101.s: ‘Andhrapatha’ was first recorded in the:
101.x: ‘Andhrapatha’ is first recorded in the Mayidavolu plates of Pallava Sivaskandavarman, written in Prakrit around 300 CE.
101.tq: Link the distinctive term with its earliest recorded source.
101.sec: Earliest Telugu words in Prakrit records → site  [GROUP-II]

101.s:
Consider the following statements about the development of Telugu script:
1. Brahmi is the source of the Telugu script.
2. Satavahana inscriptions were written in Prakrit using Brahmi script.
3. Telugu and Kannada began to differentiate during the Rashtrakuta–Eastern Chalukya age.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
101.x: All three statements are correct. Telugu script developed from Brahmi; Satavahana inscriptions used Prakrit and Brahmi; and differentiation from Kannada began during the Rashtrakuta–Eastern Chalukya age.
101.tq: Combine source, language and script-development statements before selecting the coded option.
101.sec: Telugu script evolution - stages from Brahmi  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

101.s: The Bhattiprolu stupa inscriptions are best described as:
o: Sanskrit inscriptions in the common Old Kannada script
Tamil inscriptions in the Grantha script
Prakrit inscriptions in a variant of Brahmi carrying early Telugu place and personal names
Telugu inscriptions in the fully developed medieval Telugu script
101.x: The Bhattiprolu inscriptions, dated approximately to 400 BCE in Guntur, use a variant of Brahmi and contain early Telugu place and personal names.
101.tq: Use the precise combination of date, place, script and linguistic evidence.
101.sec: Telugu script evolution - stages from Brahmi  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

101.s:
Arrange the following stages in the evolution of Telugu script in chronological order:
A. Separate Telugu script with rounded letters and vowel signs
B. Bhattiprolu variant of Brahmi
C. Common Old Kannada–Telugu script
D. Beginning of differentiation between Telugu and Kannada
101.x: The sequence is Bhattiprolu Brahmi variant, common Old Kannada–Telugu script, differentiation during the Rashtrakuta–Eastern Chalukya age, and separate Telugu script in the 11th–14th centuries.
101.tq: Fix the earliest script stage first and then place the transition stages.
101.sec: Telugu script evolution - stages from Brahmi  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

101.s: Which statement correctly reflects the chronology of the emergence of the distinct Telugu script?
o: It emerged only after the 14th century.
It developed directly from the Tamil script during the 4th century BCE.
It was fully distinct during the Satavahana period.
It had emerged by the 11th century, with full separation placed broadly in the 11th–14th centuries.
101.x: One account places the emergence of distinct Telugu script by the 11th century, while another describes full separation over the 11th–14th centuries.
101.tq: Reconcile close chronological formulations instead of treating them as contradictory.
101.sec: Telugu script evolution - stages from Brahmi  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

101.s: Telugu belongs to which sub-branch of the Dravidian language family?
101.x: Telugu belongs to the South-Central Dravidian sub-branch.
101.tq: Test the exact linguistic sub-classification rather than the broader family name.

101.s: Which of the following are identified as sister languages of Telugu within the South-Central Dravidian group?
101.x: Gondi and Kui are identified among the sister languages of Telugu in the South-Central Dravidian sub-branch.
101.tq: Distinguish sister languages from other Dravidian languages outside the stated sub-branch.

101.s:
Consider the following statements about Telugu:
1. It is the official language of Andhra Pradesh.
2. It is included among the 22 languages in the Eighth Schedule.
3. It belongs to the Indo-Aryan language family.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
101.x: Telugu is the official language of Andhra Pradesh and one of the 22 Eighth Schedule languages. It belongs to the Dravidian, not Indo-Aryan, family.
101.tq: Reject the broad-family trap while retaining the constitutional and state-language facts.

101.s: The theory that Telugu grew out of the Desi bhasha, identified with Paisachi of Prakrit, is associated with the view that:
o: Telugu was created by the Kakatiya court
Desi words show close resemblance to Telugu
101.x: The stated theory connects Telugu with the Desi bhasha or Paisachi of Prakrit, and D.C. Sircar observed that Desi words were very close to Telugu.
101.tq: Connect the etymological theory with the linguistic evidence cited for it.

101.s: The Trilinga theory derives the name Andhra from the three Shaiva centres of:
101.x: The Trilinga theory refers to Srisailam, Kaleshwaram and Draksharama as the three Shaiva centres of Trilinga desa.
101.tq: Use a three-place association to distinguish the Trilinga theory from other regional lists.
101.sec: Names of the language - etymology theories  [GROUP-II]

101.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Telugu — derived by all scholars exclusively from Tamil
Trilinga — associated with three Shaiva centres
Andhrika — an alternative name of the language
Tenugu — derived by some from tene, meaning honey
101.x: The material presents Telugu, Andhra, Andhrika and Tenugu as names or theories of origin; it does not support an exclusive Tamil derivation accepted by all scholars.
101.tq: Identify the overgeneralised attribution using the extreme word ‘all’.
101.sec: Names of the language - etymology theories  [GROUP-II]

101.s: Telugu was declared a Classical Language by the Government of India in:
101.x: Telugu was granted Classical Language status by the Union Government in 2008, together with Kannada.
101.tq: Use the year options to distinguish Telugu’s status from Tamil’s earlier recognition.

101.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the recognition of Classical Languages is correct?
o: The Government of Uttar Pradesh granted Classical Language status to Telugu.
Tamil was recognised in 2008, after Telugu.
Telugu and Kannada were recognised in 2008, while Tamil was the first in 2004.
Malayalam and Odia were recognised in 2008 along with Telugu.
101.x: Tamil was the first, receiving recognition in 2004. Telugu and Kannada received it in 2008; the granting authority was the Union Government, not Uttar Pradesh.
101.tq: Trap the swapped year and wrong authority in a recognition-related statement.

101.s: Which of the following correctly states the years in which Malayalam and Odia received Classical Language status?
101.x: Malayalam received Classical Language status in 2013 and Odia in 2014.
101.tq: Separate nearby recognition years instead of grouping all languages under 2008.

101.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer.
List-I (Author)
a. Vidyanatha
b. Jayapa Senani
c. Sakalya Mallabhattu
List-II (Association)
i. Named among Sanskrit authors at the Kakatiya court
ii. Prataparudra Yashobhushanam
iii. Nritta Ratnavali, Geeta Ratnavali and Vadya Ratnavali
101.x: Vidyanatha wrote Prataparudra Yashobhushanam; Jayapa Senani wrote the three Ratnavali works; Sakalya Mallabhattu is named among the Sanskrit authors.
101.tq: Start with the distinctive group of three works associated with Jayapa Senani.
101.sec: Sanskrit authors at the Kakatiya court  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

101.s: Jayapa Senani held the office of Gajasahini under Ganapatideva. The office refers to his role as:
101.x: Gajasahini means commander of the elephant corps. Jayapa Senani’s military office should not be confused with the subjects of his Ratnavali works.
101.tq: Use the occupational meaning of the title to avoid the profession trap.
101.sec: Sanskrit authors at the Kakatiya court  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

101.s: Which attribution is specifically identified as requiring caution because of differing evidence?
101.x: Ravipati Tripurantakudu is credited with the Sanskrit Niroshthya Ramayanam, but an APP fragment attributes Niroshtya Ramayana and Udara Raghavam to Takavelli Mallikarju Bhattu.
101.tq: Recognise the source-attribution dispute rather than treating similar author claims as identical.
101.sec: Sanskrit authors at the Kakatiya court  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

101.s: Tikkana’s title ‘Ubhayakavimitrudu’ is associated with his position as a poet in the court of:
101.x: Tikkana was associated with the court of Manumasiddhi II of Nellore and bore the title Ubhayakavimitrudu.
101.tq: Distinguish Tikkana’s patron from the Kakatiya rulers connected with his period.
101.sec: Tikkana - patron, parvas, independent works, philosophy  [GROUP-II]

101.s: Which of the following is an independent work of Tikkana rather than a portion of his Mahabharata translation?
101.x: Krishna Satakam is listed as an independent work of Tikkana. The other works are associated with different authors or literary contexts.
101.tq: Separate a poet’s independent work from works of nearby authors and traditions.
101.sec: Tikkana - patron, parvas, independent works, philosophy  [GROUP-II]

101.s: Tikkana’s Harihara philosophy was intended principally to:
o: Separate religious literature from royal patronage
Replace Telugu with Sanskrit in court literature
101.x: Tikkana propounded Harihara philosophy, described as Harihara Dvaitam, to reconcile Shaiva and Vaishnava traditions.
101.tq: Infer the practical religious purpose from the philosophical label.
101.sec: Tikkana - patron, parvas, independent works, philosophy  [GROUP-II]

101.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer.
List-I (Siva Kavi)
a. Mallikarjuna Panditaradhya
b. Nannechoda
c. Palkuriki Somanatha
List-II (Work or contribution)
i. Basava Puranam and Panditaradhya Charitra
ii. Sivatattvasaram
iii. Kumarasambhavam
101.x: Mallikarjuna Panditaradhya is associated with Sivatattvasaram, Nannechoda with Kumarasambhavam, and Palkuriki Somanatha with Basava Puranam and Panditaradhya Charitra.
101.tq: Match the poets through their distinctive Shaiva works.

101.s: Which one of the following statements correctly distinguishes the claims regarding the first Satakam?
o: Sivatattvasaram is identified in one source, while Vrushadhipa Satakam is identified in another.
Only Vrushadhipa Satakam is ever identified as the first Satakam.
Basava Puranam is identified by both sources as the first Satakam.
Only Sivatattvasaram is ever identified as the first Satakam.
101.x: The sources differ: one identifies Sivatattvasaram as the first Satakam, while another identifies Vrushadhipa Satakam.
101.tq: Handle a documented source variation without converting it into a false single-answer claim.

101.s: Nannechoda is associated with which of the following combinations?
o: Vrushadhipa Satakam and the title Gajasahini
Basava Puranam and the title Prabandha Parameswara
101.x: Nannechoda wrote Kumarasambhavam and bore the title Kavirajasekhara. He is also associated with eight descriptions characteristic of the prabandha tradition.
101.tq: Combine the work and title that belong to the same poet.

101.s: Kreedabhiramam is credited to Vinukonda Vallabharaya, also known as:
101.x: Kreedabhiramam is credited to Vinukonda Vallabharaya, who was also known as Vallabhamatya.
101.tq: Test the alternate name of the attributed author.

101.s: The authorship debate concerning Kreedabhiramam arises partly because it is a Telugu rendering of which Sanskrit play?
101.x: Kreedabhiramam is regarded as a Telugu rendering of Ravipati Tripurantakudu’s Sanskrit play Premabhiramam, creating an attribution issue alongside its credit to Vallabharaya.
101.tq: Separate the Telugu rendering, its Sanskrit source and the credited author.

101.s: Which of the following features is associated with the Orugallu described in Kreedabhiramam?
o: The maritime trade of Motupalli alone
Markets, nightlife and the Kakati Devi temple
Only the military fortifications of the city
101.x: Kreedabhiramam describes Orugallu, or Warangal, through its markets, nightlife and Kakati Devi temple, and calls it ‘Andhra Nagari’.
101.tq: Select the cluster of urban features actually described in the work.

101.s: Kreedabhiramam belongs to the post-Kakatiya period associated with the:
101.x: Kreedabhiramam was written in the post-Kakatiya period associated with the Reddi era.
101.tq: Use the dynastic-period clue rather than the city’s earlier Kakatiya association.

101.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
101.x: Vrushadhipa Satakam is attributed to Palkuriki Somanatha. Sumati Satakam was composed by Baddena, while Sivatattvasaram belongs to Mallikarjuna Panditaradhya.
101.tq: Use author–Satakam pairings to distinguish closely related early Telugu works.

101.s: Baddena, the author of Sumati Satakam, is also associated with the title or work:
101.x: Baddena is associated with Sumati Satakam and Nitisastra Muktavali.
101.tq: Link the author with the second work listed alongside the better-known Satakam.

101.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.

List-I (Work)
a. Manucharitra
b. Parijatapaharanam
c. Panduranga Mahatmyam
d. Vasucharitra

List-II (Author)
i. Tenali Ramakrishna
ii. Nandi Timmana
iii. Ramaraja Bhushana
iv. Allasani Peddana
101.x: Manucharitra was written by Allasani Peddana, Parijatapaharanam by Nandi Timmana, Panduranga Mahatmyam by Tenali Ramakrishna and Vasucharitra by Ramaraja Bhushana.
101.tq: Start from the sure work–author pair and eliminate codes that disturb the remaining literary associations.

101.s: Vasucharitra, composed by Ramaraja Bhushana, was dedicated to which ruler?
101.x: Ramaraja Bhushana dedicated Vasucharitra to Tirumala Raya.
101.tq: Distinguish the author of a work from its patron or dedicatee.

101.s: Who among the following wrote both Kalapurnodayam and Raghavapandaviyam?
101.x: Pingali Surana was the author of both Kalapurnodayam and Raghavapandaviyam.
101.tq: Use the paired-work method to identify the author associated with both titles.

101.s: Varadambika Parinayam, a Sanskrit work, was written by
101.x: Tirumalamba wrote the Sanskrit work Varadambika Parinayam.
101.tq: Apply language discrimination when similar court-literature names appear together.

101.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
101.x: Madhura Vijayam was written in Sanskrit by Gangadevi, not by Pingali Surana. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
101.tq: Find the swapped author by checking the work–author association rather than the literary genre alone.

101.s: Madhura Vijayam, a Sanskrit work, was composed by
101.x: Gangadevi composed Madhura Vijayam in Sanskrit.
101.tq: Separate Sanskrit court works from Telugu works with similar historical settings.

101.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.

List-I (Title)
a. Kavibrahma
b. Sambhudasa
c. Andhra Kavita Pitamaha
d. Kavisarvabhauma

List-II (Holder)
i. Allasani Peddana
ii. Srinatha
iii. Tikkana
iv. Errana
101.x: Tikkana was Kavibrahma, Errana was Sambhudasa, Allasani Peddana was Andhra Kavita Pitamaha and Srinatha was Kavisarvabhauma.
101.tq: Begin with the distinctive title–poet pair and use code elimination for the rest.

101.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
101.x: Potana held the title Sahaja Panditya. Kaviraja Sikhamani belonged to Nannechoda, Kavisarvabhauma to Srinatha and Andhra Kavita Pitamaha to Allasani Peddana.
101.tq: Use title–holder discrimination to avoid swapping famous Telugu poets.

101.s:
Which of the following statements regarding the transition to the Prabandha form is correct?
1. The epic kavya gave way to the prabandha.
2. The prabandha generally treats a single episode rather than an entire epic.
3. The prabandha is marked by elaborate descriptions and a strong shringara element.
4. The prabandha dispenses with strict metrical rules.
101.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because the prabandha follows strict metrical rules.
101.tq: Reject the statement that reverses a defining feature of the literary form.
101.sec: Prabandha age - features, first prabandha, leading poets, patronage

101.s: Who introduced the set descriptions that became characteristic of the Prabandha tradition through Kumarasambhava?
101.x: Nannechoda's Kumarasambhava introduced the set descriptions associated with the Prabandha tradition.
101.tq: Link the literary innovation directly to the poet and work rather than to the later peak period.
101.sec: Prabandha age - features, first prabandha, leading poets, patronage

101.s:
Consider the following statements about the emergence of the Prabandha style:
1. Errana is credited in one classification with being the first Prabandha writer.
2. Srinatha is described as a pioneer of the style.
3. Sringara Naishadham and Haravilasam are associated with Srinatha's pioneering role.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
101.x: All three statements are correct. Errana is credited as the first Prabandha writer in one classification, while Srinatha is identified as a pioneer through works such as Sringara Naishadham and Haravilasam.
101.tq: Retain both closely related literary attributions instead of treating them as mutually exclusive.
101.sec: Prabandha age - features, first prabandha, leading poets, patronage

101.s: The Prabandha style reached its peak in the court of
o: Devaraya II, through the Reddi poets
101.x: The Prabandha style reached its peak with the Ashtadiggajas at the court of Krishnadevaraya.
101.tq: Match a literary movement with its principal court and associated group.
101.sec: Prabandha age - features, first prabandha, leading poets, patronage

101.s:
Which of the following statements regarding patronage of the Prabandha tradition is correct?
1. The Reddi courts supported Srinatha and Errana.
2. The Vijayanagara Nayaka courts helped spread the style.
3. The style was confined exclusively to the court of Krishnadevaraya.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
101.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the Reddi courts and Vijayanagara Nayaka courts also supported or spread the Prabandha style.
101.tq: Watch for the extreme word ‘exclusively’ in a statement about literary patronage.
101.sec: Prabandha age - features, first prabandha, leading poets, patronage

101.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.

List-I (Sanskrit work and Telugu rendering)
a. Harivamsa
b. Markandeya Puranam
c. Naishadham
d. Dasakumara Charitra

List-II (Translator or Telugu author)
i. Ketana
ii. Srinatha
iii. Errana
iv. Marana
101.x: Errana translated Harivamsa, Marana translated Markandeya Puranam, Srinatha rendered Naishadham as Sringara Naishadham and Ketana translated Dasakumara Charitra.
101.tq: Start with the distinctive translation pair and eliminate codes containing swapped translators.
101.sec: Sanskrit works translated into Telugu - translator

101.s: Who translated Harivamsa into Telugu and dedicated it to Prolaya Vema?
101.x: Errana translated Harivamsa and dedicated it to Prolaya Vema.
101.tq: Separate the translator of a main text from the author of its Uttara section.
101.sec: Sanskrit works translated into Telugu - translator

101.s: Which of the following is correctly matched?
101.x: Uttara Harivamsa was written by Nachana Somana. Markandeya Puranam is associated with Marana, Naishadham with Srinatha and Dasakumara Charitra with Ketana.
101.tq: Discriminate between closely related texts belonging to the same translation tradition.
101.sec: Sanskrit works translated into Telugu - translator

101.s: Marana, who translated Markandeya Puranam into Telugu, was a disciple of
101.x: Marana was a disciple of Tikkana.
101.tq: Connect a translator with his literary teacher instead of confusing him with the translator's subject text.
101.sec: Sanskrit works translated into Telugu - translator

101.s: Ketana's Telugu Dasakumara Charitra was based on which Sanskrit work?
101.x: Ketana translated the Sanskrit Dasakumara Charita as Dasakumara Charitra in Telugu.
101.tq: Distinguish near-identical Sanskrit and Telugu titles rather than treating them as separate works.
101.sec: Sanskrit works translated into Telugu - translator

101.s: Manchena's Keyurabahu Charitra is associated with the Telugu rendering of
101.x: Manchena rendered Viddhasalabhanjika as Keyurabahu Charitra in Telugu.
101.tq: Use the source-work to target-work association to distinguish similar classical titles.
101.sec: Sanskrit works translated into Telugu - translator

101.s:
Arrange the following periods of Telugu literature in chronological order:
A. Nannaya age
B. Tikkana age
C. Srinatha age
D. Prabandha or Rayala age
101.x: The Nannaya age belongs to the 11th century, followed by the Tikkana age in the 13th century, the Srinatha age in the 15th century and the Prabandha or Rayala age in the 16th century.
101.tq: Place the periods by their century markers, then verify the sequence from earliest to latest.

101.s: The Shiva Kavi Yugam in Telugu literary periodisation is generally assigned to
101.x: The Shiva Kavi Yugam is assigned to the period from 1060 to 1260.
101.tq: Use the stated range directly and reject adjacent-looking chronological intervals.

101.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with its period of Telugu literature?
1. Nannaya age — 11th century
2. Tikkana age — 13th century
3. Errana age — 14th century
4. Srinatha age — 15th century
101.x: All four pairs are correctly matched: Nannaya belongs to the 11th century, Tikkana to the 13th, Errana to the 14th and Srinatha to the 15th century.
101.tq: Check each century independently before selecting the coded combination.

101.s: Which one of the following represents the correct sequence after the Srinatha age in Telugu literary periodisation?
o: Prabandha age, Dakshinatya age, Modern age
Dakshinatya age, Prabandha age, Modern age
Modern age, Prabandha age, Dakshinatya age
Prabandha age, Modern age, Dakshinatya age
101.x: The Srinatha age is followed by the Prabandha or Rayala age in the 16th century, the Dakshinatya or southern Nayaka age in the 17th–18th centuries and the Modern age from the 19th century onward.
101.tq: Follow the period labels and their century ranges from early modern to modern literature.

101.s:
Which of the following statements about the periodisation of Telugu literature is correct?
1. The Pre-Nannaya period extends approximately up to 1000.
2. The Modern age begins in the 19th century and continues thereafter.
3. All the boundaries of the periods are precise and uniformly fixed.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
101.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because boundaries other than the specifically marked ones are approximate.
101.tq: Identify the qualification that limits an otherwise broad periodisation scheme.

101.s: Which of the following is the correct association of a title, its holder and the literary basis of the title?
101.x: Ketana was called Abhinava Dandi for his Telugu Dasakumara Charitra. The other options swap the holders of the titles.
101.tq: Verify all three elements of a composite association instead of relying on the title alone.

101.s: The Telugu Mahabharata was completed over which of the following three historical eras?
o: Eastern Chalukya, Kakatiya and Reddi eras
Vijayanagara, Qutb Shahi and Asaf Jahi eras
101.x: The Telugu Mahabharata was completed over three successive eras: the Eastern Chalukya, Kakatiya and Reddi periods.
101.tq: Use the dynasty sequence to identify the correct historical span.

101.s: Which one of the following best explains the significance of Nannaya's contribution to Telugu literature?
o: He established the desi-metre tradition during the Vijayanagara period.
He introduced Persian vocabulary into Telugu court literature.
He fixed the grammar and literary register of classical Telugu and initiated the Kavitrayam tradition.
He was the first poet to compose a Telugu satakam.
101.x: Nannaya's Bharatam helped fix the grammar and literary register of classical Telugu and began the tradition of the Kavitrayam.
101.tq: Select the option that combines the stated literary contributions without adding an unrelated claim.

101.s:
Consider the following pairs:

1. Andhra Mahabharatamu — First Telugu book
2. Andhra Shabda Chintamani — First Telugu grammar, written in Sanskrit
3. Ganita Sara Sangraha — First Telugu mathematics book

Which of the pairs given above are correct?
101.x: All three pairs are correct. Andhra Mahabharatamu is identified as the first Telugu book, Andhra Shabda Chintamani as the first Telugu grammar in Sanskrit, and Ganita Sara Sangraha as the first Telugu mathematics book.
101.tq: Check each first independently before selecting the coded combination.

101.s: Telugu Language Day is observed on 29 August because it commemorates the birth anniversary of whom?
101.x: Telugu Language Day is observed on 29 August, the birth anniversary of Gidugu Venkata Ramamurthy.
101.tq: Match the commemorative date with the associated personality.

101.s:
With reference to the Telugu Language Day observances, consider the following statements:

1. Telugu Language Day is observed on 29 August.
2. Telugu Language Awards are also associated with 29 August.
3. The date is connected with the birth anniversary of Gidugu Venkata Ramamurthy.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
101.x: All three statements are correct. Telugu Language Day and the Telugu Language Awards are associated with 29 August, the birth anniversary of Gidugu Venkata Ramamurthy.
101.tq: When all statements describe closely linked aspects of one observance, verify the date, event and person together.

101.s: From 2026, the annual Telugu Mahotsavam in Andhra Pradesh is intended to be held:
o: Once every decade under the Archaeological Survey of India
Only on Telugu Language Day in alternate years
Once every five years during the World Telugu Conference
Every year as an annual Telugu cultural event
101.x: Andhra Pradesh announced that Telugu Mahotsavam would be held every year from 2026.
101.tq: Distinguish an annual recurring programme from periodic conferences and commemorative events.

101.s: Who announced the annual Telugu Mahotsavam at the valedictory programme held at the Undavalli Caves?
o: The Director-General of the Archaeological Survey of India
101.x: Culture Minister Kandula Durgesh announced the annual Telugu Mahotsavam at the valedictory programme at the Undavalli Caves.
101.tq: Identify the office-holder associated with the announcement rather than the venue or implementing agency.

101.s: An Archaeological Survey of India survey in the Nallamala Tiger Reserve during 11–13 June 2026 copied how many inscriptions?
101.x: The ASI survey in the Nallamala Tiger Reserve copied 25 inscriptions dating from the 2nd to the 16th century CE.
101.tq: For numerical current-affairs questions, separate the exact count from the associated date and range.

101.s: The Telugu records identified during the ASI survey of the Nallamala Tiger Reserve date from which period?
101.x: The Telugu records found in the survey date from the 7th to the 16th centuries CE.
101.tq: Compare the competing chronological ranges carefully; the broader survey range and the Telugu-record range are different.

101.s: An eighth-century Telugu inscription was reported at which place?
101.x: An eighth-century Telugu inscription was reported at Pitikayagulla.
101.tq: Use location-based recall for an inscriptional discovery.

101.s:
Consider the following pairs relating to the early history of Telugu:

1. Nagabu — First Telugu word
2. Kalamalla — First Telugu inscription
3. Addanki — First poetic inscription

Which of the pairs given above are correct?
101.x: All the pairs are correctly matched: Nagabu is associated with the first Telugu word, Kalamalla with the first Telugu inscription, and Addanki with the first poetic inscription.
101.tq: Start from the sure location–fact pairs and verify all three early Telugu milestones.

101.s: Which one of the following statements correctly describes the linguistic and literary situation during the Kakatiya period?
o: Telugu grammar, poetics and the desi-metre tradition developed, although Sanskrit remained the inscriptional language.
Persian became the principal language of Kakatiya inscriptions.
Only Tamil was used for literary composition and inscriptions.
Telugu literature declined, while Sanskrit disappeared from inscriptions.
101.x: The Kakatiya era saw the development of Telugu grammar, poetics and the desi-metre tradition. Telugu literature flourished, while Sanskrit continued as the inscriptional language.
101.tq: Separate the language of literary development from the language retained in inscriptions.

101.s: Which of the following is correctly matched?
o: Andhra Bhasha Bhushanam — First Telugu Ramayana
101.x: Ranganatha Ramayanam is identified as the first Telugu Ramayana. Bhaskara Ramayanam is associated with the first Telugu champu, while Andhra Bhasha Bhushanam is associated with grammar.
101.tq: Discriminate among closely related literary firsts by matching each work with its genre or status.

101.s: Which one of the following represents the source-wise variation regarding the first Telugu Purana?
o: Andhra Mahabharatamu or Ganita Sara Sangraha
Andhra Shabda Chintamani or Andhra Bhasha Bhushanam
101.x: Different sources identify either Markandeya Puranam or Basava Puranam as the first Telugu Purana. The variation reflects differing criteria and traditions concerning literary 'firsts'.
101.tq: Read the wording closely where alternative traditions are expressly recognised instead of forcing a single answer.

101.s:
Consider the following statements about Krishnadevaraya and Telugu literary culture:

1. The line “Desa Bhashalandu Telugu Lessa” is associated with Krishnadevaraya.
2. The Ashtadiggajas are associated with the peak of Telugu literary culture during this period.
3. The Kakatiya period alone is identified with the Ashtadiggajas.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
101.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the Ashtadiggajas are associated with the peak of Telugu literature during the Vijayanagara period, particularly under Krishnadevaraya.
101.tq: Reject the statement that transfers a famous literary group to the wrong historical period.

101.s: Tikkana Somayaji was the first Telugu poet to have a work dedicated to him. Which work was dedicated to him?
o: Ranganatha Ramayanam by Gona Budda Reddy
101.x: Ketana dedicated Dasakumara Charitra to Tikkana Somayaji, making Tikkana the first Telugu poet to have a work dedicated to him.
101.tq: Use the author–work–dedicatee relationship rather than confusing it with authorship of the major epics.

101.s: Telugu was recognised as a classical language of India in which year?
101.x: Telugu has been recognised as a classical language since 2008.
101.tq: Distinguish the exact recognition year from nearby milestone years.

101.s: The proposal to install a statue of Tikkana Somayaji was associated with which district?
101.x: Andhra Pradesh discussed installing a statue of Tikkana Somayaji in SPSR Nellore district.
101.tq: Match the literary personality with the district linked to the current proposal.

101.s:
Arrange the following Telugu literary and inscriptional milestones in chronological order, beginning with the earliest:

A. Kalamalla inscription
B. Pitikayagulla eighth-century inscription
C. Addanki poetic inscription
D. Telugu records of the Nallamala survey extending to the sixteenth century
101.x: Kalamalla is dated to 575 CE, the Addanki poetic inscription belongs later, the Pitikayagulla inscription is from the eighth century, and the surveyed Telugu records extend up to the sixteenth century. Hence the order is A, C, B, D.
101.tq: Anchor the sequence with the known 575 CE date and the sixteenth-century end point, then place the eighth-century item carefully.

101.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Gidugu Venkata Ramamurthy — Birth anniversary commemorated on Telugu Language Day
Tikkana Somayaji — Birth anniversary commemorated on 29 August

101.tq: Find the single mismatched personality–observance pair rather than accepting all familiar Telugu literary names.

Jaichand was appointed Ghori's representative in India.

o: Reliance on war elephants and slow infantry formations
Complete absence of cavalry in Turkish armies

o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

102.s: Which statement correctly describes the foundation of the Ghaznavid line?
o: Mahmud founded the line after the conquest of Somnath.
Alptigin and Sabuktigin were both rulers of the Ghurid dynasty.
Sabuktigin founded the line, while Alptigin was only a later governor.
Alptigin founded the line, while Sabuktigin is regarded as its real founder.

104.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Seydi Ali Reis — Italy — Ottoman admiral
Mahmud Wali Balkhi — Balkh — Qutb Shahi court
Mir Zainul Abidin — Persia — Muhammad Qutb Shah
104.x: Seydi Ali Reis was from Turkey and was an Ottoman admiral, not from Italy. Tavernier was French, Mir Zainul Abidin was Persian and Mahmud Wali Balkhi came from Balkh.

o: Barbosa, Seydi Ali Reis and Mahmud Wali Balkhi
Marco Polo, Ibn Battuta and Tavernier

104.s: Al-Biruni came to India in approximately which year and century?
o: Around 1030 CE in the eleventh century
Around 1450 CE in the fifteenth century
Around 1300 CE in the fourteenth century
Around 1150 CE in the twelfth century

104.s: Which one of the following statements about Al-Biruni is correct?
o: He confined his study of India exclusively to military campaigns.
He wrote in Persian without learning any Indian language.
He was patronised by Deva Raya II of Vijayanagara.
He wrote in Arabic after learning Sanskrit and studied Indian religion, philosophy, astronomy and caste.
104.x: Al-Biruni learned Sanskrit and wrote in Arabic on Indian religion, philosophy, astronomy and the caste system. He was associated with Mahmud of Ghazni, not Vijayanagara.
104.tq: Use the language, subjects and patron together to identify the correct biographical statement.
104.sec: Al-Biruni - century, patron, works, views on India

104.s: According to Al-Biruni’s account, which of the following was observed on Kartika Amavasya?
o: The conquest of Madurai by Kampana
The coronation of Muhammad bin Tughlaq
The annual court of the Qutb Shahis
104.x: Al-Biruni recorded the celebration of Diwali on Kartika Amavasya.
104.tq: Match the festival and its calendrical occasion with the appropriate chronicler.
104.sec: Al-Biruni - century, patron, works, views on India

104.s: Which one of the following was Al-Biruni’s observation about Indian society?
o: Indians had abandoned Sanskrit learning entirely.
Indian society was free from caste distinctions.
Indians were unwilling to share learning with outsiders.
Indian scholars refused to study astronomy.
104.x: Al-Biruni observed that Indians were unwilling to share their learning with outsiders. He nevertheless studied Indian religion, philosophy, astronomy and caste through Sanskrit sources.
104.tq: Identify the precise social observation without reversing its meaning.
104.sec: Al-Biruni - century, patron, works, views on India

104.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Ramacharitam — Sandhyakara Nandi — Life of Ramapala
Prithviraja Vijaya — Gangadevi — Life of Prithviraj Chauhan
Madhura Vijayam — Jayanaka — Conquest of Madurai
104.x: Ramacharitam was written by Sandhyakara Nandi and deals with the life of Pala king Ramapala. Prithviraja Vijaya was by Jayanaka, Madhura Vijayam by Gangadevi and Siddhesvara Charitam by Kase Siddhappa.
104.tq: Start with the author–work pair and check the subject attached to each regional source.

104.s: Madhura Vijayam provides information chiefly about which of the following?
o: Kampana’s conquest of Madurai and conditions under Tughlaq rule
The conquest of Golconda by Aurangzeb
The life of Pala king Ramapala
104.x: Madhura Vijayam, written by Gangadevi, describes Kampana’s conquest of Madurai and conditions under Tughlaq rule.
104.tq: Associate the regional biography with its protagonist, campaign and political context.
104.sec: Regional and Sanskrit sources - Rajatarangini, biographies, Vijayanagara and Qutb Shahi works

104.s: Siddhesvara Charitam, written in Telugu by Kase Siddhappa, is a source for the study of which subject?
104.x: Siddhesvara Charitam is a Telugu work by Kase Siddhappa that provides information on Kakatiya-era society and religion.
104.tq: Match the language and author with the regional historical theme.
104.sec: Regional and Sanskrit sources - Rajatarangini, biographies, Vijayanagara and Qutb Shahi works

104.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Tarikh-i-Firishta — Muhammad Qasim Firishta — Deccan history
Hadikat-us-Salatin — Ali bin Tahir Bustani — Qutb Shahis
Kumara Ramana Charitam — Kannada — South India after the fall of Warangal
104.x: Muntakhab-ul-Lubab was written by Khafi Khan and deals with Aurangzeb’s conquest of Golconda. Gangadevi wrote Madhura Vijayam.
104.tq: Detect the swapped author in a list of regional and Deccan sources.
104.sec: Regional and Sanskrit sources - Rajatarangini, biographies, Vijayanagara and Qutb Shahi works

104.s: Tarikh-i-Firishta is also known as which of the following?
104.x: Tarikh-i-Firishta is also called Gulshan-i-Ibrahimi and was written by Muhammad Qasim Firishta.
104.tq: Discriminate between similar Persian titles by identifying the alternate title of the same work.
104.sec: Regional and Sanskrit sources - Rajatarangini, biographies, Vijayanagara and Qutb Shahi works

104.s:
Which of the following statements regarding Muhammad Qasim Firishta is correct?
1. He was born in Astarabad in Iran.
2. He was born in 1552.
3. His work calls Telangana ‘Tilang’.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
104.x: All three statements are correct. Firishta was born at Astarabad in Iran in 1552, and his Deccan history refers to Telangana as ‘Tilang’.
104.tq: Combine biographical numbers with a distinctive terminology clue.
104.sec: Regional and Sanskrit sources - Rajatarangini, biographies, Vijayanagara and Qutb Shahi works

104.s: Tarikh-i-Firishta was dedicated to which ruler?
104.x: Muhammad Qasim Firishta dedicated Tarikh-i-Firishta, or Gulshan-i-Ibrahimi, to Ibrahim Adil Shah of Bijapur.
104.tq: Distinguish the dedicatee from the rulers whose dynasties are described in the work.
104.sec: Regional and Sanskrit sources - Rajatarangini, biographies, Vijayanagara and Qutb Shahi works

104.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with a Qutb Shahi source?
o: Tarikh Muhammad Qutb Shah — Mirza Ibrahim Zuberi
History of the Qutb Shahi Dynasty — Anonymous, 1617
104.x: Hadikat-us-Salatin was written by Ali bin Tahir Bustani and deals with the Qutb Shahis. Basatin-us-Salatin was by Mirza Ibrahim Zuberi, Tarikh Muhammad Qutb Shah is anonymous and dated 1617, while H.K. Sherwani wrote the modern history.
104.tq: Use the author–title pair as the anchor and eliminate shifted authorship and dates.
104.sec: Regional and Sanskrit sources - Rajatarangini, biographies, Vijayanagara and Qutb Shahi works

104.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
104.x: Akbarnama was written by Abul Fazl. Tuzuk-i-Baburi was written by Babur, Humayun-nama by Gulbadan Begum and Padshahnama by Abdul Hamid Lahori.
104.tq: Use author–work matching and reject swapped authors.
104.sec: Royal memoirs and court histories → author

104.s: The Tuzuk-i-Baburi, also known as Baburnama, was written by Babur in which language?
104.x: Babur wrote the Tuzuk-i-Baburi in Turki. It is one of the important royal memoirs of the Mughal period.
104.tq: Test the exact language associated with a royal memoir.
104.sec: Royal memoirs and court histories → author

104.s: Who among the following authored the Humayun-nama?
104.x: Humayun-nama was authored by Gulbadan Begum, the daughter of Babur and sister of Humayun.
104.tq: Discriminate among closely associated Mughal court authors.
104.sec: Royal memoirs and court histories → author

104.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri — Jahangir
2. Ain-i-Akbari — Abul Fazl
3. Padshahnama — Abdul Hamid Lahori
4. Humayun-nama — Gulbadan Begum
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
104.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri was written by Jahangir, Ain-i-Akbari by Abul Fazl, Padshahnama by Abdul Hamid Lahori and Humayun-nama by Gulbadan Begum.
104.tq: Verify each author–work pair before selecting the complete combination.
104.sec: Royal memoirs and court histories → author

104.s: Which of the following statements is correct regarding Mughal literary works and translations?
o: The Mahabharata was translated into Persian as Kalila wa Dimna.
The Panchatantra was translated into Persian as Ain-i-Akbari.
The Ramayana was translated into Persian as Padshahnama.
The Mahabharata was translated into Persian as Razmnama.
104.x: The Persian translation of the Mahabharata was known as Razmnama. Kalila wa Dimna was the Persian rendering of the Panchatantra.
104.tq: Separate translated works from the titles of their Persian versions.
104.sec: Royal memoirs and court histories → author

104.s: The Ain-i-Akbari, dated to 1590, contains an early reference to which festival?
104.x: The Ain-i-Akbari, dated to 1590, mentions Diwali. This makes it an important early textual reference to the festival.
104.tq: Link the precise date with the cultural fact rather than a nearby festival.
104.sec: Royal memoirs and court histories → author

104.s: The Ghazinagar Persian inscription is located in which present-day district, and is associated with which Qutb Shahi ruler?
o: Medak district — Jamsheed Quli Qutb Shah
Warangal district — Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah
104.x: The Ghazinagar inscription is in Nalgonda and is associated with Ibrahim Quli. It dates to 1576–77.
104.tq: Combine location, ruler and date in an inscription-based identification.
104.sec: Inscriptions and coins as medieval sources

104.s: Which of the following correctly lists the Qutb Shahi inscriptions and their dates?
104.x: The Daru-Shifa inscription dates to 1595, while the Badshahi Ashurkhana inscription dates to 1592–96. The other dates belong to different records.
104.tq: Match inscriptions with their exact dates and avoid date swapping.
104.sec: Inscriptions and coins as medieval sources

104.s: The Nizami Mosque inscription at Golconda is significant because it dates Quli Qutb-ul-Mulk's independence to:
104.x: The Nizami Mosque inscription at Golconda dates the independence of Quli Qutb-ul-Mulk to 1518.
104.tq: Test the precise date attached to a political event in an inscription.
104.sec: Inscriptions and coins as medieval sources

104.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Vilasa copper plate — Musunuri Prolaya Nayaka
Palam Baoli inscription — Musunuri Prolaya Nayaka
104.x: The Palam Baoli inscription is a Sanskrit record praising Balban and dates to 1276. The Vilasa copper plate is associated with Musunuri Prolaya Nayaka.
104.tq: Find the wrongly assigned person by checking the inscription–issuer relationship.
104.sec: Inscriptions and coins as medieval sources

104.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Vilasa copper plate is associated with Musunuri Prolaya Nayaka.
2. The Kaluvacheru inscription is associated with Anitalli.
3. The Warangal inscription of Shitab Khan dates to 1504–06.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
104.x: All three statements are correct. The Vilasa copper plate dates approximately to 1330, the Kaluvacheru record is associated with Anitalli, and Shitab Khan's Warangal inscription dates to 1504–06.
104.tq: Check names, record types and dates independently before choosing the combination.
104.sec: Inscriptions and coins as medieval sources

104.s: Mahmud of Ghazni's Lahore dirhams are especially significant as medieval sources because they contain:
o: An Arabic legend and its Sanskrit translation in Sharada script
A Telugu inscription and an Arabic translation
A Sanskrit legend and its Persian translation in Devanagari script
Only a Persian inscription in Nastaliq script
104.x: The Lahore dirhams of Mahmud of Ghazni carry an Arabic legend along with a Sanskrit translation written in Sharada script.
