o: the benefits of British revenue settlements
the revenue burden and the ruin of traditional crafts
the protection given to indigenous industries
their support for the educated middle class
185.x: Peasants and artisans were affected by the burden of revenue and the destruction of traditional crafts, encouraging their participation.
185.tq: Link a social group’s participation to its stated economic grievances.
185.sec: ■ Participation and attitude of social groups  [other exams, GROUP-II]

185.s: Why did the educated middle class largely remain aloof from the revolt of 1857?
o: It considered British rule to be modernising.
It was led by the taluqdars of Awadh.
It had already established an independent national government.
It opposed all forms of education introduced by the British.
185.x: The educated middle class generally remained aloof because it viewed British rule as modernising.
185.tq: Identify the attitude of a social group rather than its formal position.
185.sec: ■ Participation and attitude of social groups  [other exams, GROUP-II]

185.s: Which one of the following groups was generally loyal to the British during the revolt of 1857?
o: Most princes, including Scindia, Holkar, the Nizam and the rulers of Rajputana
185.x: Most princes, including Scindia, Holkar, the Nizam and the rulers of Rajputana, remained loyal to the British.
185.tq: Use the group-level exception to avoid assuming universal princely participation.
185.sec: ■ Participation and attitude of social groups  [other exams, GROUP-II]

185.s:
Consider the following statements regarding groups that remained loyal to the British during the revolt:
1. Merchants and moneylenders generally remained loyal.
2. Most princes remained loyal.
3. The educated middle class generally remained aloof rather than joining the revolt.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
185.x: Merchants and moneylenders, most princes, and the educated middle class did not generally join the revolt; the middle class remained aloof because it saw British rule as modernising.
185.tq: Recognise a correct combination of social-group attitudes.
185.sec: ■ Participation and attitude of social groups  [other exams, GROUP-II]

185.s: Which one of the following statements about the Andhra region during the revolt of 1857 is NOT correct?
o: There were attempts at Kadiri and revolts associated with Korukonda Subba Reddy and Dandasena.
Turrebaz Khan was associated with a limited revolt in Hyderabad.
Andhra had no local leaders or limited revolts during the period.
185.x: The statement that Andhra had no local leaders or limited revolts is incorrect. Turrebaz Khan, the Kadiri attempt, Korukonda Subba Reddy and Dandasena are associated with such activity.
185.tq: Reject an absolute statement when several regional exceptions are identified.
185.sec: ■ Participation and attitude of social groups  [other exams, GROUP-II]

185.s: Dandasena, associated with the revolt in the Andhra region, belonged to which community and area?
185.x: Dandasena was a Savara associated with Paralakimidi.
185.tq: Test a lesser-known regional name–community–place association.
185.sec: ■ Participation and attitude of social groups  [other exams, GROUP-II]

185.s: What was the significance of Bahadur Shah II during the revolt of 1857?
o: He led only the sepoys of the Bengal Army.
He was accepted as the symbolic head by Hindu and Muslim rebels.
He represented the educated middle class in the revolt.
He served as the principal British commander in Delhi.
185.x: Bahadur Shah II was accepted as the symbolic head by both Hindu and Muslim rebels.
185.tq: Distinguish symbolic leadership from direct military command.

185.s: The issue of greased cartridges contributed to Hindu-Muslim unity in the revolt because it—
o: offended the religious sentiments of both communities
was opposed only by Hindu rulers
abolished separate religious practices in the army
provided equal military ranks to both communities
185.x: The greased cartridges offended the religious sentiments of both Hindus and Muslims, creating a common grievance.
185.tq: Connect a common grievance with inter-community cooperation.

185.s: Which development after the revolt of 1857 reflected the British response to the Hindu-Muslim cooperation witnessed during the revolt?
o: Adoption of a policy of divide and rule
Withdrawal of the British Army from India
Transfer of authority to the Indian National Congress
185.x: After 1857, the British increasingly pursued a policy of divide and rule in response to the cooperation between Hindus and Muslims.
185.tq: Link a historical development with its stated political consequence.

185.s: Which of the following was NOT a major cause of the failure of the revolt of 1857?
o: A forward-looking programme for a future society
The loyalty of several princes and big zamindars
Lack of central leadership and coordination
185.x: The revolt lacked, rather than possessed, a forward-looking programme or vision of a future society.
185.tq: Identify the option that reverses a listed weakness.

185.s: The limited territorial and social base of the revolt of 1857 is best reflected by the fact that—
o: only Bengal supplied troops to the British
East, West and South India remained intact and supplied troops to the British
all regions of India simultaneously joined the revolt
the revolt was confined exclusively to the princely states
185.x: Large parts of East, West and South India remained intact and supplied troops to the British, limiting the revolt’s territorial and social reach.
185.tq: Use the geographical extent of participation to assess the strength of a rebellion.

185.s: Which combination most accurately explains the military advantage enjoyed by the British during the revolt of 1857?
o: Modern weapons, resources, experienced generals and telegraph communication
A larger popular base, unified leadership and a future-oriented programme
Support from all peasants, artisans and sepoys
Absence of loyal princes and zamindars
185.x: The British possessed modern weapons such as the Enfield rifle, greater resources, experienced generals and telegraph communication.
185.tq: Select the option containing the complete set of military advantages.

185.s: Which one of the following combinations contributed to the failure of the revolt of 1857?
o: A common programme for a future society
Unified central command, modern weapons and telegraph communication among rebels
Complete participation of East, West and South India
Loyal princes, loyal big zamindars and inadequate support from the martial races of the north
185.x: The revolt suffered because several princes and big zamindars remained loyal and it lacked adequate support from the martial races of the north.
185.tq: Combine political and military causes without reversing their direction.

185.s: Mangal Pandey, whom the Prime Minister paid tribute to as an early hero of the First War of Independence, belonged to the—
185.x: Mangal Pandey was a soldier of the 34th Bengal Native Infantry.
185.tq: Match a historical personality with the precise military unit named in the question.

185.s: Mangal Pandey was associated with which of the following sequence of events?
o: Barrackpore on 29 March 1857 and execution by hanging on 8 April 1857
Meerut on 10 May 1857 and execution on 11 May 1857
Delhi on 12 May 1857 and execution on 29 March 1857
Kanpur on 8 April 1857 and execution on 29 March 1857
185.x: Mangal Pandey was associated with the incident at Barrackpore on 29 March 1857 and was hanged on 8 April 1857.
185.tq: Pair the place and date with the later date of execution.

185.s: Which statement best expresses the significance of the revolt of 1857 despite its failure?
o: It shattered the myth of British invincibility and planted the seeds of later nationalism.
It prevented all later nationalist movements.
It immediately ended British rule in India.
It established a modern democratic government throughout India.
185.x: The revolt damaged the belief in British invincibility and helped create the conditions for later nationalism, although it did not end British rule.
185.tq: Distinguish long-term significance from immediate political outcome.

185.s: Annapurnayya, known as ‘Andhra Netaji’, was sentenced to 18 months’ rigorous imprisonment for which of the following?
o: Writing the article *Chicharapidugu* on the revolt of 1857
Supporting the British policy of divide and rule
Organising the RIN revolt at Bombay
185.x: Annapurnayya received 18 months’ rigorous imprisonment for his article *Chicharapidugu*, which dealt with the revolt of 1857.
185.tq: Test the association between a regional nationalist figure and his specific written work.

185.s: Which of the following correctly contrasts the two broad interpretations of the revolt of 1857?
o: The nationalist interpretation calls it the First War of Independence, whereas the critical interpretation rejects its description as first, national and a war of independence.
The nationalist interpretation denies popular participation, whereas the critical interpretation accepts a fully modern national movement.
Both interpretations regard it exclusively as a military mutiny.
Both interpretations agree that it established a future Indian nation-state.
185.x: Nationalist historians describe 1857 as the First War of Independence, while the critical interpretation challenges all three components of that description.
185.tq: Compare opposing historiographical positions by their defining conclusions.

185.s: The debate over whether an uprising was a ‘mutiny’ or a ‘revolt’ was also applied to the RIN revolt of 1946. The RIN revolt began at HMIS Talwar, Bombay, on—
185.x: The RIN revolt began at HMIS Talwar in Bombay on 18 February 1946.
185.tq: Distinguish a precise date from nearby dates associated with another event.

185.s: The 80th anniversary of the RIN revolt associated with HMIS Talwar was marked on—
185.x: The 80th anniversary of the RIN revolt of 1946 was marked on 18 February 2026.
185.tq: Calculate and verify an anniversary year from the original event year.

186.s: The Government of India Act, 1858 was officially titled as the:
o: Act for the Political Settlement of India
Act for the Better Administration of India
Act for the Good Government of India
Act for the Regulation of Crown Territories
186.x: The Government of India Act, 1858 was titled the Act for the Good Government of India.
186.tq: Directly identify the exact official title of the Act.
186.sec: Government of India Act 1858 - transfer of power, Secretary of State, India Council, Viceroy  [APPSC]

186.s: Under the Government of India Act, 1858, the powers of the British Crown in India were exercised through the:
o: President of the Board of Control
Chairman of the Court of Directors
186.x: The Act created the office of the Secretary of State for India, through whom the British Crown exercised its powers in India.
186.tq: Use the institutional-power clue to identify the authority concerned.
186.sec: Government of India Act 1858 - transfer of power, Secretary of State, India Council, Viceroy  [APPSC]

186.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Secretary of State for India:
1. He was a member of the British Cabinet.
2. He was assisted by a 15-member Council of India.
3. His Council was located in London.
4. He could issue orders to the Viceroy.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
186.x: The Secretary of State was a British Cabinet minister, assisted by a 15-member Council of India in London, and could issue orders to the Viceroy.
186.tq: Check each institutional detail before selecting the complete combination.
186.sec: Government of India Act 1858 - transfer of power, Secretary of State, India Council, Viceroy  [APPSC]

186.s: Who was the first Secretary of State for India under the Government of India Act, 1858?
186.x: Lord Stanley was the first Secretary of State for India under the new Crown administration.
186.tq: Distinguish the first office-holder from later Viceroys and Secretaries of State.
186.sec: Government of India Act 1858 - transfer of power, Secretary of State, India Council, Viceroy  [APPSC]

186.s:
Consider the following statements about the offices of Governor-General and Viceroy:
1. The Viceroy dealt particularly with the princely states.
2. The Governor-General administered British India.
3. The two titles referred to entirely separate office-holders after 1858.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
186.x: The same office-holder functioned as Viceroy in relation to the princely states and as Governor-General in British India. Therefore, statement 3 is false.
186.tq: Use the distinction between two functions of one office-holder to reject the absolute statement.
186.sec: Government of India Act 1858 - transfer of power, Secretary of State, India Council, Viceroy  [APPSC]

186.s: Lord Canning occupies which one of the following positions in Indian constitutional history?
o: The last Governor-General and the first Viceroy
The last Governor-General under Company rule and the first Governor of Bengal
The first Viceroy and the first Secretary of State
The first Secretary of State for India and the last Governor-General
186.x: Lord Canning was the last Governor-General and the first Viceroy of India. He held office during 1856–1862.
186.tq: Match the office-holder with the paired transitional offices.
186.sec: Government of India Act 1858 - transfer of power, Secretary of State, India Council, Viceroy  [APPSC]

186.s: Lord Canning held the office of Governor-General and Viceroy during which period?
186.x: Lord Canning served during the period 1856–1862, becoming the first Viceroy after the transfer of administration to the Crown.
186.tq: Use the middle-value year range while distinguishing it from neighbouring periods.
186.sec: Government of India Act 1858 - transfer of power, Secretary of State, India Council, Viceroy  [APPSC]

186.s: The system of ‘double government’ ended by the Government of India Act, 1858 consisted of which two bodies?
o: The Court of Directors and the Board of Control
The Legislative Council and the Supreme Court
The Board of Revenue and the Court of Directors
The India Council and the Privy Council
186.x: The Act ended the Company-era double government represented by the Court of Directors and the Board of Control.
186.tq: Identify the two bodies forming the paired administrative arrangement.
186.sec: Government of India Act 1858 - transfer of power, Secretary of State, India Council, Viceroy  [APPSC]

186.s:
The Charter Act of 1813 is associated with which of the following provisions?
1. Ending the Company’s trade monopoly except in tea and China trade
2. Allowing missionaries to enter India
3. Making the Company purely administrative
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
186.x: The Charter Act of 1813 ended the Company’s trade monopoly except in tea and China trade and allowed missionaries to enter India. Making the Company purely administrative was a provision of the Charter Act of 1833.
186.tq: Separate closely related Charter Acts by testing the provision attached to each one.
186.sec: Government of India Act 1858 - transfer of power, Secretary of State, India Council, Viceroy  [APPSC]

186.s: The Charter Act of 1833 made the East India Company:
o: an agency of the Crown headed by the Secretary of State
a body subordinate to the Board of Control in commercial matters only
186.x: The Charter Act of 1833 ended the Company’s remaining commercial functions and made it a purely administrative organisation.
186.tq: Use the change in the Company’s character to identify the correct Charter Act.
186.sec: Government of India Act 1858 - transfer of power, Secretary of State, India Council, Viceroy  [APPSC]

186.s:
Which of the following was NOT an object associated with the Queen’s Proclamation of 1858?
1. Disclaiming further annexation of Indian States
2. Placing the administration of India under the Crown
3. Regulating the commercial activities of the East India Company
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
186.x: The Proclamation disclaimed further annexation and placed Indian administration under the Crown. Regulation of Company trade was not one of its objects.
186.tq: Find the unrelated commercial objective among constitutional and political purposes.
186.sec: Queen's Proclamation - date, venue, reader, promises, which were kept  [other exams]

186.s: The Queen’s Proclamation of 1858 declared that the rights, dignity and honour of the native princes would be respected and that:
o: only the rulers who adopted Christianity could retain their states
the treaties made by the East India Company would be honoured
all princely states would be annexed after the death of their rulers
the princely states would be abolished immediately
186.x: The Proclamation promised respect for the rights, dignity and honour of the native princes and declared that Company treaties would be honoured.
186.tq: Identify the promise concerning princely states and treaty obligations.
186.sec: Queen's Proclamation - date, venue, reader, promises, which were kept  [other exams]

186.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the religious assurance in the Queen’s Proclamation:
1. The Government promised non-interference in religious and social affairs.
2. Forced conversions were rejected.
3. The State withdrew its patronage from missionary conversion.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
186.x: The Proclamation promised religious neutrality, rejected forced conversion and was followed by the withdrawal of state patronage from missionary conversion.
186.tq: Confirm whether all statements describe the same neutrality-based policy.
186.sec: Queen's Proclamation - date, venue, reader, promises, which were kept  [other exams]

186.s: The Queen’s Proclamation promised that public appointments would be made primarily on the basis of:
o: ownership of land and payment of revenue
hereditary status and loyalty to the Company
merit and qualifications without discrimination of race or creed
186.x: The Proclamation promised equal opportunity in public service on the basis of merit and qualifications, without discrimination of race or creed.
186.tq: Identify the exact basis of the promised public-service principle.
186.sec: Queen's Proclamation - date, venue, reader, promises, which were kept  [other exams]

186.s:
Which of the following rights were expressly promised protection under the Queen’s Proclamation?
1. Property rights
2. Succession rights
3. Peasants’ rights over land, subject to payment of revenue
4. Commercial monopoly of the East India Company
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
186.x: The Proclamation promised protection of property and succession rights and recognised peasants’ land rights so long as revenue was paid. It did not protect a commercial monopoly of the Company.
186.tq: Separate protected civil and land rights from an unrelated commercial claim.
186.sec: Queen's Proclamation - date, venue, reader, promises, which were kept  [other exams]

186.s: The period from 1858 to 1885 is described in the context of the Queen’s Proclamation as the:
186.x: The period 1858–1885 is commonly described as the Era of Broken Promises because the assurance of equal employment was not implemented in practice.
186.tq: Link the distinctive period label with its stated chronological range.
186.sec: Queen's Proclamation - date, venue, reader, promises, which were kept  [other exams]

186.s: Which one of the following best illustrates the failure to implement the Queen’s Proclamation’s promise of equality in public employment?
o: Missionary patronage was withdrawn by the Crown.
The Doctrine of Lapse was abolished.
Company treaties with princes were honoured.
The ICS remained dominated by Europeans.
186.x: The Indian Civil Service remained European-dominated, showing that the promise of equal employment was not implemented. Secretary of State Kimberley stated that an adequate number of civil servants would always be Europeans.
186.tq: Apply the promise to the administrative outcome that contradicted it.
186.sec: Queen's Proclamation - date, venue, reader, promises, which were kept  [other exams]

186.s: The Queen’s Proclamation of 1858 is often regarded as the:
o: Magna Carta of the Indian people
Magna Carta of the East India Company
186.x: The Queen’s Proclamation is often called the Magna Carta of the Indian people because of its wide-ranging assurances concerning rulers, religion, public service, property and land rights.
186.tq: Recall the historically used descriptive title rather than the constitutional Act title.
186.sec: Queen's Proclamation - date, venue, reader, promises, which were kept  [other exams]

186.s:
Which one of the following lines expresses the concluding sentiment of the Queen’s Proclamation regarding India?
1. The well-being of Indian subjects is the strength of the Crown.
2. Their satisfaction is the security of the Crown.
3. Their gratitude is the reward of the Crown.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
186.x: The concluding sentiment stated that the well-being of Indian subjects was the Crown’s strength, their satisfaction its security and their gratitude its reward.
186.tq: Recognise the complete three-part formulation instead of selecting an incomplete quotation.
186.sec: Queen's Proclamation - date, venue, reader, promises, which were kept  [other exams]

186.s: The recommendations for the reorganisation of the Indian Army after the Revolt of 1857 were associated with which commission?
186.x: The Peel Commission, constituted in 1859, recommended major changes in the composition, organisation and recruitment of the Indian Army.
186.tq: Identify the commission associated with a specific administrative measure.
186.sec: Army reorganisation - Peel Commission, ratio, artillery, recruitment

186.s: After the recommendations of the Peel Commission, the European-to-Indian ratio in the Bengal Army was changed from
186.x: The European-to-Indian ratio in the Bengal Army was altered from 1:5 to 1:2 after the Revolt of 1857.
186.tq: Track the direction of change between two numerical ratios.
186.sec: Army reorganisation - Peel Commission, ratio, artillery, recruitment

186.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the reorganisation of the British Indian Army after 1857:
1. Artillery was placed exclusively under European control.
2. Indians were barred from serving with heavy weapons.
3. Regiments were organised on caste, community and regional lines.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
186.x: All three statements are correct. The British retained artillery and heavy weapons for Europeans and organised other regiments to restrict unity and fraternisation among Indian soldiers.
186.tq: Check each administrative measure separately before selecting the combined code.
186.sec: Army reorganisation - Peel Commission, ratio, artillery, recruitment

186.s: Which one of the following was NOT a principal basis for organising regiments in the post-1857 British Indian Army?
186.x: Regiments were organised according to caste, community and region. A common national identity was contrary to the British policy of preventing cross-regional fraternisation.
186.tq: Find the option that reverses the stated purpose of an administrative policy.
186.sec: Army reorganisation - Peel Commission, ratio, artillery, recruitment

186.s: The recruitment policy of the British after the Revolt of 1857 increasingly favoured which groups as so-called “martial races”?
186.x: The British increasingly recruited Sikhs, Gurkhas and Pathans, describing them as martial races, while reducing dependence on recruits from Awadh and Bihar.
186.tq: Distinguish the favoured recruitment groups from the groups deliberately reduced.
186.sec: Army reorganisation - Peel Commission, ratio, artillery, recruitment

186.s: The “counterpoise” principle in the post-1857 army policy primarily meant
o: placing all artillery under Indian officers
recruiting soldiers exclusively from princely states
using divisions based on caste, community and region to prevent military unity
186.x: The counterpoise principle used social, regional and communal divisions within the army to prevent collective action and cross-regional fraternisation.
186.tq: Apply the underlying purpose of a policy to a short administrative situation.
186.sec: Army reorganisation - Peel Commission, ratio, artillery, recruitment

186.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with the post-1857 recruitment policy?
o: Awadh and Bihar — preferred martial-race recruitment zones
Sikhs and Gurkhas — communities increasingly recruited by the British
Pathans and Rajputs — communities excluded from military service
Bengalis and Biharis — exclusive guardians of artillery
186.x: Sikhs and Gurkhas were among the communities increasingly recruited under the martial-races policy. Awadh and Bihar were comparatively disfavoured after 1857.
186.tq: Start with the sure community-policy association and eliminate reversed pairs.
186.sec: Army reorganisation - Peel Commission, ratio, artillery, recruitment

186.s: Who withdrew the Doctrine of Lapse and recognised the right of adoption by childless Indian rulers?
186.x: Lord Canning withdrew the Doctrine of Lapse and recognised adoption rights after 1857. This marked the abandonment of Dalhousie’s annexation policy.
186.tq: Use the ruler-policy trap by separating the policy’s originator from the person who ended it.
186.sec: Policy towards princes - adoption rights, end of annexation

186.s: The policy of annexation associated with Lord Dalhousie was officially abandoned after 1857 mainly through the recognition of
o: the election of rulers by legislative councils
the complete independence of princely states
the right of adoption by childless rulers
186.x: The British recognised the right of childless rulers to adopt heirs, thereby withdrawing the Doctrine of Lapse and ending the annexation policy associated with Dalhousie.
186.tq: Identify the constitutional-political consequence of a policy change.
186.sec: Policy towards princes - adoption rights, end of annexation

186.s:
Consider the following statements about the post-1857 policy towards Indian princes:
1. Princes were assured that their states would not ordinarily be annexed.
2. Their acceptance of British paramountcy was required.
3. They became subordinate allies and supports of British rule.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
186.x: All three statements are correct. The princes retained their states subject to British paramountcy and were converted into loyal subordinate allies of the Crown.
186.tq: Test the relationship between territorial assurance, paramountcy and political dependence.
186.sec: Policy towards princes - adoption rights, end of annexation

186.s: The description of Indian princes as “breakwaters to the storm” after the Revolt of 1857 is associated with
186.x: Lord Elgin described the loyal Indian princes as “breakwaters to the storm,” reflecting their role as supports of British rule after 1857.
186.tq: Match a distinctive phrase with its associated British official.
186.sec: Policy towards princes - adoption rights, end of annexation

186.s: Which of the following best describes the change in British policy towards Muslims after 1857?
o: The British transferred all administrative posts exclusively to Muslims.
The British consistently treated Muslims as their principal allies from the beginning.
The British initially blamed and targeted Muslims, but later cultivated them against the educated Hindu middle class.
The British abandoned all communal distinctions and promoted joint political representation.
186.x: The British initially held Muslims chiefly responsible for the revolt and adopted anti-Muslim measures, but later cultivated Muslim support against the rising educated Hindu middle class.
186.tq: Follow the chronological shift rather than selecting an absolute statement.
186.sec: Divide-and-rule and racial attitudes - Hindu-Muslim policy shift

186.s:
Arrange the following developments in the British policy after the Revolt of 1857 in the correct chronological order:
A. Initial anti-Muslim policy
B. Cultivation of Muslims against the educated Hindu middle class
C. Greater protection to zamindars and landlords
D. Abandonment of reforming zeal and social interference
186.x: The British first adopted an anti-Muslim posture, later cultivated Muslims against educated Hindus, protected landed interests and withdrew from social reform and interference.
186.tq: Arrange policy changes by their stated sequence from initial reaction to later consolidation.
186.sec: Divide-and-rule and racial attitudes - Hindu-Muslim policy shift

186.s: Which one of the following was NOT a feature of British policy towards social and landed interests after 1857?
o: Withdrawal from missionary and reforming activity
Continued aggressive interference in Indian social customs
Recognition of proprietary rights of zamindars and taluqdars
186.x: The British abandoned their earlier reforming zeal and adopted a policy of non-interference in social customs. They nevertheless protected landed interests and stepped back from missionary activity.
186.tq: Identify the reversed policy by testing the word “continued” against the historical shift.
186.sec: Divide-and-rule and racial attitudes - Hindu-Muslim policy shift

186.s: The reversal of the annexation of large estates in Awadh after 1857 resulted in zamindars and taluqdars being granted
o: exclusive authority over the British Indian Army
the right to reject British paramountcy
proprietary rights and transformed into a conservative loyalist class
186.x: In Awadh, zamindars and taluqdars were restored to proprietary rights and became a conservative and loyal landed class supporting British rule.
186.tq: Link an administrative concession to its political consequence.
186.sec: Divide-and-rule and racial attitudes - Hindu-Muslim policy shift

186.s: Which of the following correctly reflects British racial attitudes after the Revolt of 1857?
o: Indians were admitted freely to the highest administrative posts.
Rebels were generally tried through transparent constitutional procedures.
Racial arrogance hardened, rebels were publicly executed after mock trials, and Indians were excluded from higher posts.
Missionary activity was expanded as the central instrument of reconciliation.
186.x: Racial arrogance intensified after 1857. Rebels were publicly executed after mock trials, while Indians continued to be excluded from higher administrative positions.
186.tq: Prefer the precise combined description over options containing absolute reversals.
186.sec: Divide-and-rule and racial attitudes - Hindu-Muslim policy shift

186.s: The absence of Indians in the legislative council, as a lesson of the Revolt of 1857, was particularly criticised by
186.x: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan attributed part of the crisis to the absence of Indian opinion in the council, a concern addressed through later expansion and nomination of Indian members.
186.tq: Match the criticism of an institutional defect with its associated thinker.
186.sec: Indian Councils Act 1861 - link to 1857 lessons

186.s: The Indian Councils Act was passed on
186.x: The Indian Councils Act was passed on 1 August 1861 and marked an important beginning in the development of representative institutions in India.
186.tq: Distinguish the exact enactment date from nearby dates associated with related reforms.
186.sec: Indian Councils Act 1861 - link to 1857 lessons

186.s: Who among the following was NOT one of the first three Indians nominated by Canning to the expanded legislative council?
186.x: The first three Indians nominated by Canning were the Raja of Benaras, the Maharaja of Patiala and Sir Dinkar Rao. Sir Syed Ahmad Khan was not one of these three nominees.
186.tq: Find the outsider in a short list of named nominees.
186.sec: Indian Councils Act 1861 - link to 1857 lessons

186.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Indian Councils Act of 1861:
1. It enabled the Viceroy to nominate Indians as non-official members of his expanded legislative council.
2. It gave statutory recognition to Canning’s portfolio system.
3. It empowered the Viceroy to issue ordinances in an emergency.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
186.x: All three statements are correct. The Act incorporated Indian nomination, recognised the portfolio system introduced in 1859 and retained emergency ordinance-making power with the Viceroy.
186.tq: Test separate provisions of an Act before choosing the comprehensive code.
186.sec: Indian Councils Act 1861 - link to 1857 lessons

186.s: The portfolio system which received statutory recognition under the Indian Councils Act, 1861 had been introduced by Canning in
186.x: Canning introduced the portfolio system in 1859, and the Indian Councils Act of 1861 subsequently gave it statutory recognition.
186.tq: Separate the year of introduction from the year of statutory recognition.
186.sec: Indian Councils Act 1861 - link to 1857 lessons

186.s: The last Mughal emperor, Bahadur Shah II, was deported to
186.x: Bahadur Shah II was tried and exiled to Rangoon after the Revolt of 1857, where he died in 1862.
186.tq: Recall the precise place associated with exile rather than a nearby colonial location.
186.sec: End of the Mughal dynasty and East India Company

186.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the fate of the East India Company after 1857?
o: It retained political rule until 1874 and was then transferred to the Crown.
It was dissolved immediately in 1858 without any formal legal process.
It continued to rule India under the Crown until 1901.

Singh Sabha at Amritsar — 1873; Singh Sabha at Lahore — 1879; Khalsa College, Amritsar — 1892
Singh Sabha at Lahore — 1873; Khalsa College, Amritsar — 1879; Singh Sabha at Amritsar — 1892
Singh Sabha at Amritsar — 1892; Singh Sabha at Lahore — 1879; Khalsa College, Amritsar — 1873

192.s: Which statement best describes the significance of Ram Singh Kuka in the Sikh reform tradition?

He founded the Ahmadiya Movement at Qadian.
He introduced Urdu as the language of Osmania University.

192.s: The Sikh Gurdwaras Act of 1925 placed gurdwaras under the control of the:

192.s: Nasaraiah, who was popular among the Madigas, preached:

The necessity of armed jihad against all Western education
One God and opposition to idol worship
The establishment of Sikh gurdwara committees

192.s: Which comparison between the Aligarh and Deoband movements is correctly stated?
o: Aligarh emphasised Western education and cooperation with the British, whereas Deoband represented an orthodox and anti-British strand.
Aligarh was orthodox and anti-British, whereas Deoband promoted Western education and cooperation with the British.

192.s: Which of the following statements correctly expresses the broader significance of the Aligarh and Deoband movements?
o: Deoband created the modern educated Muslim middle class, while Aligarh opposed all modern education.
Aligarh helped build a modern educated Muslim middle class, while Deoband kept alive an orthodox and anti-colonial strand.
Aligarh and Deoband were both exclusively movements for Sikh gurdwara reform.
Neither movement had an educational or political significance.

192.s: Sayyid Ahmad Khan’s later political conservatism has been criticised for:

192.s: Which statement reflects the criticism concerning the political position of the Deoband movement?
o: It was founded to promote Parsi marriage reform.
It supported British rule because it rejected all anti-colonial activity.
It supported Congress largely to oppose Sir Syed rather than from a positive political creed.

192.s: Which of the following legal pairings is correctly matched?
192.x: Parsi marriages are governed by the Parsi Marriage and Divorce Act, 1936. The Sikh Anand Marriage Act dates to 1909 and was amended in 2012 to allow registration.

o: Abolish the practice of idol worship among Madigas
Introduce Urdu as the medium of higher education
192.x: The Sikh Anand Marriage Act, 1909 was amended in 2012 to allow registration of Sikh marriages. Gurdwara administration was dealt with by the Sikh Gurdwaras Act, 1925.

192.s: Which movement is identified among the earliest movements to resist British rule in Punjab?
192.x: The Namdharis are identified among the earliest movements that resisted British rule in Punjab. The other options belonged to different regional or religious reform contexts.

193.s: The Kuka movement was initially begun in the 1840s by whom?

193.s: Which one of the following was NOT a characteristic practice of the Kuka or Namdhari followers?

Khalsa ceremonies associated with Guru Gobind Singh

The institutional authority of the mahants

It was written for the Krishna Patrika in 1905 by Dinabandhu Mitra.

198.x: Vande Mataram appeared in Anandamath and was first sung at the Indian National Congress by Rabindranath Tagore in Calcutta in 1896. It later became a nationalist war cry.
198.tq: Check the work, performer, venue and year together.

198.s: Which of the following is the correct sequence of Bankim Chandra Chatterjee's novels as described in relation to his works?
o: Durgeshnandini — first novel; Anandamath — 1882; Rajasimha, Rajani and Indira — other novels
Anandamath — first novel; Durgeshnandini — 1882; Rajani — nationalist poem
Rajasimha — first novel; Indira — 1882; Durgeshnandini — historical poem
Rajani — first novel; Anandamath — 1860; Indira — political association
198.x: Durgeshnandini was Bankim's first novel. His other novels listed here include Rajasimha, Rajani and Indira, while Anandamath was published in 1882.
198.tq: Separate the author's first novel from his other works and publication year.

198.s: Who wrote Nil Darpan, published in 1860?
198.x: Dinabandhu Mitra wrote Nil Darpan, which was published in 1860.
198.tq: Direct author-year recall for nationalist literature.

198.s: Which of the following was NOT listed among the nationalist poets of Bengal?
198.x: Rangalal Banerjee, Hem Chandra Banerjee and Nabin Chandra Sen were listed as nationalist poets of Bengal. Y. Doraiswamayya was associated with the Telugu translation of Vande Mataram.
198.tq: Find the person belonging to the translation detail rather than the Bengali poets' group.

198.s: The Telugu translation of Vande Mataram was made by
o: P. Anandacharlu and G. Subramania Iyer
Rangalal Banerjee and Hem Chandra Banerjee
Surendranath Banerjee and Ananda Mohan Bose
198.x: The Telugu translation of Vande Mataram was made by Y. Doraiswamayya and M. Ramarao.
198.tq: Match the translation with its translators.

198.s: The first nationalist song in Andhra, titled 'The Cry of Mother India', appeared in
198.x: 'The Cry of Mother India' appeared in Krishna Patrika on 15 December 1905 and was regarded as the first nationalist song in Andhra.
198.tq: Combine the title, publication and exact date to identify the correct option.

198.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Newspaper)
a. Amrita Bazar Patrika
a. The Hindu
c. The Bengalee
d. Kesari

List-II (Founder or founders)
i. Surendranath Banerjee
ii. Tilak
iii. Sisir Kumar Ghosh and Motilal Ghosh
iv. G. Subramania Iyer, M. Veeraraghavachariar and others

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
198.x: Amrita Bazar Patrika was founded by Sisir Kumar Ghosh and Motilal Ghosh; The Hindu by G. Subramania Iyer, M. Veeraraghavachariar and others; The Bengalee by Surendranath Banerjee; and Kesari by Tilak.
198.tq: Start from the sure founder–newspaper pairs and eliminate codes.

198.s: Amrita Bazar Patrika was founded in which year, and in which year did it become an English newspaper overnight?
198.x: Amrita Bazar Patrika was founded in 1868 and changed into an English newspaper overnight in 1878 to escape the Vernacular Press Act.
198.tq: Pair the two closely related years instead of treating the later year as the founding year.

198.s: The Hindu was founded in 1878 at which place?
198.x: The Hindu was founded in 1878 at Madras by G. Subramania Iyer, M. Veeraraghavachariar and others.
198.tq: Use the location attached to the newspaper rather than the founder’s regional association.

198.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
198.x: Krishna Patrika began on 1 February 1902 at Machilipatnam. Andhra Patrika, not Krishna Patrika, began in 1908.
198.tq: Find the swapped year among newspapers from the same nationalist period.

198.s:
With reference to the following newspapers, consider the statements:
1. Swadesamitran was a Tamil newspaper founded by G. Subramania Iyer.
2. Krishna Patrika was founded by Konda Venkatappayya and Dasu Narayana Rao, with Mutnuri Krishna Rao as editor.
3. Andhra Patrika was founded by Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
198.x: All three statements are correct. Swadesamitran was a Tamil paper of G. Subramania Iyer; Krishna Patrika had the stated founders and editor; and Andhra Patrika was founded by Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao.
198.tq: Check each founder–language–editor combination independently.

198.s: Krishna Patrika was first published on 1 February 1902 at:
198.x: Krishna Patrika began publication on 1 February 1902 at Machilipatnam.
198.tq: Distinguish the journal’s place of origin from the later centres of other Telugu newspapers.

198.s:
Arrange the following political associations in chronological order:
A. Indian Association
B. East India Association
C. Madras Mahajana Sabha
D. Landholders’ Society
198.x: The Landholders’ Society was founded in 1838, the East India Association in 1866, the Indian Association in 1876 and the Madras Mahajana Sabha in 1884.
198.tq: Fix the earliest and latest associations first, then place the two middle dates.

198.s:
Which of the following gives the correct chronological sequence of the early political associations?
1. Bangabhasha Prakasika Sabha
2. Bengal British India Society
3. British Indian Association
4. Madras Native Association and Bombay Association
198.x: The sequence is Bangabhasha Prakasika Sabha (1836), Bengal British India Society (1843), British Indian Association (1851), and Madras Native Association and Bombay Association (1852).
198.tq: Convert the dates into a straight ascending sequence.

198.s:
Which of the following is the correct chronological order after the formation of the Indian Association?
A. Madras Mahajana Sabha
B. Bombay Presidency Association
C. Indian National Congress
D. Indian Association
198.x: The Indian Association was founded in 1876, the Madras Mahajana Sabha in 1884, the Bombay Presidency Association and the Indian National Congress in 1885. The two 1885 bodies are placed in the order given in the established sequence.
198.tq: Anchor the 1876 association and then arrange the later 1884–1885 developments.

198.s: The Poona Sarvajanik Sabha petitioned the House of Commons in 1875 primarily for:
o: Reduction of the ICS age limit
Indian representation in the British Parliament
Abolition of the Vernacular Press Act
198.x: The Poona Sarvajanik Sabha asked for Indian representation in the British Parliament through its 1875 petition to the House of Commons.
198.tq: Match the association with the specific constitutional demand it advanced.

198.s: Who was the first person to spread national ideas in Andhra?
198.x: Gazula Lakshmi Narasu Chetty is credited with being the first to spread national ideas in Andhra.
198.tq: Distinguish the early Andhra propagator from later newspaper and association leaders.

198.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Surendranath Banerjee:
1. He passed the ICS examination in 1869.
2. He was initially disqualified over an age dispute and was later reinstated.
3. He was dismissed in 1874 on the ground of a minor irregularity.
4. He was never involved in opposition to the reduction of the ICS age limit.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
198.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because Banerjee toured the country against the reduction of the ICS maximum age from 21 to 19.
198.tq: Identify the single reversal in an otherwise chronological biographical sequence.
198.sec: Surendranath Banerjee - ICS episode, Indian Association, National Conference  [other exams]

198.s: The British reduction of the maximum age for the Indian Civil Service from 21 to 19 was criticised because it:
o: Transferred the examination from Britain to India
Made it more difficult for Indians to enter the service
Allowed only Indians to enter the ICS
198.x: The reduction from 21 to 19 was viewed as a measure to exclude Indians from the ICS, and Surendranath Banerjee campaigned against it.
198.tq: Read the policy effect as an exclusionary administrative measure.
198.sec: Surendranath Banerjee - ICS episode, Indian Association, National Conference  [other exams]

198.s: Surendranath Banerjee’s tour in connection with the ICS age issue reached Andhra in:
198.x: Surendranath Banerjee’s campaign tour against the reduction of the ICS age limit reached Andhra in 1878.
198.tq: Distinguish the tour year from the years of the Indian Association and National Conference.
198.sec: Surendranath Banerjee - ICS episode, Indian Association, National Conference  [other exams]

198.s: Which one of the following statements about the Indian National Conference is correct?
o: It was convened by Surendranath Banerjee in 1883 and 1885 and later merged with the INC.
It was convened only once in 1895 at Poona.
It was founded by Lytton in 1877 to support the colonial administration.
It was convened by Tilak in 1881 and remained separate from the INC.
198.x: Surendranath Banerjee convened the Indian National Conference in 1883 and 1885; it subsequently merged with the Indian National Congress.
198.tq: Use the founder, two conference years and merger as a combined identifying set.
198.sec: Surendranath Banerjee - ICS episode, Indian Association, National Conference  [other exams]

198.s: Surendranath Banerjee was known by the title:
198.x: Surendranath Banerjee was known as Rashtraguru. He also edited The Bengalee and presided over the INC at Poona in 1895 and Ahmedabad in 1902.
198.tq: Match the political leader with his distinctive honorific.
198.sec: Surendranath Banerjee - ICS episode, Indian Association, National Conference  [other exams]

198.s: Surendranath Banerjee presided over the Indian National Congress at:
198.x: Surendranath Banerjee presided over the Congress session at Poona in 1895 and at Ahmedabad in 1902.
198.tq: Pair the president with both session locations and years.
198.sec: Surendranath Banerjee - ICS episode, Indian Association, National Conference  [other exams]

198.s: Which of the following was NOT an unintended result of British rule that helped the growth of Indian nationalism?
o: Uniform laws and English as a link language
Development of railways, telegraph and postal communication
Complete economic prosperity of Indian artisans
198.x: British rule produced political, administrative and economic integration through railways, telegraph, post and uniform laws, but economic exploitation ruined many artisans rather than bringing them prosperity.
198.tq: Reject the extreme economic claim that reverses the nationalist critique.
198.sec: Factors of nationalism - western education, press, history-writing, economic critique  [other exams]

198.s:
Which combination best explains the contribution of Western education to the growth of Indian nationalism?
1. It introduced Indians to Western liberal ideas.
2. It helped English function as a link language.
3. It created a new educated middle class of lawyers, journalists and teachers.
4. It ended all racial discrimination in administration.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
198.x: Western education spread liberal ideas, promoted English as a link language and produced an educated middle class. It did not end racial discrimination.
198.tq: Separate the genuine institutional effects of education from an absolute social claim.
198.sec: Factors of nationalism - western education, press, history-writing, economic critique  [other exams]

198.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
198.x: Veeresalingam’s Vivekavardhani, published in 1874, represented the contribution of socio-religious reform and the press to nationalism.
198.tq: Check both the publication and its associated reformer before selecting the pair.
198.sec: Factors of nationalism - western education, press, history-writing, economic critique  [other exams]

198.s: The rediscovery of India’s past contributed to nationalism mainly by:
o: Encouraging Indians to reject all modern education
198.x: The rediscovery and reinterpretation of India’s past gave Indians a sense of self-confidence and historical pride.
198.tq: Match the cultural factor with its stated psychological effect.
198.sec: Factors of nationalism - western education, press, history-writing, economic critique  [other exams]

198.s: Which of the following was NOT listed as a reaction that stimulated Indian nationalism?
o: Universal acceptance of Indians as equals by the colonial state
Inspiration from the American, French and Italian movements
Economic exploitation through the drain of wealth
198.x: Economic exploitation, racial arrogance, Lytton’s policies, the Ilbert Bill controversy and foreign nationalist movements stimulated nationalism. Universal racial equality was not a feature of colonial rule.
198.tq: Identify the option that contradicts the stated experience of colonial rule.
198.sec: Factors of nationalism - western education, press, history-writing, economic critique  [other exams]

198.s:
Assertion (A): British rule unintentionally helped create conditions for the growth of Indian nationalism.
Reason (R): Railways, telegraph, postal services and uniform laws promoted political, administrative and economic unification.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
198.x: Both statements are true, and the integrative infrastructure and uniform legal-administrative framework directly explain how British rule unintentionally facilitated nationalism.
198.tq: Test whether the reason directly explains the broad historical assertion.
198.sec: Factors of nationalism - western education, press, history-writing, economic critique  [other exams]

198.s: The Delhi Durbar of 1877 was significant because it:
o: Announced the end of the Second Afghan War
Proclaimed Queen Victoria as Empress of India
198.x: The Delhi Durbar of 1877 proclaimed Queen Victoria as Empress of India, even as millions were suffering in the famine of 1876–78.
198.tq: Match the ceremonial event with its constitutional-symbolic significance.

198.s:
Consider the following statements about Lytton’s policies:
1. The Vernacular Press Act of 1878 restricted the Indian-language press.
2. The Arms Act of 1878 disarmed Indians but exempted Europeans.
3. The Second Afghan War of 1878–80 placed a financial burden on Indian revenues.
4. The famine of 1876–78 occurred during a period of widespread prosperity.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
198.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because the famine caused widespread starvation while the Delhi Durbar was held in 1877.
198.tq: Find the statement that reverses the social and economic context of a policy period.

198.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with respect to Lytton’s measures?
1. Vernacular Press Act — 1878
2. Arms Act — 1878
3. Second Afghan War — 1878–80
4. Delhi Durbar — 1877
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
198.x: All four pairs are correct: the Vernacular Press Act and Arms Act were enacted in 1878, the Second Afghan War lasted from 1878 to 1880, and the Delhi Durbar took place in 1877.
198.tq: Verify each date against the associated measure before choosing the complete combination.

198.s: The early political associations contributed to the rise of the Indian National Congress chiefly by:
o: Restricting political activity exclusively to princely states
Training the English-educated class in petitions, memorials and all-India coordination
Organising armed revolts against every colonial institution
198.x: These associations trained educated Indians in constitutional political methods such as petitions and memorials and promoted all-India coordination, leading to the formation of the INC in 1885.
198.tq: Apply the institutional legacy of the associations to the emergence of the INC.

198.s:
Which of the following statements about the early political associations is correct?
1. They were often led by landlords or the urban elite.
2. They were generally regional in character.
3. They immediately represented all sections of Indian society equally.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
198.x: The early associations were largely led by landlords or the urban elite and were regional in character. They did not immediately represent all sections of society equally.
198.tq: Reject the overbroad claim of complete social representation.

198.s:
Which of the following associations is correctly matched with its year and regional significance?
1. Madras Native Association — 1852
2. Madras Mahajana Sabha — 1884
3. Krishna District Association — 1892
4. Bombay Presidency Association — 1885
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
198.x: All four associations and years are correctly matched. The first three were important links in the regional and Andhra-related development of pre-Congress political activity.
198.tq: Check each association–year pair and retain the complete set when no pair is displaced.

198.s: The Krishna District Association was modelled on:
o: The British Indian Association’s demand for separate electorates
The INC’s advice to form district bodies
The East India Association’s overseas branches
The Vernacular Press Act’s press committees
198.x: The Krishna District Association was modelled on the Indian National Congress’s advice to establish district-level political bodies.
198.tq: Identify the organisational model behind the regional association.

198.s:
Which one of the following represents the correct sequence of the principal Andhra-linked political associations?
A. Madras Native Association
B. Madras Mahajana Sabha
C. Krishna District Association
D. Indian National Congress
198.x: The Madras Native Association was founded in 1852, the Madras Mahajana Sabha in 1884, the Krishna District Association in 1892, and the Indian National Congress in 1885. However, in the stated principal association sequence, the INC follows the 1884 Sabha and precedes the 1892 district body; therefore the historically chronological order is A, B, D, C.
198.tq: Check every date rather than accepting a sequence built from the order of presentation.

199.s: The first session of the Indian National Congress was shifted from Poona to Bombay because of
199.x: The proposed session at Poona was shifted to Bombay because of a cholera outbreak.
199.tq: Test the specific cause of a venue change rather than merely recalling the final venue.
199.sec: Founding - year, venue shift, delegates, president, Viceroy  [APPSC]

199.s: At which of the following places was the first session of the Indian National Congress held?
199.x: The inaugural session met at the Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College in Bombay.
199.tq: Distinguish the exact institutional venue from the city of the session.
199.sec: Founding - year, venue shift, delegates, president, Viceroy  [APPSC]

199.s: Who served as the General Secretary of the Indian National Congress at its foundation?
199.x: A.O. Hume became the General Secretary of the Indian National Congress at its foundation.
199.tq: Ask who performed the organisational role instead of who presided over the session.
199.sec: Founding - year, venue shift, delegates, president, Viceroy  [APPSC]

199.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the first session of the Indian National Congress:
1. It was attended by 72 delegates.
2. W.C. Bonnerjee presided over it.
3. A.O. Hume served as its General Secretary.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
199.x: All three statements are correct: the first session had 72 delegates, was presided over by W.C. Bonnerjee, and had A.O. Hume as General Secretary.
199.tq: Check all three linked facts about the inaugural session before selecting the combined code.
199.sec: Founding - year, venue shift, delegates, president, Viceroy  [APPSC]

199.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the composition of the delegates to the first session of the Indian National Congress?
o: 54 Hindus and 2 Muslims, besides Jains and Parsis
36 Hindus and 36 Muslims, besides Jains and Parsis
54 Muslims and 2 Hindus, besides Sikhs and Christians
72 Hindus, with no delegates from other communities
199.x: The 72 delegates included 54 Hindus and 2 Muslims, along with Jains and Parsis.
199.tq: Test composition figures through a precise membership comparison.
199.sec: Founding - year, venue shift, delegates, president, Viceroy  [APPSC]

199.s: The delegates to the first session of the Indian National Congress were drawn mainly from which occupational groups?
199.x: Most delegates were lawyers, journalists and teachers.
199.tq: Identify the social-professional base of the early Congress from closely related occupational groups.
199.sec: Founding - year, venue shift, delegates, president, Viceroy  [APPSC]

199.s: Which of the following was NOT one of the demands of the first session of the Indian National Congress?
o: Simultaneous ICS examinations in England and India
Immediate establishment of complete provincial autonomy
Opposition to the annexation of Upper Burma
Election in place of nomination for councils
199.x: The first session demanded simultaneous ICS examinations, elected councils, opposition to the annexation of Upper Burma and reduction of military expenditure. Immediate complete provincial autonomy was not listed among its four demands.
199.tq: Find the one demand that falls outside the specific four-point programme.
199.sec: Founding - year, venue shift, delegates, president, Viceroy  [APPSC]

199.s:
Which of the following combinations correctly represents two demands of the first session of the Indian National Congress?
1. Simultaneous ICS examinations in England and India
2. Reduction in military expenditure
3. Annexation of Upper Burma
4. Nomination instead of election to councils
199.x: The session demanded simultaneous ICS examinations and cuts in military expenditure. It opposed the annexation of Upper Burma and sought election instead of nomination to councils.
199.tq: Reverse the wording of two demands to detect the false alternatives.
199.sec: Founding - year, venue shift, delegates, president, Viceroy  [APPSC]

199.s:
Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
A. Private meeting of 17 persons after the Theosophical Convention at Madras
B. First session of the Indian National Congress
C. Second session of the Indian National Congress
D. Formation of Hume's Indian National Union
199.x: The private meeting followed the December 1884 Theosophical Convention, Hume's Indian National Union preceded the Congress, the first session was held in 1885, and the second in 1886.
199.tq: Anchor the sequence around the 1884 origin and the 1885–1886 Congress sessions.
199.sec: Founding - year, venue shift, delegates, president, Viceroy  [APPSC]

199.s: The origin of the Indian National Congress is associated with a private meeting of how many persons after the Theosophical Convention at Madras in December 1884?
199.x: A private meeting of 17 persons after the Theosophical Convention at Madras is associated with the early origin of the Congress.
199.tq: Use the exact small-number detail rather than confusing it with delegate figures.
199.sec: Founding - year, venue shift, delegates, president, Viceroy  [APPSC]

199.s: Which organisation was associated with A.O. Hume before the establishment of the Indian National Congress?
199.x: A.O. Hume's Indian National Union is identified as one of the organisational origins of the Congress.
199.tq: Distinguish Hume's organisation from other pre-Congress political bodies.
199.sec: Founding - year, venue shift, delegates, president, Viceroy  [APPSC]

199.s: The credit for giving the organisation the name “Indian National Congress” is generally associated with
199.x: The name “Indian National Congress” is credited to Dadabhai Naoroji.
199.tq: Separate the person credited with the nomenclature from the founder-organiser and first president.
199.sec: Founding - year, venue shift, delegates, president, Viceroy  [APPSC]

199.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. William Wedderburn — British founding member
2. Justice John Jardine — British founding member
3. A.O. Hume — General Secretary at the foundation
4. Dadabhai Naoroji — President of the first session
199.x: William Wedderburn and Justice John Jardine were British founding members, and Hume was General Secretary. Dadabhai Naoroji did not preside over the first session; W.C. Bonnerjee did.
199.tq: Use the founder-role swap trap to reject the statement assigning the first presidency to Naoroji.
199.sec: Founding - year, venue shift, delegates, president, Viceroy  [APPSC]

199.s: Which one of the following sets contains only Andhra delegates to the first session of the Indian National Congress?
o: P. Anandacharlu, P. Rangaiah Naidu, Nyapathi Subbarao, Gutti Kesava Pillai and Venkata Subbarayudu
P. Anandacharlu, Dadabhai Naoroji, Nyapathi Subbarao, George Yule and Venkata Subbarayudu
P. Rangaiah Naidu, William Wedderburn, Gutti Kesava Pillai, Pherozeshah Mehta and Nyapathi Subbarao
Nyapathi Subbarao, W.C. Bonnerjee, P. Anandacharlu, Gutti Kesava Pillai and Dinshaw Wacha
199.x: The Andhra delegates listed were P. Anandacharlu, P. Rangaiah Naidu, Nyapathi Subbarao, Gutti Kesava Pillai and Venkata Subbarayudu.
199.tq: Start from the sure regional names and eliminate options containing national Congress presidents.
199.sec: Founding - year, venue shift, delegates, president, Viceroy  [APPSC]

199.s:
Which of the following statements about A.O. Hume is correct?
1. He was a retired member of the Indian Civil Service.
2. He was demoted in 1879 after a clash with Lord Lytton.
3. He retired in 1882 and settled in Shimla.
4. He drew the idea of local self-government from Lord Ripon.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
199.x: All four statements describe the background of A.O. Hume as given: his ICS career, clash and demotion under Lytton, retirement and settlement at Shimla, and influence of Ripon's local self-government policy.
199.tq: Verify each biographical detail separately before choosing the complete combination.
199.sec: Founding - year, venue shift, delegates, president, Viceroy  [APPSC]

199.s: A.O. Hume was considered closer politically to which group than to the Calcutta leaders?
199.x: Hume was regarded as closer to the Bombay-Poona groups than to the leaders of Calcutta.
199.tq: Test the regional political association of a person through a close geographical contrast.
199.sec: Founding - year, venue shift, delegates, president, Viceroy  [APPSC]

199.s: The second session of the Indian National Congress is associated with approximately how many delegates?
199.x: The second session at Calcutta in 1886 is cited with 436 delegates.
199.tq: Distinguish the sharply increased second-session attendance from the 72 delegates of 1885.
199.sec: INC sessions → president + venue (early sessions and FIRSTs)  [APPSC]

199.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
199.x: William Wedderburn presided over the 1889 session held at Bombay, not Calcutta. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
199.tq: Check the venue against the president and year, especially where adjacent sessions are involved.
199.sec: INC sessions → president + venue (early sessions and FIRSTs)  [APPSC]

199.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The 1890 session was held at Calcutta under Pherozeshah Mehta.
2. Kadambini Ganguly addressed the 1890 session.
3. Kadambini Ganguly was the first woman graduate of Calcutta University.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
199.x: All three statements are correct. Pherozeshah Mehta presided at Calcutta in 1890, and Kadambini Ganguly addressed that session; she was the first woman graduate of Calcutta University.
199.tq: Combine the session detail with the biographical identity of the woman who addressed it.
199.sec: INC sessions → president + venue (early sessions and FIRSTs)  [APPSC]

199.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
199.x: P. Anandacharlu presided over the Nagpur session of 1891, the seventh session. Sayani presided in 1896, Dinshaw Wacha in 1901, and Naoroji in Lahore in 1893.
199.tq: Match the year, venue and president while using neighbouring sessions as distractors.
199.sec: INC sessions → president + venue (early sessions and FIRSTs)  [APPSC]

199.s: At which session of the Indian National Congress was “Vande Mataram” sung for the first time?
199.x: “Vande Mataram” was first sung at the Calcutta session of 1896, presided over by Rahimtulla M. Sayani; Rabindranath Tagore sang it.
199.tq: Link the cultural first with its exact session rather than the more famous inaugural sessions.
199.sec: INC sessions → president + venue (early sessions and FIRSTs)  [APPSC]

199.s: Who made the first appearance on the Indian National Congress platform at the 1901 Calcutta session?
199.x: Mahatma Gandhi made his first appearance on the Congress platform at the Calcutta session of 1901.
199.tq: Test the specific first appearance associated with a session instead of a later leadership role.
199.sec: INC sessions → president + venue (early sessions and FIRSTs)  [APPSC]

199.s: Who was the first Telugu woman to attend a session of the Indian National Congress?
199.x: Ponaka Kanakamma is identified as the first Telugu woman to attend an Indian National Congress session.
199.tq: Use the regional identity qualifier to distinguish this first from national-level women leaders.
199.sec: INC sessions → president + venue (early sessions and FIRSTs)  [APPSC]

199.s: Who was the youngest president of the Indian National Congress, according to the cited early Congress records?
199.x: Maulana Abul Kalam Azad became the youngest Congress president at the age of 35 at the special Delhi session of 1923.
199.tq: Distinguish the age-based “youngest” record from the later presidents associated with youth and radical politics.
199.sec: INC sessions → president + venue (early sessions and FIRSTs)  [APPSC]

199.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched regarding Dadabhai Naoroji and W.C. Bonnerjee?
1. Dadabhai Naoroji — Calcutta 1886, Lahore 1893 and Calcutta 1906
2. W.C. Bonnerjee — Bombay 1885 and Allahabad 1892
3. Dadabhai Naoroji — two presidencies
4. W.C. Bonnerjee — three presidencies
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
199.x: Naoroji presided three times—in Calcutta 1886, Lahore 1893 and Calcutta 1906—while Bonnerjee presided twice, at Bombay 1885 and Allahabad 1892.
199.tq: Use the presidency-count trap by checking both the locations and the number of terms.
199.sec: PERSON - Called as/Known as (Grand Old Man of India) and number of presidencies  [APPSC]

205.sec: Indian Councils Act 1909 - name, electorates, first Indian on Executive Council  [APPSC]

205.s: The Morley-Minto Reforms were introduced mainly to:

Transfer the capital from Delhi to Calcutta
Abolish princely states and establish a republic

205.s: Which one of the following was NOT an aim of the All-India Muslim League in its early phase?
o: Keeping Muslims away from the Congress
Launching an immediate armed revolt against British rule
Promoting loyalty to the British Empire

205.s: The Lucknow Congress Session of December 1916 was presided over by:
205.x: Ambika Charan Majumdar presided over the Lucknow Congress Session of December 1916.
205.tq: Avoid swapping the session president with the principal brokers of the pact.

205.s:
The Lucknow Congress Session of 1916 was historically significant because it witnessed:
1. Reunion of Moderates and Extremists
2. The Congress-League alliance
3. Tilak's return to the Congress fold
Which of the statements given above are correct?
205.x: The 1916 session marked the reunion of Moderates and Extremists, Tilak's return and the Congress-League alliance represented by the Lucknow Pact.
205.tq: Identify all historically linked features of a landmark session.

205.s: The Muslim League delegation associated with the Lucknow Pact was led by the:
205.x: The League's Young Party, associated with Jinnah and the Ali Brothers, led the League side in the Lucknow Pact negotiations.
205.tq: Discriminate between similarly named political groupings.

205.s:
Who among the following were important brokers of the Lucknow Pact?
1. B.G. Tilak
2. M.A. Jinnah
3. Annie Besant
Which of the statements given above are correct?
205.x: B.G. Tilak and M.A. Jinnah were principal brokers, while Annie Besant also worked for the Pact.
205.tq: Use the complete set of negotiators rather than selecting only the two principal names.

205.s: Under the Lucknow Pact, the Congress accepted which major concession to the Muslim League?
o: Direct British appointment of Muslim representatives
205.x: The Congress accepted separate electorates for Muslims, which was a major concession under the Lucknow Pact.
205.tq: Identify the specific concession rather than the general objective of the pact.

205.s: Under the Lucknow Pact, a bill concerning a particular community could not be passed if opposed by what proportion of the members of that community?
205.x: The communal veto clause required that three-fourths of the members of the concerned community must not oppose the bill; if three-fourths opposed it, the bill could not be passed.
205.tq: Treat a constitutional fraction as an exact figure, not an approximate majority.

205.s:
Which of the following formed part of the Lucknow Pact proposals?
1. Separation of the executive from the judiciary
2. Elected majority in provincial legislatures
3. Self-government as a common goal
Which of the statements given above are correct?
205.x: The Pact accepted self-government as its goal and included separation of the executive and judiciary and elected majorities in provincial legislatures.
205.tq: Combine institutional provisions with the shared political objective.

205.s: Which one of the following statements about the Congress and the Muslim League in 1916 is correct?
o: The League abandoned its separate political agenda permanently.
The Congress rejected all communal representation.
They merged into a single organisation with one annual session.
They held separate annual sessions despite reaching an agreement through the Lucknow Pact.
205.x: The Congress and the League continued to hold separate annual sessions with distinct agendas even after the Lucknow Pact.
205.tq: Separate political alliance from organisational merger.

205.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
205.x: The Surat Split occurred in 1907. The partition was annulled in 1911, the August Declaration was made in 1917 and the Swaraj Party was formed in 1923.
205.tq: Match each event with its exact year and reject shifted dates.

205.s: Partition of Bengal was annulled on 12 December 1911, and the imperial capital was shifted from:
205.x: The annulment was announced through King George V, and the capital was shifted from Calcutta to Delhi.

205.s:
Which of the following events was associated with the tenure of Lord Minto II as Viceroy?

2. Surat Split
3. Newspapers Act
4. Muzaffarpur case
Which of the statements given above are correct?
205.x: Lord Minto II was Viceroy from 1905 to 1910, during which the Muslim League was formed in 1906, the Surat Split occurred in 1907, and the Newspapers Act and Muzaffarpur case occurred in 1908.

205.s: Lord Minto II held which office during the period 1905–1910?
o: President of the Viceroy's Executive Council

o: Secretary of State for India in London
205.x: John Morley was the Secretary of State for India, based in London, and Lord Minto was the Viceroy in India.
205.tq: Apply the location-and-office distinction between British authorities in London and India.

205.s: Who is known as the “Father of the Communal Electorate” in British India?
205.x: Lord Minto is known as the Father of the Communal Electorate because the reforms associated with him introduced separate electorates for Muslims.
205.tq: Use the person–policy association and distinguish Minto from other Viceroys.

205.s: Which one of the following best describes the long-term political consequence of the Indian Councils Act, 1909?
o: It abolished communal representation in legislatures.
It legally institutionalised communalism and contributed to the growth of the Two-Nation Theory.
It established complete responsible government at the Centre.
It introduced universal adult franchise in British India.
205.x: The 1909 Act legally institutionalised communal representation, thereby strengthening communal politics and contributing to the emergence of the Two-Nation Theory.
205.tq: Identify the precise consequence rather than being distracted by extreme constitutional claims.

205.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Lucknow Pact, 1916:
1. It represented a short-term phase of Hindu-Muslim political unity.
2. Congress accepted separate electorates and weightage for Muslims.
3. Its provisions helped legitimise communal politics in the long term.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
205.x: All three statements are correct. The Pact produced temporary Congress-League unity, but Congress’s acceptance of separate electorates and weightage also legitimised communal political arrangements.
205.tq: Test both the immediate achievement and the long-term criticism of the same agreement.

205.s: The principal criticism of the Congress’s acceptance of separate electorates in the Lucknow Pact was that it
o: legitimised communal politics and laid groundwork for the Partition of India
rejected all forms of Muslim political representation
ended cooperation with the Muslim League immediately
transferred the capital from Delhi to Calcutta
205.x: The criticism was that acceptance of separate electorates and weightage legitimised communal politics and ultimately provided part of the groundwork for Partition.
205.tq: Apply the critique to the political consequence instead of recalling only the Pact’s short-term success.

205.s: With reference to the Muslim League during 1912–1924, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: It was dominated entirely by British officials.
It was led exclusively by Hindu nationalists.
It was dominated by younger Muslim nationalists whose nationalism nevertheless viewed politics communally.
It had ceased to exist as a political organisation.
205.x: During 1912–1924, younger Muslim nationalists exercised growing influence in the League. Their nationalism was still shaped by a communal view of politics.
205.tq: Distinguish a qualified description from absolute alternatives such as “entirely” and “exclusively”.

205.x: Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao and Bodi Narayana Rao were arrested on 18 July 1908 and are identified as the first Telugu political prisoners in this context.

206.x: Barindra Kumar Ghosh wrote the revolutionary manual Mukti Kon Pathe in 1906.

2. The procession passed through Chandni Chowk.
3. Lord Hardinge was killed in the attack.
Which of the statements given above are correct?

o: Muzaffarpur Conspiracy Case — Khudiram Bose and Prafulla Chaki
