One-third of the crop instead of one-half
The entire crop without payment of rent
216.x: The bargadars demanded two-thirds of the produce, reducing the landlord’s share from one-half to one-third, with storage in their own godowns.
216.tq: Watch the reversed-share trap: the demand concerns the bargadar’s share, not the landlord’s share.
216.sec: Tebhaga - demand and province  [other exams]

216.s: Which legislation is associated with the outcome of the Tebhaga Movement?
216.x: The Bargadari Act of 1950 is associated with the outcome of the Tebhaga struggle.
216.tq: Match the movement with its later legislative outcome while rejecting earlier regional laws.
216.sec: Tebhaga - demand and province  [other exams]

216.s: Which of the following factors contributed to the limited short-run success of the Tebhaga Movement?
o: A government ban before the movement began and a famine in Gujarat
The transfer of the movement from Bengal to Hyderabad
Limited spread and the Hindu-Muslim rift
Complete support from all zamindars and the absence of peasant participation
216.x: The movement’s short-run success was limited by its restricted spread and the Hindu-Muslim rift.
216.tq: Identify the paired outcome factors rather than confusing them with causes of other movements.
216.sec: Tebhaga - demand and province  [other exams]

216.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the broad historical transition in Indian peasant movements?
o: From sporadic revolts against zamindars and moneylenders to Gandhian satyagraha and then organised Kisan Sabhas
From organised Kisan Sabhas to sporadic revolts and then to plantation movements
From tribal movements to exclusive urban labour movements
From revolutionary violence directly to constitutional reforms without mass participation
216.x: Before 1917, peasant movements were often sporadic revolts against zamindars and moneylenders; they later developed into Gandhian satyagraha and organised Kisan Sabhas in the 1930s.
216.tq: Recognise the chronological sequence of changing forms of agrarian mobilisation.
216.sec: Universal angles

216.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched in relation to peasant movements in Gujarat?
o: Bardoli — Baba Ramchandra and Madari Pasi
Kheda — Ishan Chandra Roy and Shambhu Pal
Bardoli — Ali Musliyar and Kunjahammad Haji
216.x: Kheda in Gujarat was associated with Patel and Mohanlal Pandya. The other pairs combine leaders from Uttar Pradesh, Bengal and Malabar movements.
216.tq: Use the region first, then verify the associated leaders.
216.sec: Peasant movements - region, year and chronology  [APPSC]

216.s: The Telangana peasant movement of 1946–51 was associated with which combination?
o: Hyderabad, the Communist Party of India and the Andhra Mahasabha
Bengal, the Indian National Congress and the Agrarian League
Gujarat, the Congress Socialist Party and the All India Trade Union Congress
Mewar, the Muslim League and the Oudh Kisan Sabha
216.x: The Telangana armed struggle occurred in Hyderabad during 1946–51 and was associated with the Communist Party of India and the Andhra Mahasabha.
216.tq: Combine the region, period and organisations to avoid confusing Telangana with Tebhaga.
216.sec: Peasant movements - region, year and chronology  [APPSC]

216.s: The anti-zamindari struggles in Andhra Pradesh mentioned in connection with land reform included which of the following?
216.x: The Nellore and Munagala anti-zamindari struggles are highlighted as important Andhra-related agrarian movements. Land reform demands also contributed to the Madras Zamindari Abolition Bill of 1947.
216.tq: Identify the Andhra-specific locations rather than selecting nationally prominent movement centres.
216.sec: Universal angles

216.s: The Madras Zamindari Abolition Bill was introduced in which year in the context of land reform demands?
216.x: Land reform demands associated with agrarian struggles led to the Madras Zamindari Abolition Bill in 1947.
216.tq: Distinguish the bill’s year from the years of the Kisan Sabha and Bargadari legislation.
216.sec: Universal angles

216.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Moplah Movement is correct?
o: It occurred in Maharashtra in 1875 and targeted moneylenders from Gujarat and Marwar.
It occurred in Bengal in 1946 and was led by bargadars demanding two-thirds of the crop.
It occurred in Gujarat in 1928 as a non-violent Congress campaign against revenue enhancement.
It occurred in Malabar in 1921 and involved Muslim tenants against landlords and the British.
216.x: The Moplah Movement took place in Malabar in 1921 and involved Muslim tenants in conflict with landlords and the British.
216.tq: Separate Moplah from Tebhaga, Deccan and Bardoli through region, year and target.
216.sec: Peasant movements - region, year and chronology  [APPSC]

216.s: Which of the following pairs of leaders was associated with the Moplah Movement?
o: Gauri Shankar Mishra and Indra Narayan Dwivedi
Variyankunnathu Kunjahammad Haji and Ali Musliyar
Sitaram Das and Vijay Singh Pathik
216.x: Variyankunnathu Kunjahammad Haji and Ali Musliyar were associated with the Moplah Movement in Malabar.
216.tq: Match the movement with its distinctive leadership rather than its general social base.
216.sec: Peasant movements - region, year and chronology  [APPSC]

219.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Revolt)
a. Santhal Hul
b. Munda Ulgulan
c. Kol/Larka rising
d. Khond rising

List-II (Leader)
i. Chakra Bisoi
ii. Birsa Munda
iii. Budhu Bhagat
iv. Sidhu and Kanhu Murmu

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
219.x: Santhal Hul was led by Sidhu and Kanhu Murmu, Munda Ulgulan by Birsa Munda, the Kol rising by Budhu Bhagat and the Khond rising by Chakra Bisoi.
219.tq: Start from the sure leader–revolt pairs and eliminate the codes.
219.sec: Tribal revolt → leader + region + present state  [APPSC]

219.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
219.x: The Bhil rising occurred in Khandesh, in present-day Maharashtra. Bhumij was associated with Manbhum, Tamar with Tamar in Jharkhand and Paika with Khurda in Odisha.
219.tq: Use the region column to distinguish closely related tribal revolts.
219.sec: Tribal revolt → leader + region + present state  [APPSC]

219.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Bhumij rising — Ganga Narayan
2. Paika Rebellion — Bakshi Jagabandhu
3. Ramosi uprising — Chittur Singh, Umaji Naik and Bapu Trimbakji Sawant
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
219.x: All three pairs are correctly matched. Ganga Narayan led the Bhumij rising, Bakshi Jagabandhu led the Paika Rebellion and the listed leaders were associated with the Ramosi uprisings.
219.tq: Check each leader against the corresponding revolt before selecting the coded combination.
219.sec: Tribal revolt → leader + region + present state  [APPSC]

219.s: The Tamar tribal rising is associated with which one of the following combinations?
o: Oraon tribes and Tamar in Jharkhand
Bhil tribes and Khandesh in Maharashtra
219.x: The Tamar rising was associated with the Oraon tribes and the Tamar region of present-day Jharkhand. Its recorded period was 1789–1832.
219.tq: Test the tribe–region association rather than relying only on the revolt name.
219.sec: Tribal revolt → leader + region + present state  [APPSC]

219.s: The British invited the Santhals to settle and cultivate the Rajmahal Hills primarily after they had failed to control the:
219.x: The British were unable to control the Paharias of the Rajmahal Hills and therefore invited the Santhals to settle and cultivate the area.
219.tq: Identify the immediate colonial administrative response to resistance in the Rajmahal Hills.
219.sec: Santhal Hul - Paharias, Rajmahal Hills, outcome  [APPSC]

219.s: The tract in the Rajmahal Hills demarcated for Santhal settlement was known as:
219.x: The tract demarcated for Santhal settlement and cultivation was called Damin-i-Koh. Kolhan was associated with the administration of the Kol region.
219.tq: Use exact administrative terminology to distinguish neighbouring tribal regions.
219.sec: Santhal Hul - Paharias, Rajmahal Hills, outcome  [APPSC]

219.s: The Santhal Hul began at Bhognadih on:
219.x: The Santhal Hul began at Bhognadih on 30 June 1855, observed as Hul Divas.
219.tq: Treat the place and exact date as a paired chronology clue.
219.sec: Santhal Hul - Paharias, Rajmahal Hills, outcome  [APPSC]

219.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Santhal Hul:
1. About 30,000 Santhals proclaimed Santhal Raj.
2. The revolt was crushed in 1856.
3. More than 15,000 Santhals were killed.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
219.x: All three statements are correct. The movement involved about 30,000 Santhals, was crushed in 1856 and caused more than 15,000 deaths.
219.tq: Verify the numerical and outcome statements together before choosing the coded option.
219.sec: Santhal Hul - Paharias, Rajmahal Hills, outcome  [APPSC]

219.s: Which of the following groups was associated with the leadership of the Santhal Hul in addition to Sidhu and Kanhu Murmu?
o: Chand, Bhairav and the sisters Phulo-Jhano
Jatra Bhagat, Govind Giri and Motilal Tejawat
Umaji Naik, Chittur Singh and Narayan Rao
Ganga Narayan, Budhu Bhagat and Tirot Sing
219.x: Chand and Bhairav, along with the sisters Phulo and Jhano, were associated with the leadership of the Santhal Hul.
219.tq: Distinguish members of one revolt’s leadership from leaders of other tribal movements.
219.sec: Santhal Hul - Paharias, Rajmahal Hills, outcome  [APPSC]

219.s: Which one of the following was an important cause of the Santhal Hul?
o: Oppression by zamindars, moneylenders and police
The abolition of the Khuntkatti system by the Santhals themselves
The transfer of Upper Assam to Purandar Singh
The introduction of bonded labour in Mewar
219.x: The Santhals faced oppression by zamindars, moneylenders, commonly called dikus, and the police. The Khuntkatti issue belonged principally to the Munda movement.
219.tq: Match the cause with the revolt instead of the similarly worded causes of other movements.
219.sec: Santhal Hul - Paharias, Rajmahal Hills, outcome  [APPSC]

219.s: After the Santhal Hul, which one of the following developments took place?
o: Santhal Parganas became a separate district with special laws protecting tribal land.
Upper Assam was restored to the Santhal leaders.
The Chotanagpur Tenancy Act was enacted in 1876.
Kolhan was placed under the Munda-Manki system immediately after the Ulgulan.
219.x: After the Hul, Santhal Parganas was created as a separate district and special laws were introduced to protect tribal land. The Chotanagpur Tenancy Act came later, in 1908.
219.tq: Find the correct post-revolt administrative consequence among closely related outcomes.
219.sec: Santhal Hul - Paharias, Rajmahal Hills, outcome  [APPSC]

219.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Santhal Parganas Tenancy Act is dated to 1876 in the cited chronology.
2. The current Santhal Parganas Tenancy Act is from 1949.
3. Santhal Parganas was created before the Santhal Hul.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
219.x: The 1876 date is associated with the Santhal Parganas Tenancy Act and the current Act is from 1949. Santhal Parganas was created after the Hul, so statement 3 is false.
219.tq: Spot the reversed before–after relationship in the third statement.
219.sec: Santhal Hul - Paharias, Rajmahal Hills, outcome  [APPSC]

219.s: Birsa Munda was born in:
219.x: Birsa Munda was born in 1875. He led the Ulgulan in 1899–1900.
219.tq: Separate the leader’s birth year from the years of his movement and its legal consequence.
219.sec: Birsa Munda - title, region, reform, Ulgulan, death  [APPSC]

219.s: Birsa Munda’s religious movement, which blended Munda tradition with Hinduism and Christianity, was known as:
219.x: Birsa Munda founded the monotheist Birsait faith, which blended elements of Munda tradition, Hinduism and Christianity.
219.tq: Use the exact name of the reform movement to distinguish it from later Bhil and Oraon movements.
219.sec: Birsa Munda - title, region, reform, Ulgulan, death  [APPSC]

219.s: Which one of the following was NOT part of Birsa Munda’s social and religious reform programme?
o: Opposition to animal sacrifice and spirit worship
Promotion of the Khuntkatti joint landholding system
219.x: Birsa’s programme opposed liquor, witchcraft, animal sacrifice and spirit worship and promoted a monotheist faith. Khuntkatti was a landholding system whose destruction helped cause the revolt; it was not a religious reform practice.
219.tq: Find the option that changes a land-rights issue into a reform practice.
219.sec: Birsa Munda - title, region, reform, Ulgulan, death  [APPSC]

219.s: The immediate agrarian grievance behind Birsa Munda’s revolt was the destruction of the:
219.x: The revolt was caused in part by the destruction of the Khuntkatti joint landholding system by zamindars, thikadars and missionaries.
219.tq: Identify the precise institution affected instead of choosing a general tribal-administration term.
219.sec: Birsa Munda - title, region, reform, Ulgulan, death  [APPSC]

219.s:
Consider the following statements about the Ulgulan:
1. It took place during 1899–1900.
2. Its objective included Abua Raj, or self-rule.
3. About 6,000 Mundas participated in it.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
219.x: The Ulgulan occurred in 1899–1900, aimed at Abua Raj and involved about 6,000 Mundas.
219.tq: Combine date, objective and participation figures in a single movement profile.
219.sec: Birsa Munda - title, region, reform, Ulgulan, death  [APPSC]

219.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the final phase of Birsa Munda’s life?
o: He was captured in February 1900 and died in Ranchi jail in June 1900.
He was captured in June 1900 and died in Bhognadih jail in February 1901.
He surrendered in 1899 and died in Khurda jail in 1908.
He was executed in 1905 after the enactment of the Chotanagpur Tenancy Act.
219.x: Birsa Munda was captured in February 1900 and died in Ranchi jail in June 1900.
219.tq: Use the sequence of capture, imprisonment and death to reject swapped dates and places.
219.sec: Birsa Munda - title, region, reform, Ulgulan, death  [APPSC]

219.s: The Chotanagpur Tenancy Act, 1908, associated with the consequences of the Ulgulan, is significant because it:
o: introduced the Eki movement in Mewar
created the Santhal Parganas as a separate district
handed Upper Assam to Purandar Singh
barred transfer of tribal land to non-tribals and recognised Khuntkatti rights
219.x: The Chotanagpur Tenancy Act, 1908, barred transfer of tribal land to non-tribals and recognised Khuntkatti rights.
219.tq: Infer the legal purpose from the land-rights grievance behind the movement.
219.sec: Birsa Munda - title, region, reform, Ulgulan, death  [APPSC]

219.s: Janjatiya Gaurav Divas is observed on 15 November in connection with the birth anniversary of:
219.x: 15 November, the birth anniversary of Birsa Munda, is observed as Janjatiya Gaurav Divas.
219.tq: Link the commemorative date with the correct tribal leader.
219.sec: Birsa Munda - title, region, reform, Ulgulan, death  [APPSC]

219.s: The Paika Rebellion of 1817 took place in:
219.x: The Paika Rebellion of 1817 took place in Khurda in present-day Odisha.
219.tq: Use the revolt–region association to distinguish Paika, Santhal, Bhil and Eki movements.

219.s:
Which of the following was a major grievance of the Paikas in 1817?
1. Loss of rent-free lands after the British conquest of 1803
2. Salt policy and revenue burdens
3. Destruction of the Khuntkatti system
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
219.x: The Paikas lost rent-free lands after the 1803 conquest and also resented salt policy and revenue burdens. Destruction of Khuntkatti was a Munda grievance.
219.tq: Separate the Paika-specific economic grievances from the Munda landholding issue.

219.s: The Paikas were traditionally:
o: moneylenders operating in the Rajmahal Hills
219.x: The Paikas were a traditional militia in the Khurda region whose rent-free lands were lost after the British conquest.
219.tq: Identify the occupational character of the group before testing the revolt’s causes.

219.s: The Ramosis of Maharashtra rose against British rule mainly after the:
o: enactment of the Chotanagpur Tenancy Act
219.x: The Ramosis rose against British rule after the fall of the Peshwa.
219.tq: Link the revolt to its immediate political background rather than to a later legal measure.

219.s:
Arrange the following tribal movements in chronological order of their beginning:
A. Santhal Hul
B. Ahom rebellion
C. Kol rising
D. Munda Ulgulan
219.x: The Ahom rebellion began in 1828, followed by the Kol rising in 1831–32, the Santhal Hul in 1855–56 and the Munda Ulgulan in 1899–1900.
219.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the middle movements by year.
219.sec: Revolt → year matching and chronology  [other exams]

219.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
219.x: The Ahom rebellion occurred in 1828, not 1855–56. The other pairs correspond to the stated periods of the respective movements.
219.tq: Look for the single year-range mismatch in a revolt chronology table.
219.sec: Revolt → year matching and chronology  [other exams]

219.s: The Khasi rising of 1829–33 was led by:
219.x: The Khasi rising of 1829–33 was associated with Tirot Sing. Gomadhar Konwar led the Ahom rebellion.
219.tq: Distinguish the leaders of the Khasi and Ahom risings through direct pairing.
219.sec: Revolt → year matching and chronology  [other exams]

219.s: The Ahom rebellion resulted in the Company handing over Upper Assam to:
219.x: The Ahom rebellion forced the East India Company to hand Upper Assam to Purandar Singh.
219.tq: Match the political outcome with the correct regional rebellion.
219.sec: Revolt → year matching and chronology  [other exams]

219.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Khasi rising is correct?
o: It began in 1899 as part of the Munda Ulgulan.
The standard chronology places it in 1829–33 under Tirot Sing.
It occurred in 1817 as a militia revolt in Khurda.
It was led by Purandar Singh against the Santhal settlement policy.
219.x: The standard chronology places the Khasi rising in 1829–33 under Tirot Sing. The other options confuse it with the Munda, Ahom and Paika movements.
219.tq: Resolve the chronology discrepancy by using the standard date and leader together.
219.sec: Revolt → year matching and chronology  [other exams]

219.s: Cleveland, the Collector of Bhagalpur in the 1780s, adopted a conciliatory plan for the Paharias by working through:
219.x: Cleveland’s conciliatory plan for the Paharias in the 1780s used hill chiefs. The Munda-Manki arrangement belonged to Wilkinson’s Rule in Kolhan.
219.tq: Ask who would perform the administrative role and distinguish the two colonial arrangements.

219.s: Wilkinson’s Rule of 1837 is associated with the administration of Kolhan through:
219.x: Under Wilkinson’s Rule, introduced in 1837, Kolhan was governed through Munda-Manki chiefs after the Kol rising.
219.tq: Use the administrative authority–local institution pairing to avoid confusing Wilkinson’s Rule with Cleveland’s plan.

219.s:
Which of the following constituted common causes of tribal revolts in colonial India?
1. Forest laws that made forests state property
2. Restrictions on podu or shifting cultivation
3. New land revenue demands
4. Land alienation caused by dikus
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
219.x: Forest laws, restrictions on podu cultivation, new revenue demands and land alienation caused by moneylenders, zamindars and traders were all important causes of tribal revolts.
219.tq: Treat the broad causal list as cumulative and check each economic and forest-related factor.

219.s: The Indian Forest Act of 1878 contributed to tribal discontent by treating forests as:
o: property of the Santhal Parganas district council
219.x: The Indian Forest Act of 1878 strengthened state control by making forests state property, adversely affecting tribal customary rights.
219.tq: Test the legal change in ownership rather than a general statement about forest administration.

219.s: In the context of tribal revolts, the term ‘dikus’ referred principally to:
219.x: Dikus were outsiders such as moneylenders, zamindars and traders whose activities contributed to tribal land alienation.
219.tq: Discriminate between a colonial social category and indigenous administrative institutions.

219.s: The common factor behind many tribal revolts, as identified in the broader interpretation of their causes, was the:
o: transfer of Upper Assam to Purandar Singh
complete disruption of the old agrarian order
219.x: A common underlying factor was the complete disruption of the old agrarian order through colonial revenue, forest and land policies.
219.tq: Move from individual causes to the wider structural explanation.

219.s: Govind Giri, also known as Guru, led the Bhils primarily against:
219.x: Govind Giri led the Bhils against bonded labour. His movement was associated with Rajasthan and Gujarat.
219.tq: Match the reform leader with the specific social grievance of the Bhils.
219.sec: Bhil reform movements in Rajasthan and Gujarat  [other exams]

219.s: The Mangarh massacre of 1913 is popularly known as the:
219.x: The Mangarh massacre of 1913 is called the “Adivasi Jallianwala.” Mangarh Dham was later recognised as a National Monument.
219.tq: Use the popular epithet to identify the correct tribal event.
219.sec: Bhil reform movements in Rajasthan and Gujarat  [other exams]

219.s: Mangarh Dham was declared a National Monument in:
219.x: Mangarh Dham, associated with the 1913 massacre, became a National Monument in 2022.
219.tq: Separate the date of the massacre from the much later date of official recognition.
219.sec: Bhil reform movements in Rajasthan and Gujarat  [other exams]

219.s: The Eki movement of 1921–22 in Mewar was led by:
219.x: Motilal Tejawat led the Eki movement in Mewar during 1921–22. Govind Giri was associated with the Bhil movement against bonded labour.
219.tq: Distinguish the two Bhil leaders by movement, region and period.
219.sec: Bhil reform movements in Rajasthan and Gujarat  [other exams]

219.s: The Rampa rebellion of 1879 took place in which of the following regions?
219.x: The Rampa rebellion of 1879 occurred in the Godavari Agency.
219.tq: Use the location-based direct-recall approach.

219.s: The Rampa rebellion of 1879 was primarily directed against which of the following?
o: The abolition of tribal customary laws by the Santhal Parganas administration
The zamindari system introduced by Cornwallis
The indigo cultivation system imposed by European planters
The exploitative mansabdar Madhava Bhupati, new taxes and forest restrictions
219.x: The rebellion opposed the exploitative mansabdar Madhava Bhupati, new taxes and restrictions on forests and podu cultivation.
219.tq: Test the cause by distinguishing the correct official and policy from nearby tribal movements.

219.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the causes of the Rampa rebellion of 1879:
1. New taxes were imposed on the tribal population.
2. Restrictions were placed on forest and podu cultivation.
3. The restrictions were associated with the Madras Forest Act.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
219.x: All three statements are correct. The rebellion was connected with new taxes and forest and podu restrictions under the Madras Forest Act.
219.tq: Combine related causes and identify the option containing all the correct statements.

219.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Leader)
A. Pulikantha Sambaiah
B. Darabandala Chandrayya
C. Karu Tammanna Dora
D. Ambul Reddy

List-II (Association with the Rampa rebellion)
1. Leader associated with the 1879 rising
2. Burnt the Addatheegala police station
3. Leader associated with the 1879 rising
4. Leader associated with the Rekapalle episode

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
219.x: Pulikantha Sambaiah and Karu Tammanna Dora were leaders of the 1879 Rampa rising; Darabandala Chandrayya burnt the Addatheegala police station; Ambul Reddy was associated with Rekapalle.
219.tq: Start from the sure pair linking Chandrayya with the Addatheegala police station.

219.s: Who among the following led the Koya rising of 1879–80, according to the cited account?
o: Tomas, also known as Tomma Dora
219.x: Tomas, also called Tomma Dora, led the Koya rising of 1879–80.
219.tq: Discriminate between leaders, officials and persons associated with different tribal movements.

219.s: Which one of the following statements about the administrative response to the Rampa rebellion is correct?
o: The British abolished the Madras Revenue Board after the rebellion.
Sullivan of the Madras Revenue Board removed the mansabdar Madhava Bhupati.
Madhava Bhupati of the Madras Revenue Board removed Sullivan.
Alluri Sitarama Raju removed the mansabdar in 1879.
219.x: Sullivan, associated with the Madras Revenue Board, removed the mansabdar Madhava Bhupati.
219.tq: Apply the ‘who did what’ trap to distinguish the official from the person against whom the revolt was directed.

219.s: In the Rampa rebellion of 1879, approximately how many rebels had been arrested by August 1879?
219.x: About 70 rebels had been arrested by August 1879.
219.tq: Use the numerical-value distinction among closely spaced figures.

219.s: The Rampa rebellion of 1879 was crushed by which of the following times?
219.x: The rebellion was crushed by November 1880.
219.tq: Separate the date of arrests from the later date of suppression.

219.s: Rekapalle, associated with the tribal rising of 1879, was located in which of the following?
219.x: Rekapalle was situated in Bhadrachalam taluk.
219.tq: Test the precise geographical location rather than the broader regional association.

219.s: During the Rekapalle episode of 1879, the podu tax per axe was raised from 4 annas to which of the following range during a famine?
219.x: During the famine, the podu tax was increased from 4 annas per axe to 4–12 annas.
219.tq: Compare the initial figure and the revised range precisely.

219.s: On which date did Ambul Reddy attack the Vaddagudem police station?
219.x: Ambul Reddy attacked the Vaddagudem police station on 10 July 1879.
219.tq: Distinguish the exact day, month and year in a date-based question.

219.s: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Rampa rebellion of 1879 from the later Rampa rebellion?
o: The 1879 rising occurred in the Godavari Agency, whereas the 1922–24 rising was led by Alluri Sitarama Raju.
The 1879 rising was led by Alluri Sitarama Raju, whereas the 1922–24 rising was led by Ambul Reddy.
The 1879 rising was a Munda movement, whereas the 1922–24 rising was a Santhal movement.
Both risings were led by Alluri Sitarama Raju and occurred during the same period.
219.x: The 1879 rising was a separate Godavari Agency rebellion, while the later Rampa rebellion of 1922–24 was led by Alluri Sitarama Raju.
219.tq: Discriminate between two similarly named but separate rebellions by their dates and leader.

219.s: The 1922–24 Rampa Rebellion was associated mainly with which communities?
219.x: The 1922–24 Rampa Rebellion led by Alluri Sitarama Raju involved the Koyas and Konda Doras.
219.tq: Use community-based discrimination among tribal movements.

219.s: Hul Divas is observed on which date?
219.x: Hul Divas is observed on 30 June.
219.tq: Test the exact date of an observance through direct recall.

219.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Debates on the Birsait faith have been linked with the question of Adivasi religious identity.
2. The Tana Bhagats have figured in recent discussions on tribal religious identity.
3. A Jharkhand project was challenged on the ground that it violated the CNT Act, 1908, and PESA.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
219.x: All three statements are correct. The discussions covered Birsait faith, Adivasi religious identity and the Tana Bhagats, while a Jharkhand project faced a challenge under the CNT Act, 1908, and PESA.
219.tq: Identify the option containing all the correctly connected contemporary tribal issues.

219.s: The Bhagwan Birsa Munda Memorial Udyan cum Freedom Fighters Museum was opened at which place in 2021?
219.x: The Bhagwan Birsa Munda Memorial Udyan cum Freedom Fighters Museum was opened in Ranchi in 2021.
219.tq: Pair the memorial with its correct location and year.

219.s: Tribal Freedom Fighter Museums are planned in how many States?
219.x: Tribal Freedom Fighter Museums are planned in 10 States.
219.tq: Use the exact count rather than a nearby rounded figure.

219.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

It neither accepted nor rejected the Award.

223.x: The Congress neither accepted nor rejected the Communal Award as a whole.
223.tq: Watch for the middle position between complete acceptance and rejection.
223.sec: Communal Award - British PM, provisions, Gandhi's fast  [APPSC]

223.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Gandhi — Harijan
2. Ambedkar — Dalit/Scheduled Castes
3. Gandhi — Legal and constitutional rights as the principal method
4. Ambedkar — Separate electorates
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
223.x: Gandhi used the term Harijan and emphasised moral persuasion, temple entry and constructive work. Ambedkar used Dalit/Scheduled Castes and advocated legal, constitutional and political rights including separate electorates; pair 3 is therefore false.
223.tq: Match each leader with his terminology and method, not merely his objective.
223.sec: Ambedkar vs Gandhi on separate electorates  [APPSC]

223.s: Which of the following best represents Ambedkar's position regarding political power for the Depressed Classes?
o: Political power was necessary to protect their interests.
Political power could be secured only through religious conversion.
Political power should remain exclusively with caste Hindus.
Political power was irrelevant because social reform alone was sufficient.
223.x: Ambedkar held that political power was necessary for the Depressed Classes to protect themselves and secure their rights.
223.tq: Test the central argument associated with a political thinker.
223.sec: Ambedkar vs Gandhi on separate electorates  [APPSC]

223.s: Which one of the following statements correctly describes Ambedkar's later assessment of the Poona Pact?
o: It replaced joint electorates with separate electorates.
It made Dalits dependent on caste Hindus.
It abolished all reserved representation for Dalits.
It made Dalits independent of caste Hindus in political matters.
223.x: Ambedkar later felt that the Pact made Dalits dependent on caste Hindus, although he had accepted joint electorates during the negotiations.
223.tq: Distinguish the immediate acceptance of an arrangement from its later evaluation.
223.sec: Ambedkar vs Gandhi on separate electorates  [APPSC]

223.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the electorates under the Communal Award and the Poona Pact?
o: The Award provided separate electorates with a general vote, while the Pact provided joint electorates with reserved seats.
The Award provided joint electorates, while the Pact provided separate electorates.
Both provided separate electorates with no reserved seats.
Neither made any provision for representation of the Depressed Classes.
223.x: The Communal Award provided a separate electorate along with a general vote, whereas the Poona Pact replaced this with joint electorates and reserved seats.
223.tq: Compare the operative electoral mechanism rather than the political controversy.
223.sec: Poona Pact - signatories, seats, electorate  [APPSC]

223.s: In addition to reserved representation, the Poona Pact promised:
o: Separate electorates for all occupational groups
Fair representation in civil services and a share of educational grants
Complete transfer of education to local bodies
223.x: The Pact promised fair representation for the Depressed Classes in civil services and a share of education grants.
223.tq: Test the less frequently recalled accompanying provisions of an agreement.
223.sec: Poona Pact - signatories, seats, electorate  [APPSC]

223.s: The Poona Pact was signed at Yerwada, Poona, in September 1932. Which date is associated with its signing in the standard account?
223.x: The standard account places the signing of the Poona Pact on 24 September 1932 at Yerwada, Poona.
223.tq: Separate the date of the fast from the date of the agreement that ended it.
223.sec: Poona Pact - signatories, seats, electorate  [APPSC]

223.s: Which sequence correctly represents the development of Ambedkar's major organisations and movement?
o: Scheduled Castes Federation — Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha — Independent Labour Party — Kalaram Temple Satyagraha
Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha — Kalaram Temple Satyagraha — Independent Labour Party — Scheduled Castes Federation
Kalaram Temple Satyagraha — Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha — Scheduled Castes Federation — Independent Labour Party
Independent Labour Party — Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha — Kalaram Temple Satyagraha — Scheduled Castes Federation
223.x: The sequence is Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha in 1924, Kalaram Temple Satyagraha in 1930, Independent Labour Party in 1936 and Scheduled Castes Federation in 1942.
223.tq: Use the dates to fix the first and last events before arranging the middle pair.
223.sec: Depressed classes associations → leader  [APPSC]

223.s: The Independent Labour Party, associated with B.R. Ambedkar, was established in:
223.x: Ambedkar's Independent Labour Party was established in 1936.
223.tq: Reject the nearby movement dates and identify the exact organisational year.
223.sec: Depressed classes associations → leader  [APPSC]

223.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: All India Depressed Classes Association — M.C. Rajah
223.x: M.C. Rajah was associated with the All India Depressed Classes Association. The Scheduled Castes Federation was established in 1942, the Independent Labour Party in 1936, and Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha was founded by Ambedkar.
223.tq: Use a sure leader–organisation pair to eliminate swapped dates and founders.
223.sec: Depressed classes associations → leader  [APPSC]

223.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. V.R. Shinde — Depressed Classes Mission
2. Bhagya Reddy Varma — Jagan Mitra Mandali
3. B.R. Ambedkar — Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha
4. Jyotiba Phule — Harijan Sevak Sangh
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
223.x: V.R. Shinde founded the Depressed Classes Mission, Bhagya Reddy Varma founded Jagan Mitra Mandali, and Ambedkar founded Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha. Harijan Sevak Sangh was the renamed form of the All India Anti-Untouchability League, not an organisation founded by Phule.
223.tq: Detect the founder substituted with a prominent but unrelated reformer.
223.sec: Anti-untouchability organisations - founder and first president  [APPSC]

223.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with the year of establishment?
223.x: Jagan Mitra Mandali was established by Bhagya Reddy Varma in 1906. Satyashodhak Samaj dates to 1873, the Depressed Classes Mission to 1906, and Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha to 1924.
223.tq: Match the organisation with its exact year while screening nearby dates.
223.sec: Anti-untouchability organisations - founder and first president  [APPSC]

223.s: The Mahad Satyagraha of 20 March 1927 was organised at which place?
223.x: The Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha organised the Mahad Satyagraha at the Chawdar Tank on 20 March 1927.
223.tq: Match a movement with its specific site rather than its leader alone.
223.sec: Anti-untouchability organisations - founder and first president  [APPSC]

223.s: Which one of the following statements correctly describes Gandhi's Andhra tour of 1932–33?
o: It collected Harijana Bhiksha and included a temple-entry initiative at Siddhantam.
It organised the Coolie Sangham exclusively for industrialists.
It established the Scheduled Castes Federation at Siddhantam.
It launched the Civil Disobedience Movement at Vizianagaram.
223.x: During his 1932–33 Andhra tour, Gandhi collected Harijana Bhiksha and launched temple entry at Siddhantam in Krishna district on 17 December 1933.
223.tq: Combine the purpose, local campaign and place of a regional tour.
223.sec: Depressed classes in Andhra - Adi-Andhra leaders

223.s: The Coolie Sangham for Dalit labour was organised by:
223.x: The communists organised the Coolie Sangham for Dalit labour.
223.tq: Identify the organisation by the political group associated with its formation.
223.sec: Depressed classes in Andhra - Adi-Andhra leaders

223.s:
Consider the following statements about journals associated with the Depressed Classes movement:
1. Mooknayak was associated with Ambedkar.
2. Bahishkrit Bharat was associated with Ambedkar.
3. Harijan was a weekly journal associated with Gandhi.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
223.x: All three statements are correct. Mooknayak was published in 1920, Bahishkrit Bharat in 1927, and Harijan was Gandhi's weekly journal from 1933.
223.tq: Confirm a complete set of leader–journal associations before selecting the inclusive code.
223.sec: Journals → leader  [APPSC]

223.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the constitutional history of the term 'Scheduled Castes' is correct?
o: It was first used by the Simon Commission, fixed by the Government of India Act, 1935, and the first list came in 1936.
It was first used in the Communal Award and abolished by the Government of India Act, 1935.
It was first used by Gandhi in 1932 and legally defined in 1942.
It was first used in the Poona Pact and listed in 1950.
223.x: The term was first used by the Simon Commission, fixed by the Government of India Act, 1935, and the first list was issued in 1936.
223.tq: Arrange the institutional stages of a constitutional term in sequence.
223.sec: Universal angles

223.s: Article 17 of the Constitution is significant in the context of the Depressed Classes movement because it:
o: Provided separate electorates for Scheduled Castes
223.x: Article 17 abolished untouchability and prohibited its practice in any form.
223.tq: Match a constitutional Article with its precise subject.
223.sec: Universal angles

223.s: The reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes under the constitutional system is conceptually linked to which feature of the Poona Pact?
o: Nomination by the British Prime Minister
223.x: The Poona Pact's model of joint electorates with reserved seats became the basis for the constitutional approach to SC political reservation.
223.tq: Identify the institutional feature that carried forward into the Constitution.
223.sec: Universal angles

224.s: Who chaired the committee that prepared the Nehru Report in 1928?
224.x: Motilal Nehru chaired the nine-member committee that drafted the Nehru Report in 1928.
224.tq: Use the person-to-role association and distinguish chairman from secretary.
224.sec: Nehru Report and Jinnah's Fourteen Points

224.s: The Nehru Report was primarily prepared in response to which of the following?
o: Lord Birkenhead's challenge to Indians to frame a constitution
The demand for a separate Muslim homeland
The failure of the Cripps Mission
224.x: The Nehru Report was prepared in reply to Secretary of State Lord Birkenhead's challenge to Indians to frame their own constitution.
224.tq: Identify the immediate cause behind a constitutional document.
224.sec: Nehru Report and Jinnah's Fourteen Points

224.s: Which one of the following was NOT a proposal of the Nehru Report?
224.x: The Nehru Report proposed joint electorates with reserved seats for minorities, not separate electorates.
224.tq: Find the reversed feature in a closely related constitutional programme.
224.sec: Nehru Report and Jinnah's Fourteen Points

224.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Nehru Report:
1. Jawaharlal Nehru served as its secretary.
2. It recommended a Supreme Court.
3. It proposed the continuation of dyarchy in the provinces.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
224.x: Jawaharlal Nehru was the secretary and the report recommended a Supreme Court. It proposed ending dyarchy, so statement 3 is false.
224.tq: Locate the one reversed constitutional recommendation.
224.sec: Nehru Report and Jinnah's Fourteen Points

224.s: At which session and in which month was the Nehru Report discussed, with a one-year ultimatum to the British?
224.x: The Nehru Report was discussed at the Calcutta session in December 1928, where a one-year ultimatum was given to the British.
224.tq: Combine the event, venue and date rather than recalling the year alone.
224.sec: Nehru Report and Jinnah's Fourteen Points

224.s: Jinnah's Fourteen Points of 1929 were formulated as the Muslim League's response to which document?
224.x: Jinnah's Fourteen Points were the Muslim League's answer to the Nehru Report.
224.tq: Discriminate between closely connected constitutional documents.
224.sec: Nehru Report and Jinnah's Fourteen Points

224.s: Which one of the following combinations correctly represents important features of Jinnah's Fourteen Points?
o: Unitary constitution, joint electorates and abolition of provincial autonomy
Federal constitution, residuary powers to provinces and separate electorates
Dominion status, nominated legislatures and universal adult franchise
Presidential government, one-third provincial seats and communal veto at all levels
224.x: Jinnah's Fourteen Points demanded a federal constitution with residuary powers to the provinces and separate electorates.
224.tq: Split the options by testing the distinctive features of a constitutional demand.
224.sec: Nehru Report and Jinnah's Fourteen Points

224.s: Under the Government of India Act, 1935, the proposed All-India Federation was to consist of
o: British provinces and directly administered tribal areas only
224.x: The proposed federation was to include both British provinces and princely states.
224.tq: Test the composition of the proposed federal scheme.
224.sec: Government of India Act 1935 - federation, autonomy, Federal Court, RBI, elections, ministries

224.s:
With reference to the federation proposed under the Government of India Act, 1935, consider the following statements:
1. Accession of princely states was optional.
2. The federation actually came into operation.
3. Dyarchy was provided at the Centre.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
224.x: Accession of princely states was optional and dyarchy was provided at the Centre. The federation never came into being, making statement 2 false.
224.tq: Separate a proposed provision from one that was actually implemented.
224.sec: Government of India Act 1935 - federation, autonomy, Federal Court, RBI, elections, ministries

224.s: The Government of India Act, 1935 is notable for being the longest British constitutional Act relating to India, containing
224.x: The Act contained 321 sections and 10 schedules; it is also described in some references as having 14 parts and 321 articles.
224.tq: Use the numerical pair rather than relying on the size description alone.
224.sec: Government of India Act 1935 - federation, autonomy, Federal Court, RBI, elections, ministries

224.s: Which one of the following was a direct consequence of provincial autonomy under the Government of India Act, 1935?
o: Introduction of dyarchy in every province
Transfer of provincial subjects to the Governor-General
224.x: Provincial autonomy abolished dyarchy in the provinces.
224.tq: Match the constitutional reform with its immediate institutional effect.
224.sec: Government of India Act 1935 - federation, autonomy, Federal Court, RBI, elections, ministries

224.s: Provincial autonomy under the Government of India Act, 1935 began in
224.x: Provincial autonomy began in April 1937.
224.tq: Discriminate between nearby years and months associated with implementation.
224.sec: Government of India Act 1935 - federation, autonomy, Federal Court, RBI, elections, ministries

224.s: Which of the following statements regarding the Government of India Act, 1935 is correct?
o: It established bicameral legislatures in some provinces and abolished the India Council.
It abolished all provincial legislatures and retained the India Council.
It abolished bicameral legislatures in the provinces.
It introduced a single legislature for all provinces.
224.x: The Act provided bicameral legislatures in some provinces and abolished the India Council.
224.tq: Combine two institutional changes and reject their reversed versions.
224.sec: Government of India Act 1935 - federation, autonomy, Federal Court, RBI, elections, ministries

224.s: How many legislative lists were provided under the Government of India Act, 1935?
224.x: The Act provided Federal, Provincial and Concurrent Lists, making three legislative lists.
224.tq: Recall the constitutional classification by counting its categories.
224.sec: Government of India Act 1935 - federation, autonomy, Federal Court, RBI, elections, ministries

224.s: The Federal Court established under the Government of India Act, 1935 was located at
224.x: The Federal Court was established at Delhi in 1937.
224.tq: Use the institution-to-location association.
224.sec: Government of India Act 1935 - federation, autonomy, Federal Court, RBI, elections, ministries

224.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Federal Public Service Commission — 1935 Act — Calcutta, 1937
Provincial Public Service Commissions — 1909 Act — Delhi, 1910
224.x: The Federal Court was established at Delhi in 1937 under the Government of India Act, 1935. The Act also provided for a Federal PSC and Provincial PSCs.
224.tq: Start from the sure institution-location-year pair and eliminate swapped authorities.
224.sec: Government of India Act 1935 - federation, autonomy, Federal Court, RBI, elections, ministries

224.s: The Reserve Bank of India began operations on
224.x: The RBI started functioning on 1 April 1935. It was nationalised later, on 1 January 1949.
224.tq: Distinguish the commencement date from the later nationalisation date.
224.sec: Government of India Act 1935 - federation, autonomy, Federal Court, RBI, elections, ministries

224.s: The establishment of the Reserve Bank of India was preceded by the recommendations of the
224.x: The Hilton Young Commission of 1926 recommended the establishment of the Reserve Bank of India.
224.tq: Match a financial institution with the commission that recommended it.
224.sec: Government of India Act 1935 - federation, autonomy, Federal Court, RBI, elections, ministries

224.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. RBI was nationalised
B. Hilton Young Commission
C. RBI started operations
D. Provincial autonomy began
224.x: The correct sequence is Hilton Young Commission in 1926, RBI operations in 1935, provincial autonomy in April 1937, and RBI nationalisation in 1949.
224.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then arrange the middle dates.
224.sec: Government of India Act 1935 - federation, autonomy, Federal Court, RBI, elections, ministries

224.s: Who became the premier of Madras after the provincial elections of 1937 when the Congress formed the ministry there?
224.x: C. Rajagopalachari became the premier of Madras in 1937.
224.tq: Distinguish the 1937 Congress ministry from the earlier Justice Party ministry.
224.sec: Government of India Act 1935 - federation, autonomy, Federal Court, RBI, elections, ministries

224.s: The Congress ministries resigned in October-November 1939 mainly because
o: The Muslim League withdrew support from all provincial ministries.
India was involved in the Second World War without the consent of Indian leaders.
The British abolished provincial legislatures without consultation.
The Federal Court rejected provincial autonomy.
224.x: The Congress ministries resigned in protest against India being dragged into the Second World War without Indian consent.
224.tq: Identify the political cause behind a major institutional action.
224.sec: Government of India Act 1935 - federation, autonomy, Federal Court, RBI, elections, ministries

224.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the political response to the resignation of the Congress ministries in 1939?
o: The Muslim League observed the Day of Deliverance on 26 January 1940, and Rajagopalachari joined it.
The Muslim League observed the Day of Deliverance on 15 August 1939, and Jinnah resigned.
The Congress observed the Day of Deliverance on 22 December 1939, and Ambedkar opposed it.
The Muslim League observed the Day of Deliverance on 22 December 1939, and B. R. Ambedkar joined it.
224.x: The Muslim League observed the Day of Deliverance on 22 December 1939; B. R. Ambedkar also joined the observance.
224.tq: Test a date-person-event combination and reject swapped participants.
224.sec: Government of India Act 1935 - federation, autonomy, Federal Court, RBI, elections, ministries

224.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Feature of the Government of India Act, 1935)
a. Instrument of Instructions
b. Federal Court
c. Emergency powers
d. Federal scheme and Public Service Commissions

List-II (Constitutional counterpart)
i. Supreme Court
ii. Directive Principles of State Policy
iii. Emergency provisions
iv. Union-State structure and UPSC/State PSCs

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
224.x: The Instrument of Instructions corresponds to the Directive Principles, the Federal Court to the Supreme Court, emergency powers to emergency provisions, and the federal scheme and PSCs to the Union-State structure and present PSC system.
224.tq: Start from the sure pair Federal Court–Supreme Court and complete the constitutional parallels.
224.sec: Borrowed features from GoI Act 1935 - constitutional provision

224.s: The Government of India Act, 1935 is regarded as the largest single source of the
224.x: The 1935 Act is considered the largest single source of the structural provisions of the Constitution of India.
224.tq: Identify the historical document's long-term constitutional significance.
224.sec: Borrowed features from GoI Act 1935 - constitutional provision

224.s: Section 63 of the Government of India Act, 1935 dealt with the Governor's
o: Power to nationalise the Reserve Bank
Power to appoint the Federal Court judges
Power to dissolve the Constituent Assembly
224.x: Section 63 enabled the Governor to address the provincial legislature in his discretion.
224.tq: Match a specific section with its constitutional function.
224.sec: Borrowed features from GoI Act 1935 - constitutional provision

224.s: The criticism that dyarchy gave ministers transferred subjects without adequate financial control was based on the fact that
o: The Governor-General controlled all transferred subjects directly.
Ministers were denied legislative powers altogether.
Finance was abolished as a provincial subject.
224.x: Dyarchy was criticised because ministers controlled transferred subjects while finance remained among the reserved subjects.
224.tq: Apply the reserved-transferred distinction to an administrative criticism.
224.sec: Universal angles

224.s: Which one of the following best explains why dyarchy was criticised as an ineffective arrangement?
o: All provincial subjects were transferred to elected ministers with complete financial authority.
The system provided no distinction between executive and legislative functions.
Transferred subjects were placed under ministers, but essential financial control remained reserved.
The arrangement abolished the office of the Governor.
224.x: Ministers were responsible for transferred subjects but lacked control over finance, which remained reserved; this limited responsible government.
224.tq: Choose the precise cause-effect explanation rather than an extreme generalisation.
224.sec: Universal angles

224.s: The first Justice Party ministry in Madras was associated with which pair of leaders?
224.x: The first Justice Party ministry in Madras was associated with Subbarayalu Reddiar and Panagal Raja.
224.tq: Distinguish the earlier Justice Party ministry from the later Congress ministry.
224.sec: Universal angles

224.s: C. Sankaran Nair was recalled in recent public discourse on the 106th anniversary of the
224.x: The Prime Minister recalled C. Sankaran Nair on the 106th anniversary of Jallianwala Bagh.
224.tq: Link a contemporary reference to the historical event it commemorates.
224.sec: Universal angles

224.s: Which one of the following was associated with the 1928 Trade Disputes and Public Safety Bills?
o: Rajagopalachari described them as the “Day of Deliverance Bills”.
Motilal Nehru described one of them as the “Slavery of India Bill”.
Ambedkar introduced them in the Federal Court.
Jinnah called both bills the “Federal India Acts”.
224.x: In the context of the 1928 Trade Disputes and Public Safety Bills, Motilal Nehru called one the “Slavery of India Bill”.
224.tq: Use the person-quotation association and reject quotations assigned to nearby leaders.
224.sec: Universal angles

224.s:
Which of the following statements correctly reflects the relationship between the Government of India Act, 1935 and the Constitution of India?
1. The Federal Court was a precursor to the Supreme Court.
2. The Instrument of Instructions influenced the Directive Principles.
3. Emergency powers under the Act influenced the emergency provisions of the Constitution.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
224.x: All three are recognised constitutional continuities between the 1935 Act and the Constitution of India.
224.tq: Recognise a cluster of borrowed constitutional features rather than an isolated provision.
224.sec: Borrowed features from GoI Act 1935 - constitutional provision
